News.title: Michael Douglas says he asked to leave Marvel film franchise: ‘They wouldn’t let me’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Michael Douglas wanted to leave the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) series after two films and asked studio bosses to kill his character off – but they refused.

The Oscar-winning actor, 82, candidly revealed that he’d had enough after starring in Ant-Man (2015) and its sequel Ant-Man and the Wasp (2018) as physicist Hank Pym.

"I would have been killed off after the second one, but they wouldn't let me," Douglas told the Happy Sad Confused podcast in a new interview.

open image in gallery Michael Douglas has appeared in four Marvel films in total ( Marvel Studios )

The actor said he originally sought out a film like Ant-Man because he had “never done a green screen movie”, and told his agents: “I’d like to do one to see what they’re like.”

“It’s amazing,” he continued. “It's nothing, just a green screen, and they show you the pictures of what it's gonna look like when it's all finished."

But Douglas, whose credits include Wall Street, Basic Instinct and Traffic, described the experience as “hard acting, man”, stating: "It's coming at you here, this and that, you know."

While he enjoyed working with “wonderful actor” Paul Rudd and his “lovely” cast mates, including Evangeline Lilly and Michelle Pfeiffer, the actor was forced to check the “fine print” of his contract after two films, but realised “you can’t get out of it” that easily.

Douglas went on to reprise his role in Avengers: Endgame (2019) and Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania (2023), as well as the animated series What If...? in 2021 and 2022.

open image in gallery Michael Douglas won’t be in the forthcoming ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ ( Marvel Studios )

The actor said earlier this year he was unlikely to return to the MCU, telling Deadline he was planning on accepting fewer roles now he’s in his 80s. “I’m enjoying my hiatus and enjoying my life,” he said.

The actor, who also produces, said that he hasn’t completely ruled out a return to acting, but it would only be “if something good comes up that I really like”.

Douglas won’t be part of the ensemble starring in Avengers: Doomsday, which is being released in December.

The film is set to be one of Marvel’s biggest crossovers yet, bringing together heroes from across three universes to confront Doctor Doom, played by former Iron Man actor Robert Downey Jr.

It will also bring back several original X-Men stars, including Patrick Stewart as Professor X, Ian McKellen as Magneto, and James Marsden as Cyclops. Avengers: Doomsday is released on 18 December.

News.title: Sixth whale rescued from theme park dies weeks after moving to new home
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A sixth whale rescued from a Canadian theme park has died just weeks after moving to its new home.

​Cyprus, a nine-year-old male beluga whale, died at SeaWorld San Diego after being taken to the theme park on August 22 from the now-closed Marineland of Canada park in Ontario.

However, Cyprus stopped eating on Saturday, prompting the park’s veterinarian and animal care teams to examine the whale, according to a statement from the park.

open image in gallery Cyprus (pictured), a nine-year-old male beluga whale, has died at SeaWorld San Diego after being rescued from a park in Canada ( SeaWorld SanDiego )

​An ultrasound uncovered that Cyprus’s intestinal tract was not functioning normally - something that can point to a life-threatening illness. Despite the park’s teams working through the night to help the whale, he died shortly after, the spokesperson says.

​The park spokesperson added that Cyprus had seemed to be settling well into his new environment in the run-up to his death, noting that belugas can mask health problems that they are experiencing.

​“Cyprus had been doing well since his arrival,” the spokesperson wrote. “He was eating consistently, acclimating to his new environment and interacting with his trainers and animal care team, along with the two other rescued belugas.”

open image in gallery SeaWorld San Diego says that it is closely monitoring the health of the other beluga whales that have been rehomed at the park ( Google Street View )

​Cyprus is the sixth whale taken from Marineland to die after leaving the park. Four died at Chicago’s Shedd Aquarium, with a fifth dying at Oceanogràfic València in Spain.

​Marineland closed down in 2024 after becoming mired in financial difficulties. A letter previously sent to Canada’s fisheries ministry detailed the park’s concerns about the future of the whales and warned that they may be euthanized if they were not rehomed.

​“The gravity of the funding crisis at Marineland cannot be overstated; any further delay jeopardizes the welfare and security of the whales, and we fear we are running out of time to act,” the letter read. “Our only options at this point are to either relocate the whales or face the devastating decision of euthanasia.”

open image in gallery Beluga whales can live up to 80 years (file photo) ( AFP/Getty )

​The SeaWorld San Diego spokesperson says that it will closely monitor the health of the other belugas rehomed at the park. For now, they remain in stable health.

“Like our colleagues at the other AZA-accredited facilities that rescued these belugas, we understood each animal would be navigating a significant transition and that their complete health picture, including conditions that may have developed over time, could only become clearer through ongoing assessment and care,” the spokesperson said.

​Although Cyprus was only 9 years old at the time of his death, beluga whales can live up to 80 years old, the Arctic WWF says. They can grow up to 5.5 meters long and weigh up to 1500kg.​

News.title: Bridget Jones author Helen Fielding announces new writer prize in North: ‘Writing opportunities are very uneven in UK’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Bridget Jones author Helen Fielding has said that writing opportunities across the UK are “very uneven” as she launches a prize for comic writers in the north.

Yorkshire-born journalist Fielding’s ciggie-loving secret diarist first began life as a column in the pages of The Independent before it became a global publishing phenomenon and series of Hollywood films. Now, 31 years later, she has set up the Bridget Jones Prize for Northern Comedy Writing to give opportunities to undiscovered writers from the north of England.

At an exclusive Q&A for Independent members at the Institute of Contemporary Arts as part of The Independent’s 40th anniversary celebrations, Fielding discussed her motivation for setting up the prize, which she has also funded.

“It’s a bit uneven, the spread of opportunity for writing in this country. In fact, it’s very uneven,” Fielding told The Independent’s Editor-in-Chief Geordie Greig at the ICA event on Monday (19 October). “There’s much more opportunity in the South than in the North where I grew up.

open image in gallery Helen Fielding spoke about the origins of Bridget Jones with The Independent's Geordie Greig on Monday (19 October) ( Joanne Davidson )

“I got so lucky really with Bridget and I just wrote 1,000 words that happened to catch on,” she said. “The idea is it’s for the funniest 1,000, first person words that stand alone and could be put in the newspaper,” adding that she hopes it will attract entries from “someone who’s being funny, living their normal life”.

The funniest 1,000-word entry, which must be a piece of first-person stand-alone prose, will win £2,000 and writing support from both Newcastle-based charity New Writing North and literary agency Aitken Alexander Associates, which represents Fielding.

Fielding was working as a newspaper journalist when she launched the anonymous column, Bridget Jones’s Diary, in The Independent in 1995. In her first entry, Fielding’s 30-something, faux pas-prone creation was born – with Bridget agonising over why her boss/office crush Daniel hadn’t called, moaning about unbearable colleague Perpetua and vowing to give up cigarettes, junk food and men.

The cash-strapped journalist had been asked to write a column about her own life as a single woman in her 30s but turned it down at first. “I was very private so I said no, but I’ll make something up. It was really sort of spontaneous and it was done in a day,” Fielding told Greig.

She initially thought the column would last just six weeks. “I didn’t tell anyone on the political desk that I was doing it. I didn’t tell my friends,” Fielding continued. “I felt, ‘Why would anyone want to read about how it takes three hours between waking up in the morning and leaving the house, and where was my skirt? Who was I with last night? All that sort of stuff.”

open image in gallery The prize winner will receive £2,000 and writing support from New Writing North and literary agency Aitken Alexander Associates ( Joanne Davidson )

As it turned out, quite a lot of people did. It ran for three years in The Independent, and later returned in 2005 and 2006, with Bridget smoking 5,277 cigarettes, drinking 3,836 alcoholic units, losing five stone two pounds, gaining five stone three pounds and spending 74 days hungover during that time.

The column was adapted into a novel in 1996 before spawning a franchise of books that has sold over 40 million copies worldwide. Bridget eventually became a film star, with four hit film adaptations being made, starting with 2001’s Bridget Jones’s Diary. Jerry Maguire’s Renée Zellweger took on the role of Bridget, receiving both Oscar and Bafta Award nominations for her performance in the first film and reprising the role in its three follow-up movies.

Last year, Bridget was immortalised in bronze as a commemorative statue to mark 25 years since the first film in the franchise.

The Bridget Jones Prize for Northern Comedy Writing is free to enter, with the winner being announced as part of a ceremony in Newcastle in summer 2027. You can find more details about eligibility and submitting entries on the New Writing North website.

News.title: Twist in case of businessman suing for £4m after slipping on Bailey's at Heathrow Airport
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A businessman suing for £4m, claiming he was left "disabled" after slipping in a puddle of spilled Bailey's at Heathrow, is facing allegations he has been seen working and training to sail a boat on the Med.

Andreas Wuchner suffered a head injury that he says resulted in "disabling migraines" after he slipped in the liqueur while rushing with a bag and tray of coffees to board a flight to Zurich in November 2017.

The 44-year-old sued British Airways, claiming the headaches led to his business’ failure and left him unable to earn a living in the near decade since.

Although a judge has already ruled he is due some compensation, Mr Wuchner now faces claims made by a former friend that he is more capable than he says, and that he has been able to work.

A court heard the man say Mr Wuchner has "actively engaged in a wide variety of business interests" since the accident, travelled extensively in Europe, bought a boat and secured a boating licence in Croatia.

However, in a hearing at Central London County Court yesterday, his barrister Sarah Prager KC branded the new evidence "gossip" involving two men who had fallen out.

"Effectively, it's tittle tattle from a former friend, it's gossip," she told Judge David Saunders. "There's clearly been a falling out between the two gentlemen."

open image in gallery During the liability trial of Mr Wuchner's claim in 2024, the judge heard Mr Wuchner was balancing a tray of espressos and two latte macchiatos when he failed to spot a patch of spilled liqueur on the floor and fell ( Champion News )

During the liability trial of Mr Wuchner's claim in 2024, the judge heard Mr Wuchner was balancing a tray of espressos and two latte macchiatos when he failed to spot a patch of spilled liqueur on the floor and fell, striking his head and suffering lasting brain damage.

Ruling on who was to blame, the judge said he found it "unusual that no immediate steps were taken by anyone from BA to prevent an accident" after the Bailey's was spilled.

"Nothing appears to have been placed over the spillage to cover it up," he said.

"That may have been simply because nothing was available, but it is surprising that this situation could not have been dealt with, at least temporarily, until all the passengers had boarded."

But he said Mr Wuchner would only be entitled to 80 percent of his compensation when finally assessed due to his own “contributory negligence” in rushing for his flight with the four delicately balanced hot beverages.

The case was set for an assessment of Mr Wuchner's damages, but took an unexpected turn last year when his former friend put forward new evidence about the impact on him of his injuries.

In his claim, Mr Wuchner said that, since the fall, he has been dogged by “constant pain and discomfort... symptoms of dizziness, nausea, forgetfulness, difficulty concentrating, memory loss, constant exhaustion, irritability and pain to his neck and back”.

It had ruined his ability to manage his once-thriving merchandising company and he ended up being unable to work due to his “severe and constant headaches”.

But for the accident he would have carried on building up his company, but it had folded and he now cannot earn and feels “like a burden” on his partner.

In a hearing in December, BA barrister Asela Wijeyaratne said Mr Wuchner had painted a picture "of gross disability caused by debilitating headaches with associated neck and back pain, cognitive and executive dysfunction, memory loss, fatigue, personality change and secondary psychological disorders."

But he told the court that evidence from Mr Wuchner's former friend and business associate, Sebastian Steiner, "paints a radically different picture."

Mr Steiner said he had seen his former friend doing lifting and carrying tasks “requiring considerable physical effort” and that the pair had also bought a boat together.

“They went on holiday together to Ibiza in September 2018. They travelled to Croatia in May 2021 where the claimant obtained his boat licence,” said the barrister.

open image in gallery The trial of Mr Wuchner's compensation claim is not now due to go before the court until next year. ( Champion News )

While Mr Wuchner did tell his friend of suffering headaches, Mr Steiner said he was able to work on his own behalf and "did not notice him experience any difficulty in completing physical tasks, answering emails or speaking on the telephone.”

He said the new evidence suggested that Mr Wuchner had "actively engaged in a wide variety of business interests since the index accident."

“These activities appear to be physically and mentally demanding, including involving long drives across continental Europe and other foreign travel, as well as requiring initiative, skill, concentration and business nous," he said.

But in court yesterday, Mrs Prager branded the new evidence "tittle tattle" which had to be looked at in the context of two men who had fallen out with each other.

And she said that, despite having introduced the new evidence, BA had not so far applied to amend their case to directly allege dishonesty or exaggeration against Mr Wuchner.

"Whoever is in the right, it just boils down to tittle tattle," she told Judge Saunders.

"There is no allegation of fundamental dishonesty or exaggeration and the defendant has had an ample opportunity to apply to amend their pleading in that respect."

Applying for the £100,000 interim damages payout, she told the court that Mr Wuchner says he has not earned any significant income since the accident nearly a decade ago.

"He needs to eat and will not have earned for 10 years by the time of the trial," she told the judge, adding that experts agree that he suffers with a "severe and disabling migraine disorder."

Awarding him the payout, Judge Saunders said £100,000 was proportionate given that the total amount which he is claiming is £4m.

"I accept there's a dispute about the extent of his claim and his credibility, and there's an underlying suggestion that there is a potential further defence of fundamental dishonesty, but as yet that hasn't been pleaded," he said.

"The credibility of Mr Steiner's evidence will depends on cross-examination in the witness box."

The trial of Mr Wuchner's compensation claim is not now due to go before the court until next year.

News.title: Thames Water lenders to appoint Lord Hutton as independent chair in takeover bid
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Thames Water’s creditors have revealed plans to appoint former business secretary Lord John Hutton as an independent chair of the water supplier if their rescue bid is given the green light to avoid it being nationalised.

The London & Valley Water consortium, a group made of lenders to the utility giant, said Lord Hutton has been selected as its choice as independent chair designate for the firm.

It comes two months after the group said it would appoint four new directors to the Thames Water board if its move was successful.

This also included former Yorkshire Water chief executive Liz Barber, Dame Bernadette Kelly, the former permanent secretary at the Department for Transport, and Clive Selley, ex-chief executive of BT Openreach.

open image in gallery Former business secretary Lord John Hutton said he is looking forward to the role (Tim Ireland/PA) ( PA Archive )

As independent chair, Lord Hutton would take on responsibility for overseeing Thames Water’s 10-year turnaround programme.

The peer served as MP for Barrow and Furness from 1992 to 2010, holding a number of cabinet roles including work and pensions secretary, business secretary and defence secretary.

The consortium – including UK and US investment companies such as Elliott Management, Aberdeen Investments and American private capital firm Apollo Global Management – previously said it was looking at offering a “golden share” to the Government as part of a revised rescue deal.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has signalled he wants to bring in a 10-year plan to renationalise the water industry, saying reform is needed to put the public interest first.

But the Government has said in the past it would prefer a “market solution” for Thames Water, which has around 16 million customers across London and the South East.

However, the influential Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee of MPs said last month it believes the potential takeover by lenders should be rejected.

Lord Hutton said: “I am looking forward to being part of the new leadership at Thames Water and helping get this hugely important business into a better place.

“People living in London and the Thames Valley have the right to expect the highest possible standards of customer service and proper environmental stewardship from their water company, and that will be our focus as we look to the future.”

Mike McTighe, vice-chair designate, said: “I am delighted that John has agreed to join this team of committed individuals who are ready and willing to apply full dedication to transforming Thames Water’s infrastructure and building a culture in which the customers and local communities come first.

“Thames Water provides the most essential public service, and it is critical that we create a strong public-private partnership to rebuild trust with the customers and public.”

News.title: French bond sell-off spreads across Europe
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. The cost of French government borrowing has risen at the fastest pace among G7 nations after a second night of riots.

The yield on 10-year French bonds, known as OATs, climbed from 4.80pc to 4.85pc on Monday, the steepest increase among major world economies.

Bond yields are effectively the interest rate paid by governments when they borrow money by issuing bonds to financial markets.

Emmanuel Macron is facing a crisis after shops were looted and vandalised across the country.

More than 2,300 people were arrested on Saturday after protests against the cost of living and poor school conditions.

Jim Reid, an analyst at Deutsche Bank, said: “This won’t make it easy for the international community to be totally comfortable buying OATs, so the modest recovery in French spreads over the last week or so will be tested today.

“With France already facing a difficult fiscal backdrop and the 2027 election approaching, the weekend adds another layer of political risk for markets.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Burnham seeks EU embrace over AI | UK presses for access to a scheme that will prioritise investment in sovereign technology

2) Larry Ellison’s TikTok bans ad account for Musk documentary | Social media company blocks promotion for the film because of its political content

3) Profit warnings rise ahead of Budget | Most companies blame government policy and geopolitical uncertainty for worsening outlook

4) Istanbul airport stockpiles jet fuel over shortage fears | Turkish hub can sustain flights for three weeks without topping up tanks

5) GB News to launch ‘all-British’ radio station | New broadcast venture will attempt to win market share from BBC

What happened overnight

Oil prices fell more than 1pc after Donald Trump’s decision to waive sweeping sanctions on Russia.

On Friday, the President signed an executive order that delayed a wave of fresh sanctions and tariffs as they were set to take effect.

Brent crude edged down by nearly 1pc to just under $109 a barrel, with West Texas Intermediate hovered at around $101 a barrel.

Asian shares were mixed as volatility in technology stocks persisted.

South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index was up 1.1pc to 5,729.58 on Monday, after falling sharply last week. The Kospi is down more than 18pc over the past month, and still well below the 9,000 mark it crossed in June at its peak on the global AI frenzy.

Japan’s Nikkei 225 lost 0.8pc to 64,799.03. Japanese chip equipment maker Tokyo Electron lost 2.1pc, and OpenAI investor SoftBank Group dropped 3.6pc.

Hong Kong’s stock market was closed because of a holiday. The Shanghai Composite index edged 0.2pc higher to 3,722.20, after China reported better-than-expected growth of 4.5pc for its economy in the third quarter.

CXMT, China’s leading memory chipmaker, fell more than 7pc despite the company forecasting a strong profit for the first nine months.

China’s official growth data is set to be issued on Monday, giving the markets a glimpse into how the world’s second-biggest economy is faring.

The data is expected to show that China’s economy expanded by 4.4pc in the third quarter, improving on a multi-year low in Q2 but still falling just short of its annual target.

Beijing is aiming for growth of around 4.5pc to 5pc this year, which is its lowest goal in decades.

However, experts think China is on course to miss its annual economic target, weighed down by the Iran war energy shock.

China’s economy has been under pressure from mounting energy costs and faltering domestic demand. Researchers polled by AFP suggested exports were its sole outperformer.

Taiwan’s Taiex fell 1pc. Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., or TSMC, the world’s biggest contract chipmaker, were down 0.6pc. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 was 0.3pc higher at 8,832.20. India’s Sensex edged down 0.1pc.

Indonesia’s benchmark stock index fell another 5pc to its lowest level since 2020, after it plunged over 11pc on Friday following a warning from index provider MSCI that it would downgrade the country from its “emerging market” status.

News.title: Europe records highest ever number of West Nile Virus cases
News.content:
Mainland Europe has seen the largest number of cases of a debilitating mosquito-borne illness, with Italy hardest hit by the disease.

According to the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control there have been 1,715 locally acquired cases of West Nile Virus so far this year, compared to 989 cases at the same point last year. Italy has been hardest hit, with 748 cases, followed by Greece with 445 cases, France with 144 and Spain with 139.

There have been 130 deaths, with the greatest number occurring in Italy, which saw 56 deaths.

The number of cases is likely to tail off over the next few weeks as the weather across Europe becomes cooler and less favourable for the Culex mosquito which spreads the disease.

West Nile Virus is in the same family of viruses as dengue, yellow fever and Japanese encephalitis. It causes flu-like symptoms and sometimes vomiting and diarrhoea but in around one in 150 cases it can develop into a disease that affects the brain and nervous system and can be fatal. There is no vaccine or treatment.

The disease is widespread in birds, but humans can only acquire it if they are bitten by an infected mosquito. The disease does not spread from human to human. Most cases of severe disease occur in older people and those with weakened immune systems.

News.title: Arsenal late show keeps heat on Man City
News.content:
In the ordinary course of a Premier League season, you would say Manchester City have applied pressure on Arsenal by opening up a six-point lead before the champions play at Nottingham Forest this afternoon.

This is not a normal Premier League season though, and we await to discover if the top of the league table is simply a mirage.

Regardless, Mikel Arteta and his Arsenal players have their own motivations to accumulate as many points as possible before January as they seek to retain the title for the first time since the 1930s.

Arsenal have struggled at the City Ground, drawing 0-0 on their last two Premier League visits. They also lost at Forest in May 2023, a result which confirmed Manchester City as champions at Arsenal’s expense, and were knocked out of the FA Cup by Forest in January 2022.

Forest are yet to score a home league goal under Oliver Glasner, another data point suggesting this will be a low-scoring game.

That might not be the full story though, with Forest creating a hatful of chances in their defeat at Crystal Palace last week and Arsenal also playing a more inventive, technical game with the ball so far this season.

Arsenal have yet to score from a non-penalty set-piece, and their percentage of goals from open play is now the highest in the Premier League.

Morgan Gibbs-White is a doubt after sustaining what Glasner described as a “minor muscle injury” at Palace and his involvement in the game will be a last-minute call. With the exception of Christos Tzolis, Piero Hincapie and long-term absentee William Saliba, Arsenal’s squad is in pretty good health. Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard, Kai Havertz, Riccardo Calafiori and Ben White could be recalled to Arteta’s starting XI after starting the Champions League win over Lille on the bench.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Slow and dull Man Utd are just not good enough
News.content:
Manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet. You fix one problem – being far too vulnerable to conceding goals – only to create another – lacking the threat to score. It is all very Meh United not Man United. The indisputable fact is they are just not very entertaining to watch. They are slow and dull.

In the end it also points to another thing. The thing highlighted in midweek by Lisandro Martínez after the Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid: they do not have the strength in depth to compete.

What they do have appears to not be fit for purpose. Certainly Michael Carrick, the under-pressure manager, is struggling to get the best out of the resources he has.

“It’s like a duvet,” Toshack, the former Real Madrid and Wales manager, famously said of football. “If you pull it up, your feet get cold. If you pull it down, your shoulders get cold.”

There will have been times in the last few days, with the intense criticism and scrutiny over his future, when Carrick will have simply felt like dragging that duvet up over his head and keeping it there.

Defeat by Leeds United would have been unthinkable. It would have put Carrick under potentially intolerable pressure in what appears to be a pivotal week, with Como away in the Champions League and a home Premier League fixture against Bournemouth in the coming days.

Was this a lifeline or the tightening of the noose for Carrick? Time will soon tell. The relief of avoiding defeat was tempered by the reality of it now being just one win in their opening seven league games – at home to newly promoted Ipswich Town – and they are down in 13th place. It is six games without a win in all competitions.

News.title: Pierre Sage fears for his Crystal Palace future after Brighton humiliation
News.content:
Pierre Sage has admitted that he fears for his future at Crystal Palace, adding that he felt “shame” after his side slumped to their joint-heaviest defeat by rivals Brighton and Hove Albion.

Sage replaced Oliver Glasner as manager in June but since then Palace have won just two league matches with him in at the helm. The south London club have taken seven points from seven Premier League games and have already conceded 17 goals, the most of any team in the league.

“I don’t know,” Sage said when asked if he will get enough time to rectify Palace’s slump. He admitted that his shame was about how Palace were overwhelmed, leaking three goals within the first nine minutes of the game before eventually losing 5-0.

“We are not at the level we expected, and I’m really sorry for that,” the 47-year-old said. “I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face.”

The Frenchman said that he took full responsibility for the 5-0 defeat, and understood why hundreds of Palace fans left well before the final whistle.

News.title: Ruthless Daniel Dubois dispatches Fabio Wardley in just two rounds
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley.

When Wardley dragged himself out of the ring at Manchester’s Co-Op LIVE Arena, the physical damage was obvious, but the psychological sting was far deeper. Wardley had Dubois severely hurt early on, flooring the Londoner twice and teetering on the verge of a career-defining stoppage. Instead, he let the knockout slip away, allowed Dubois to find his rhythm, and was ultimately broken down and halted in the 11th round - surrendering his WBO heavyweight belt in a dramatic comeback victory.

Now, just five months after that gruelling night, the two heavyweights meet again at London’s O2 Arena in an immediate rematch that carries potentially massive implications for the entire division.

For Wardley (20-1-1, 19 KOs), the decision to trigger his rematch clause was instant. Dismissing concerns over the severe punishment he absorbed down the stretch, the Ipswich man is motivated entirely by redemption and the belief that his early success proved Dubois is beatable.

Dubois (23-3, 22 KOs), however, views things very differently. Entering as The Ring’s No. 1 heavyweight contender and a proven two-time world champion, Dubois has brushed off Wardley’s power, claiming his rival “punches like a baby” and insists Wardley threw away his one and only chance at glory in Manchester.

With Oleksandr Usyk approaching the final chapter of his career and the Anthony Joshua vs. Tyson Fury blockbuster looming just eight weeks away, this London clash is far more than a personal grudge match. The winner won’t just walk away with the WBO strap; they will stake an undeniable claim as the torch-bearer for the heavyweight division’s next era if they can land another title fight in short order.

News.title: Newcastle jeers tell Matthias Jaissle his ‘vertical’ football is not working
News.content:
Newcastle United look like a poor team playing badly. The evidence is increasingly damning after Matthias Jaissle’s side were loudly booed off at the end of this limp defeat.

This has all the makings of a long, hard season. Anger is already rising to the surface, even though Jaissle claimed Newcastle deserved more from a game they “controlled” in the first half and “dominated” in the second. Those comments jarred with what we had just seen.

After four years of enjoying an upward trajectory under Eddie Howe, the team faded last season, sold their best players in the summer, lost the manager and there is no evidence yet they have replaced anything with better.

This was supposed to be a reaction to the embarrassing 4-1 thrashing at Coventry City, but it led to another loss and, in the first half at least, another abject display. Aston Villa were always the more fluent and more threatening. They should have won by more than just Johan Manzambi’s first-half header.

News.title: Liverpool’s £400m front line clicks but win at Brentford turns on red card
News.content:
Only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

Admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

But as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

Sports.title: Voice of EA FC Derek Rae explains his commentary sheet after pic of his crammed notes went viral

THE VOICE of EA FC Derek Rae’s commentary sheet went viral as his notes were so crammed it made it look impossible to read.

Rae, 59, works for a number of broadcasters, such as ESPN and ABC in the United States as well as Amazon Prime Video in the UK, while lending his voice for the famous video game’s English version.



And the Scottish commentator’s notes leaked on social media ahead of Sunday’s crunch LaLiga clash between Real Madrid and Sevilla at Santiago Bernabeu.

The broadcaster took to Twitter and explained he adopted that method of cramming all his notes in one page because he often works in confined spaces.



Rae tweeted: “Noticed my commentary sheet getting more attention than usual on here.

“Keep in mind: – It’s purely for my own use as part of my prep. No one else‘s.

“Copying & pasting is not learning – My eyes are on the pitch but if I need to glance at it, I know where the info is.

“Every commentator does it differently. Why? Because we all digest information & learn in different ways.

“There’s no correct way for us all. Only what fits the individual. This has been my way for 40+ years.

“And why just 1 page? Because we often work in cramped spaces.”

Sports.content:

COMEDIAN Lloyd Griffith left fans in stitches after heading a ball while watching Liverpool’s win over Brentford.

The BBC star, 43, was in the stands as the Reds beat nine-man Brentford 2-1 on Saturday.



And he has gone viral after being filmed nodding a wayward ball back onto the pitch.

Griffith – who is a Grimsby Town fan – said the feat was a lifelong ambition of his and even thanked Liverpool star Alexis Mac Allister for the “assist”.



He was sitting with three other girls during the game and they couldn’t hold in their laughter after the hilarious moment.

Griffith posted the clip on Instagram and wrote: “Well, it finally happened.



“After going to football matches since 1990 I managed to header a ball at a game thanks to a wayward Liverpool free kick.

“Seconds before this video, I said ‘get ready to header the ball girls’, not sure why, just had a feeling.

“Sometimes you can just feel it. Glad I put my sunglasses away. Anyway, cheers to @alemacallister for the assist.”

The post has been liked nearly 150,000 times at the time of writing.



Griffith watched on as Andoni Iraola‘s Liverpool came from behind to win after Keane Lewis-Potter’s first-half opener.

Sports.title: Rise of Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler from modelling and being sacked as an art dealer to being tipped for Man Utd job
Sports.content:
Next

FABIAN HURZELER once dreamed of starring in front of the camera.

Unfortunately for the teenage wannabe model, there were not any offers of employment.



But times have changed for the 35-year-old amid continued speculation surrounding the Manchester United job.

Brighton sit third in the Prem, with Sunday’s 5-0 win over their A23 rivals Crystal Palace.



It makes it four straight league wins with a whopping scoreline of 15-0.

But long before he was tipped to become the next United boss, 16-year-old Hurzeler was posing in photoshoots.

Speaking to GQ last year, Hurzeler said: “It turns out that no company really wanted to hire me.

“I had to accept that my body and face are not perfect for being a model.”

Instead, he continued at fifth-tier Pipinsried as player-manager.

The Bayern academy product, who was raised in Munich after being born in Texas, featured in the reserves at Hoffenheim and 1860 Munich.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

And by 23, Hurzeler decided he would have to call it quits on the pitch if he was really going to make it ‘big time’.

While coaching the village club, the bills kept coming and the money rolling out.

Hurzeler found work selling paintings for an art dealer in Munich, but he struggled to put his beautiful game on the backburner.

He admitted: “The owner recognised that I’m watching more football during working time instead of really working because we didn’t sell any more paintings.”



And he was sacked.

Hurzeler, as a little boy, would hide under a table to avoid going to training before his dad forced him to go.

But it was not long before the reluctance vanished.

Family holidays turned into keep ups at the airport gate. He was determined to be the best.



At home, there was no escape from the competition with two dentists for parents and three siblings.

Even Uno at Christmas could sour the celebrations.

He said: “When I’m sitting with my family, let’s say at Christmas time, and we played games and I lost the game, the night was over for me.”

But Hurzeler was not the sort to command the room.



As an early teen, the Bayern youth captain was expected to give a speech after a tournament.

But when handed the mic, Hurzeler gave it straight back.

The awkward silence that followed and his clumsy two sentences have haunted the Brighton boss ever since.

But there has been much less hesitation on the touchline since.



Winning the second division title with St Pauli in 2024 led to the end of their 13-year absence from the Bundesliga.

And it was not long before Brighton picked up the phone.



The seaside club named him as their next manager after Roberto De Zerbi.

At 31, Hurzeler became the youngest permanent boss in Prem history.

After a move to the South Coast, he and girlfriend Anna Karolin Berger have maintained a long-distance relationship.

The Munich-based actress, 34, stars in the popular German soap Sturm der Liebe [Love Storm].

And she has appeared in a host of films and TV shows since making her screen debut in 2017.



Berger recently popped over for one of London’s NFL games amid a busy filming schedule.



In the meantime, Hurzeler has leant into ordinary pleasures of Sunday roasts, walks along the Brighton promenade, with a trip to see Coldplay at the end of 2025 – even training for a Hyrox.

But even his downtime comes with a score to settle.

The Prem boss paired up with Brighton chief executive Paul Barber to take down Bobby Zamora and Jamie Redknapp in a brutal game of padel, having recovered from 6-1 down.

Talking to club media, Hurzeler said: “I had to be on the winning side otherwise I know what people would have said afterwards, especially in the building!”

And it’s his ‘hunger to win’ attitude that has kept his career alive long enough to see the good days.



Back in February, Brighton were handed a heartbreaking 1-0 home defeat at the hands of Palace – leaving them in 14th with just one victory from 12 league games.

Stomach-churning chants fired from the Amex stands as supporters sang songs of his incoming P45.

Yet, eight months later, the Seagulls were singing songs of praise.



The home side went three up in ten minutes including Diego Gomez’s screamer from the halfway line in a five-goal thriller.

Hurzeler signed a new contract until June 2029 in May before guiding them to an eighth place finish and European football.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But the Red Devils could be plotting a hijack having seen the former art dealer’s handiwork first hand.

Last month, Brighton came from two down inside ten minutes to win 3-2 at Old Trafford – knocking Carrick’s side out of the League Cup.

Sports.title: Egypt bosses and player slapped with combined 11-MATCH ban after World Cup chaos against Argentina
Sports.content:
Next

EGYPT bosses and player Mostafa Zico have been hit with a combined 11-MATCH ban.

The punishments come after the Pharaohs’ chaotic exit from the World Cup in the summer.



Egypt were dumped out of the tournament across the Atlantic by eventual finalists Argentina.

Mohamed Salah and co were beaten in heartbreaking fashion after they threw away a two-goal lead in the round of 16 clash



After full-time, there were accusations towards referee François Letexier of bias towards the South Americans.

Hossam Hassan, 60, was sanctioned after blaming refereeing errors for his country’s exit.



Pyramids star Zico also insulted the official during a post-match interview.

Speaking after the game he said Letexier was “not good” and called the game “rigged”.

He said: “The referee wasn’t good, he was unfair. His injustice was clear. He persecuted us from the start of the match. He doesn’t want us to win.

“It was a rigged game. It wasn’t our fault. That referee… it seems like this match was rigged.



“We were winning 2-0, and he kept coming at us. Congratulations to Argentina on another World Cup, it seems.”

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The duo and team manager Hassan’s brother Ibrahim have all been banned from matches.

The two Hassans have both been banned for three games while Zico has been banned for five by Fifa.

As a result, the Hassans will miss the two games against Malawi next month in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers.

They will also be sidelined for the qualifying game with Angola in March.



Zico, 29, will miss two more games and will not feature in any of the four remaining AFCON 2027 qualifiers.

The forward had been in impressive form for his nation with five goals in nine caps.

He had a goal controversially ruled out in the game against Argentina due to a foul on Lisandro Martinez by Marwan Attia in the build-up.

The Egyptian Football Association had previously tried to defend the trio by submitting legal clarifications about their behaviour.

However, the Fifa Disciplinary Committee decided that the actions of the Hassans and Zico warranted the bans.

Sports.title: Boulter puts rain delays behind her to progress at Japan Open
Sports.content:
A day after heavy rainfall caused play to be suspended, Britain's Katie Boulter returned to clinch a 6-3 6-1 victory at the Japan Open over wildcard Himeno Sakatsume.

The world No 58 concluded a dominant victory in one hour and 32 minutes in Osaka, and she will next face Swiss player Viktorija Golubic for a place in the quarter-finals.

The victory gives Boulter a 20-20 record across her last 40 matches, and a confidence boost following a period in which she has only played three matches since September 30, owing to early exits at the China Open (second round) and Wuhan Open (first round).

On Monday, the match between Boulter and Sakatsume had barely started when the players were forced off court after torrential rain arrived in Osaka. Given the venue didn't have a roof, the court was open to all of the elements.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Boulter showed the umpire the weather app on her phone on court, ahead of play being suspended for the day shortly after.

By that point, only three games had been played in the first set, with Sakatsume leading 2-1 at the time of the suspension.

Play was resumed, but another rain delay followed with the score 6-3 3-1 (40-30) to Boulter, meaning both players had to leave court and return on Tuesday to finish the contest.

When play restarted again, 30-year-old Boulter continued to dominate, winning seven of her eight service games overall and claiming five of nine break point chances.

Swiatek withdraws from Ningbo Open with left thigh injury

Elsewhere, Iga Swiatek has withdrawn from the Ningbo Open in China because of an injured left thigh, diminishing her chances of contesting the season-ending WTA Finals at Indian Wells next month.

The six-time major winner lost to eventual champion Maja Chwalinska in the semi-finals at the Wuhan Open last week and struggled at times in that match.

"After careful consideration, I've decided to withdraw from the tournament," Swiatek said in a statement posted on social media Tuesday by the Ningbo tournament. "I've been experiencing an ongoing problem with my left thigh over the past weeks and I feel that giving myself the time to rest and recover is the right decision."

Swiatek was one of three players in contention for the last spot in the eight-player field for the WTA Finals with Karolina Muchova and Marta Kostyuk ahead of tournaments this week.

The WTA, in a preview of the Ningbo tournament, said if Swiatek didn't reach the quarter-finals and Kostyuk doesn't reach the final here, Muchova will secure the remaining spot for the season-ending tournament at Indian Wells starting November 8.

Sports.title: Are LeBron's Sixers actually good enough to win NBA title?
Sports.content:
There are 1,230 games across 169 days in the NBA regular season - but the biggest draw of them all could come on day one.

One of the greatest players in the sport's history in LeBron James will make his 76ers debut alongside a plethora of other superstars in a new-look Philadelphia side that visit the title holders - New York Knicks - at Madison Square Garden, live on Sky Sports Main Event from 11pm on Tuesday.

It doesn't get any bigger than this to begin a new season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player James got 10 points, five assists and four rebounds in the first half during his Philadelphia 76ers debut in a pre-season match against Brooklyn Nets

Much of the off-season discussion has centred around James' move to the east coast and the threat his Sixers side could pose to existing title contenders.

That is talk that a stacked Knicks team will be hoping to prove is cheap at the very first opportunity in front of what is set to be a raucous New York crowd, with the home side set to hoist the Larry O'Brien trophy in front of their fans pre-match after winning their first championship in 53 years.

So - is Philadelphia's drastic off-season rebuild actually enough to give them true title credentials? Or are the Knicks still in pole position to retain the NBA championship?

We assess the state of play in the Eastern Conference heading into the blockbuster match that opens the new NBA season...

Sixers' puzzle pieces need to fit

Image: Jaylen Brown was traded from the Celtics to the Sixers in a blockbuster trade involving wing Paul George

The optimism in Philadelphia in May was palpable after Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey led the Sixers to a famous game seven victory on the road against the second seed Boston Celtics.

They secured a remarkable 4-3 first-round win after coming from 3-1 down, their first post-season series win against their fierce rivals since 1982.

Their joy was short-lived. The eventual champion Knicks made quick work of the Sixers, winning four out of four to secure the series sweep and condemn them to yet another second-round exit - a stage of the playoffs they have not been able to progress past in seven attempts since 2001.

That record is what James' side will be hoping to change. His addition gives the Sixers a formidable starting five featuring all-star point guard Tyrese Maxey, promising second-year wing VJ Edgecombe, and another headline addition in the NBA's leading scorer Jaylen Brown, who arrives after a blockbuster summer trade that saw the Sixers give up Paul George and draft picks in return.

The frontcourt of superstars James and Joel Embiid boasts an incredible level of NBA acumen, with five NBA MVP awards between them.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Last month James spoke to the media for the first time since signing for Philadelphia 76ers

"I didn't leave my family [in Los Angeles] to lose in the second round," James said on the Sixers' pre-season media day. "I know that for sure. Work needs to be done, and I'm ready to get to work."

The key to their success will be whether head coach Nick Nurse can find a sense of balance in a starting five that features four players averaging over 20 points a night.

A 42-year-old James has already embraced the change from scorer to facilitator in his older years. After the Lakers' playoff defeat to the Thunder, he told a press conference that it was "pretty cool" to play as the third scoring option for his former team in 2025/26.

He looks set to continue that transition in a team with three of the NBA's top 10 scorers from last season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player James has stunned the basketball world once again by announcing he had signed for the Philadelphia 76ers, a franchise that hasn't won an NBA title in 43 years

The biggest challenge for Philadelphia will come on the defensive side of the ball. While Edgecombe solidified his status as a defender of significant calibre in his rookie season, each of the other four starters are more offensive-minded - meaning at least one will have to put himself forward to take on the more challenging defensive match-ups.

They will need to find that balance fast against a multi-faceted Knicks offence - otherwise, the NBA's newest 'super team' could find itself with more questions than answers at the start of a crucial campaign.

Knicks showing no signs of slowing down

Image: New York erupted after the Knicks won their first title for 53 years last season

The Knicks, in many ways, are an example of the opposite path to success than their opening-day opponents are attempting to follow.

Their championship run was the result of a roster built over multiple years, prioritising significant depth and a team-first underdog mentality epitomised by star Jalen Brunson, who himself was passed on by multiple teams in the draft - and free agency in years past - due to doubts over his physical attributes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fans of the New York Knicks gathered to celebrate their NBA Playoff Final win

The spine of their championship-winning side also boasts a level of familiarity that is the envy of much of the NBA. Three of their core players - Brunson, guard Josh Hart and forward Mikal Bridges - won a national championship together at college level with Villanova, and are entering their third season on the same NBA team.

That championship-level chemistry - that the Knicks built from the ground up - is what the Sixers will be hoping to establish with their newly acquired superstars in just a fraction of the time.

New York's off-season activity prioritised continuity, retaining three of the four team members eligible for free agency and making just one signing: that of former Sixers centre Andre Drummond on a veteran's minimum deal, replacing Mitchell Robinson after he was poached on a three-year, $47.4m (£35.6m) contract by the Celtics.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the NBA Finals Game 5 match-up between the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs

Robinson's loss is a significant one, but retaining the services of 10 of the 11 core players in a championship-winning side conveys a clear message: they believe in their championship-winning formula, and are hungry for more.

"We're all excited for the opportunity to do it again," Hart told reporters on media day. "You guys will see that with how we conduct ourselves and how we play, that we're not satisfied with one."

Recording an opening-night win and maintaining the status quo against a team who have been the off-season talk of the league would make a clear statement - one that could help determine the course of the Eastern Conference throughout the rest of the season.

Sports.title: Reese scores 30 points as Atlanta win at Golden State to level WNBA Finals
Sports.content:
Angel Reese delivered 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals after she struggled down the stretch in the series opener, as the Atlanta Dream stymied the Golden State Valkyries at both ends in the second half to win 79-65 and level the best-of-seven series at 1-1.

In front of the Valkyries' raucous home crowd, the Atlanta star had no choice but to raise her voice - and Reese knew she had to raise her game, too.

"For me, I think I let my team down last game not really contributing as much as I could in the second half," Reese said.

"Not even just about scoring, my screen quality, me hustling and running to get rebounds, just doing the things that they know me to do. So I just wanted to make sure I came out tonight and left my mark and did whatever I could to get the win, and I think I did that tonight."

Rhyne Howard set a Finals record with six steals, Allisha Gray added 18 points, and Jordin Canada contributed 13 points, 10 assists and seven rebounds as the Dream earned the franchise's first Finals victory after going winless in three previous trips - 0-10 overall.

They now head home having salvaged a split in front of the boisterous "Ballhalla" crowd at Chase Center. "It's just the next step of who Atlanta is," Reese said.

Sports.title: Eagles QB Hurts set to miss rest of NFL season due to blood clots
Sports.content:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is set to miss the remainder of the 2026 NFL season after being diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli.

The Eagles and Hurts' agent Nicole Lynn released a joint-statement on Monday saying he will be placed on blood thinners and is unable to play football until his recovery.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that Hurts is out for the rest of the year, adding that the former Super Bowl MVP was in hospital until 4am and did not sleep prior to Philadelphia's defeat to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London.

Image: Hurts is set to be out for the rest of the season

"Over the past few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition," the joint-statement read.

"Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation [ie. 'blood thinners']. During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football."

The statement adds that a "full recovery" is expected for Hurts and no long-term effects are anticipated.

Rapoport added that the initial blood clot issue was revealed on the Saturday afternoon to be several blood clots on Hurts' lungs.

'I miss him' - Sirianni on losing Hurts for the season
