Sports.title: Poll: Does F1 needs its cost cap – or is it just holding back the smaller teams? | Debates and Polls
Sports.content:
The difficulty of creating a level playing field for sporting competitions in a world where teams teams are sold for billions has been highlighted by recent developments in the English football Premier League.

Multiple champions Manchester City were found guilty of cheating the league’s Financial Fair Play rules using sham contracts to hide funding of over £830 million . The league is yet to confirm their penalty and the club intends to appeal.

F1 introduced its equivalent rules, the budget cap, five years ago. No teams has committed a breach on anything like the same scale as that seen in the Premier League. When Red Bull was found to have overspent in the first year under the budget cap, but their £1.864m overspend amounts to just 0.2% of Manchester City’s breach. What’s more, Red Bull’s error was not found to be deliberate, unlike Manchester City’s.

Other breaches have occured, including in the recently-introduced engine cost cap. But these have usually been relatively minor procedural matters, nothing on the scale of Manchester City case, which spanned nine seasons.

But while F1’s budget cap appears to have been enforced effectively, is it having a positive effect on the championship?

Some of F1’s smaller teams said they would not have been able to continue without it. However others have expressed concerns the spending limit has created a “cost cap trap”.

Williams team principal James Vowles described the problem recently. “When we did the cost cap, this is way back [during] Covid, when we had a phone call about it, there were three key tasks that we wanted out of it,” he explained.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“We wanted long-term financial sustainability, and I think in that goal, not just have we achieved it, but we’ve exceeded it. This business now has good investment that allows us to go on, and they’re businesses. They weren’t businesses before 2021 at all.

“The two others, though, that went with it were sporting equity and, effectively, compression of the field, so effectively competitiveness that compressed together. Those are the three goals of cost cap, and those two have failed.”

Vowles said the data shows the leading four teams are in a strong position under the cost cap. “If I take the last five years of the sport, the five that we’ve been in as cost cap right now, currently the top four teams score 83% of the points. Before that it was in the seventies, just to be clear about it.

“In other words, we have made the situation worse, where the top four are the top four and all the rest of us are fighting over, ballpark, 17% of the points.”

According to Vowles, the chasing teams can’t catch up because the cost cap effectively cements their disadvantage. “When you’re in a cost cap, I’m not spending money on the car. I’m spending millions, tens of millions actually, just on basic systems, so you just know where a part is in the factory. So that’s not going to the car, it’s not going to a front wing, it’s not going to an upgrade. It’s going on systems that I need to do just to do the very basics.

“So, we’re caught in a cost cap trap, because if I do anything short-term – and I always talk about investing in the future, now you understand why – if I do anything that’s about this year, I will slow myself down in the future, and I can’t do that.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“We have a two-tier championship. That’s not me telling you that. That is just what is on the table right now in terms of points score.”

FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem indicated his dissatisfaction with the cost cap last year. “I’m looking at the cost cap and it’s just giving the FIA a headache,” he said. “So what’s the point of it? I don’t see the point.”

Does F1’s cost cap still have a point? Is it protecting the smaller teams from collapse or holding them back from competing with the front runners? And could what happened with Manchester City ever happen in F1?

Sports.title: Russell and Leclerc are the joint ‘sprint race champions’ of 2026 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli can clinch the drivers’ championship at the next round – but three of his rivals out-scored him over the course of Formula 1’s six sprint races this year.

Singapore played host to F1’s sixth and final sprint race of 2026 last weekend. The sprint races were won by four different drivers: George Russell won three (Shanghai, Montreal and Zandvoort), while his team mate Andrea Kimi Antonelli triumphed at Silverstone, Lando Norris won in Miami and it was Max Verstappen’s turn in Singapore.

Russell could have beaten Verstappen last weekend, of course, having taken the lead off him at the start. But his crash at the end of lap one ended his chances of winning a fourth sprint race.

It also meant he ended the year with as many sprint race points as a driver who didn’t win any of these races. Charles Leclerc collected 34 points from sprint races, the same as Russell. This was made possible by the single-point gaps between finishing positions in sprint races, which are much closer than those used in grands prix.

After Russell’s retirement, Norris was on course to end the year as the top sprint race points-scorer. But his last-lap tangle with his team mate cost him three points and left him third.

As points are only awarded to the top eight finishers in sprint races, the drivers from the top four teams tended to monopolise them, with one exception: Isack Hadjar did not score a single point in a sprint race.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Liam Lawson scored points for both Red Bull (while substituting for Hadjar at Zandvoort) and Racing Bulls in sprint races. His regular team mate Arvid Lindblad also took sprint race points, as did Alpine’s Pierre Gasly and Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg.

But for almost half the grid, the sprint races offered nothing. The addition of four more sprint races next year could further increase the gap between the leading teams and the midfield.

Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster Claims He Can Dominate Emanuel Navarrete
Sports.content:
O’Shaquie Foster insists he has Emanuel Navarrete completely figured out ahead of their October 24 unification bout in San Antonio. Foster plans to outclass him, take his belt, and force critics to treat him like an elite name at 130 pounds.

Foster claimed he could turn this into a one-sided blowout if he simply sticks to the outside and picks Navarrete apart.

“I believe not only that I can beat Navarrete, I believe that I can do it in a dominant fashion, a super dominant fashion,” Foster said to Bradley’s channel. “I can make it an easy night and just box his head off.”

At the same time, Foster called this matchup a nine out of ten in difficulty and admitted it represents the biggest threat of his career. Navarrete throws wild, looping bombs from angles nobody learns in the gym. Foster insists none of that will rattle him. He points to past rounds with Rey Vargas, Robson Conceicao, and Jon Fernandez as proof that he knows how to handle height, awkward attacks, and long-range pressure.

Navarrete brings chaos, not textbook mechanics. Surviving separate elements from past opponents does not guarantee Foster can absorb the non-stop pressure Navarrete brings from opening bell to the final seconds. Foster cannot afford to run and let rounds slip away on activity alone.

He claims he wants to dominate, yet talking about an easy night while hunting for a highlight reel finish creates immediate risk. If Foster gets trapped between cruising on points and trying to look spectacular, Navarrete will make him pay with relentless volume.

“I’m looking to come in to make a statement,” Foster said. “I’m coming in to put on a dominant performance, show the world who I really am.”

Trying to invent power and aggression at age 31 against Navarrete is playing with fire. If Foster wants to leave San Antonio with the belts, he has to accept who he is, ignore the crowd, use his legs, and be content with a disciplined, ugly points win. Anything else plays right into Navarrete’s hands.

Foster has his sights set on undisputed status before jumping up in weight. Talking about blowing through Navarrete is bold talk, but a flat decision win will not deliver the respect he expects. Foster made big promises, and on October 24, he has to back them up against a puncher who never stops coming forward.

Sports.title: David Benavidez Plans His Own Promotional Company
Sports.content:
David Benavidez is launching DB Promotions to guide his own career once his contract with Sampson Lewkowicz wraps up in December. Even with the change, he intends to keep working alongside PBC and his existing inner circle.

Benavidez revealed his upcoming December bout marks the end of his decade-long deal with Lewkowicz. He treated the decision as a natural progression, making sure to acknowledge the promoter who helped build him into an attraction.

“This is the last fight on my contract,” Benavidez said to Brian Custer. “You know, I’ve honored the contract. The contract has been 10 years.”

Benavidez spoke carefully about the shift, never downplaying Lewkowicz while making it clear he is ready for independence.

“Sampson, he’s did a wonderful job,” Benavidez said. “He’s one of the greatest promoters of all time. But, you know, it’s just my time to do my own thing.”

When questioned about the venture’s name, he confirmed it will be DB Promotions, serving as his primary promotional banner starting early next year.

Stepping out on his own gives him significant leverage over the business side of his fight nights. Still, key details like equity splits, bankrolling, and operational responsibilities remain unstated, meaning the precise financial upside is impossible to calculate right now.

Putting his name on the banner gives Benavidez a chance to pocket more of the promotional money. That’s an obvious reason to make the move. But he still wants Al Haymon and TGB running the show alongside him. Having his own company won’t make the television money his, and he’ll still need those partners to get fights funded and dates booked.

Benavidez also aims to look past his own headline slots, expressing interest in signing boxers who train alongside him and his father, Jose Benavidez Sr.

“There’s a lot of great fighters I could take under my wing and put them under the promotion company,” he remarked.

Signing prospects gives DB Promotions life after Benavidez hangs up the gloves, yet building an actual stable turns a fighter into a financier. The expenses add up quickly with club show site rentals, airfare, hotel blocks, and purse guarantees that rarely turn a dime. Promoting his own headlining dates is one thing, but bankrolling young talent is a financial drain that devours capital long before a prospect ever sniffs a television date.

The move could let Benavidez pocket more of the money from potential fights with Jai Opetaia, Artur Beterbiev or Oleksandr Usyk. But with Haymon and TGB still involved, putting DB Promotions on the banner hardly means he’s going it alone.

Sports.title: Lucas Bahdi Seeks Schofield Rematch Over Knockdown Calls
Sports.content:
Most Valuable Promotions has formally challenged Lucas Bahdi’s defeat against Floyd Schofield III, petitioning the WBA for an immediate rematch after claiming uncalled knockdowns cost their fighter the vacant lightweight world championship.

The promotional outfit submitted video footage alongside detailed documentation to the WBA following the October 10 clash in Chicago. MVP maintains that if the referee had correctly recognized and scored the disputed incidents, Bahdi would have emerged with a majority decision win instead of leaving the ring empty-handed.

Schofield took the vacant belt by unanimous decision, capturing wide margins on the official cards with scores of 116 to 110, 115 to 111, and a steep 119 to 108. Bahdi’s side now wants the sanctioning body to grant another title opportunity, arguing that multiple officiating blunders corrupted those final numbers.

“The video evidence demonstrates multiple significant officiating errors that directly impacted the outcome of the fight,” MVP said in its statement. “Our review shows that had these knockdowns been properly ruled and scored, Lucas would have won the WBA lightweight world championship by majority decision.”

That claim sounds bold on paper, yet MVP failed to provide the necessary receipts to back it up. The public release never identified which specific rounds contained the uncalled drops, nor did it offer an adjusted scorecard breakdown to illustrate how Bahdi overturned an eleven-point deficit on the widest card.

Rather than rehashing standard complaints about judges favoring the house fighter, MVP pinned the blame directly on the third man in the ring. The core of their protest argues that referee mistakes prevented the judges from scoring mandatory 10 to 8 rounds, skewing the overall totals.

“We have submitted our findings to the WBA and requested an immediate rematch,” MVP said.

Securing a second fight remains an uphill climb. A rematch forces Schofield to revisit an opponent he already officially conquered, and lodging a protest never guarantees the WBA will order the boxers back into the ring. The sanctioning body has not issued a ruling on the video review, leaving MVP’s victory claim as promotional posturing until officials deliver a verdict.

Sports.title: Does Oleksandr Usyk Need Daniel Dubois Again?
Sports.content:
Daniel Dubois’ second-round stoppage of Fabio Wardley gives Oleksandr Usyk another possible opponent for his farewell fight. It also raises a harder question: how much would Usyk gain by beating someone he has already stopped twice?

Dubois retained his WBO heavyweight title on Saturday in London, rebuilding interest in a third meeting with the unbeaten Ukrainian. Usyk stopped him in nine rounds in 2023 and five rounds in their 2025 rematch. Those results leave Dubois needing the fight far more than Usyk does.

At 39, Usyk is choosing how to finish his career rather than working his way toward another championship opportunity. He has already become undisputed champion at cruiserweight and heavyweight, with two victories apiece over Anthony Joshua, Tyson Fury and Dubois.

That leaves a shortage of unfinished business.

A proposed Deontay Wilder fight would have offered a recognizable opponent Usyk had never faced. However, those negotiations have reportedly collapsed, with Fury and David Benavidez emerging as alternatives for a possible final appearance.

Fury’s appeal depends heavily on his December 11 fight with Joshua. A strong victory would give promoters something fresh to sell: Fury returning from that British heavyweight clash to take another run at the man who beat him twice in 2024. A defeat would make a third Usyk fight considerably harder to justify.

Dubois has strengthened his own case by stopping Wardley twice this year. Yet beating Wardley does not answer the technical questions Usyk posed in their previous meetings. Dubois would still need to show he can land consistently against Usyk’s movement and avoid being drawn into a fight where the Ukrainian controls the pace.

Benavidez would offer a different opponent and a fresh style, although his ability to compete with Usyk at heavyweight remains untested.

Usyk’s next fight needs more than a famous name or another belt attached to it. A Dubois trilogy would give the younger man a chance to overturn two defeats. The challenge for its backers is explaining why Usyk should spend his final appearance giving him that opportunity.

Sports.title: Artur Beterbiev Targets David Benavidez In Risky Cruiserweight Jump
Sports.content:
Artur Beterbiev wants David Benavidez next. He has spent over twenty months sitting on the sidelines, hoping for a trilogy clash with Dmitry Bivol that never materialized. Jumping up to cruiserweight offers a fresh target, but it also threatens to drag out his inactivity even longer.

Beterbiev dropped fresh training clips online this Monday, poking fun at his age while calling out the new division player. He joked about his physique looking like a man of forty-five, scaring people off. In reality, he sits at 41, turning 42 this coming January. That birthday will likely pass before he steps inside a ring again, especially since talks for a clash with Benavidez point toward 2027.

“Hope nobody was scared off by my 45-year-old physique,” Beterbiev wrote on social media.

Benavidez revealed the interest himself on Inside The Ring earlier this month. The former undisputed light heavyweight ruler reached out to his camp about meeting at the 200-pound limit. Benavidez sounded open to giving him the shot.

Chasing Benavidez hands Beterbiev a sensible target after the Bivol pursuit hit a wall. His February 2025 rematch with Bivol stands as his last sanctioned outing. Wasting nearly two years on that stalled trilogy took away precious championship time he can never get back.

The workout clips prove his muscle hasn’t vanished, but raw power was never the concern. The real test is sharpness under fire. Sitting idle chips away at reflexes, punch rhythm, championship stamina.

Benavidez brings relentless punch output that gym sessions cannot duplicate. Stepping up to 200 pounds also forces Beterbiev to show his heavy knockout power can hurt naturally larger men.

At the same time, Benavidez cannot sleep on the veteran. Beterbiev still carries sledgehammer power on the inside, creating real danger for anyone willing to stand in the pocket.

Sitting around waiting for Dmitry Bivol is pure career poison at this stage. Beterbiev is burning daylight he simply doesn’t have.

Turning 42 in January means every single idle month takes a bite out of his remaining sharpness. If the Benavidez camp can actually nail down a firm date for early 2027, fine, he can target that window. But if those talks drag out into vague promises or get pushed deep into the summer, Beterbiev cannot afford to sit in a training camp doing nothing.

The Bivol ship has sailed. Bivol went through back surgery, took other obligations, and showed zero urgency to jump straight back into a grueling trilogy war. Beterbiev spent the better part of two years holding out hope for that rubber match while his prime years slipped right out from under him.

If Benavidez isn’t locked in for Q1 2027, Beterbiev needs a stay-busy fight by late spring at the absolute latest. Even taking a mid-tier cruiserweight test to acclimatize to the 200-pound frame would do wonders for his timing. Heavy bag work and sparring with headgear can never replicate live incoming fire, especially against relentless combination punchers like Benavidez

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Wanted $15 Million Per Fight From Zuffa
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson wanted $15 million per fight from Zuffa Boxing regardless of who stood across from him, according to reporter Sean Zittel. The reported figures explain why Stevenson parted ways with the promotion without stepping into their ring.

Zittel reports that Zuffa explored a January date against Jose ‘Rayo’ Valenzuela in Newark that would have paid Stevenson roughly $7 million, with an alternative December slot against an undetermined opponent carrying similar money. Stevenson turned both options down, holding out for top-tier compensation. Zittel added that Stevenson initially accepted $15 million to fight Haney before raising his demands even higher. The reporter did not disclose the final dollar amount Stevenson sought after moving the goalposts.

“He wanted $15 million no matter who was going to be put in front of him,” Zittel said on his channel about Shakur’s purse expectations.

Zittel clarified that the $15 million target was originally connected to a potential showdown with Devin Haney. Instead of treating that number as an opponent-specific purse, Stevenson reportedly wanted that guarantee for every outing. Zittel noted that while he reached out without receiving a response from Stevenson or his team, his sourcing did not come from Bill Haney or anyone in the Haney camp.

He described the split between Shakur and Zuffa as mutual, with the fighter unhappy about the available money and the company unwilling to meet his price. Walking away leaves Stevenson searching for a backer willing to exceed that $7 million mark. While launching his own promotional company grants him control over his schedule, another outfit or broadcaster still must step up to fund those purses.

High-profile opponents demand substantial guarantees of their own, quickly inflating the total cost of staging an event.

Shakur earned a defining victory over Teofimo Lopez in January, yet his tenure with Zuffa concluded without another appearance. Turning down the Valenzuela bout kept him on the sidelines during prime earning months.

Unless a network or deep-pocketed backer agrees to meet that 15 million asking price, Stevenson will struggle to balance his self-valuation with what the sport is willing to pay him. Standing firm on an inflated number risks keeping him on the shelf while the rest of the division continues to move forward without him.

Sports.title: Carlos Adames Zuffa Debut Draws Fan Criticism
Sports.content:
Carlos Adames’ reported Zuffa Boxing debut against Gerome Warburton is drawing criticism from fans who see the Welsh fighter as an underwhelming opponent for the WBC middleweight champion.

According to Dan Rafael, Adames will face Warburton in the November 14 main event in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The bout will take place above 160 pounds, with Adames’ WBC title not at stake.

For Zuffa, signing Adames brings an established champion into its middleweight roster. However, introducing him against Warburton gives fans little opportunity to judge him against one of the division’s leading contenders. It looks like an opportunity for Adames to collect a win and make an impression before moving toward a bigger fight.

Warburton, 31, has an 18-2-2 record with two knockouts. That limited knockout total helps explain the reaction to his selection. Adames is accustomed to facing world-level opposition, and Warburton has yet to prove he belongs in that company.

His fourth-round stoppage loss to Kieron Conway in May 2025 is another reason fans are questioning the matchmaking. Conway beat him at British and Commonwealth level. Now Warburton is being brought in to headline against a reigning world champion.

There is some recent form in Warburton’s favor. He has won three consecutive fights since that defeat, including victories over Nathan Heaney in March and September this year. Those results deserve recognition when discussing how he landed this opportunity.

Nonetheless, beating Heaney twice does not establish Warburton as one of the best middleweights available. Adames represents a much higher level, and the pressure will be on the champion to produce a performance that reflects that difference.

A quick stoppage would give Zuffa a highlight to promote. A long, competitive fight could bring more criticism of Adames and raise questions about what this debut achieved.

The matchup gives Warburton a major opportunity. Adames has considerably less to gain.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Leaves Zuffa After Three Months
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson says Zuffa Boxing granted his release over the weekend, ending his three-month stay without a fight. The unbeaten four-division champion plans to start his own promotional company and pursue opponents at lightweight and light welterweight.

Stevenson announced the split in a video posted on his YouTube channel and shared on X. He described spending eight weeks in camp preparing for fights that never materialized.

“I requested to be released from Zuffa Boxing. Now over the weekend, my request has been granted, and now I am officially a free agent,” Stevenson said.

The 29-year-old signed with the Dana White-led company in July. He hasn’t fought since defeating Teofimo Lopez on January 31 at Madison Square Garden to win the WBO and Ring light welterweight titles.

Negotiations for a Devin Haney fight failed to produce an agreement amid disagreements over weight and rehydration conditions. Talks involving WBA light welterweight champion Gary Antuanne Russell also failed to produce a fight.

Stevenson insisted he wasn’t looking to blame anyone for his inactivity.

“This is the business of boxing. I’m not mad at anyone. I’m not pointing no fingers.”

Nevertheless, leaving so soon after signing shows how quickly his plans with Zuffa unraveled. The company secured a prominent unbeaten champion, but the relationship ended before he appeared on one of its cards. Zuffa declined immediate comment to The Ring.

Stevenson now wants control over how his next fights are arranged.

“I am now taking my career in my own hands and I’m starting my own promotional company,” he said.

He added that he is willing to work with other promoters and networks, opening the possibility of partnerships rather than another exclusive promotional deal. Shakur calling himself a promoter sounds empowering on social media, but acting as an actual bank is an entirely different business.

Starting a promotional banner without self-funding just means running an LLC to collect an extra operational fee while someone else assumes all the downside risk. If Stevenson expects a guaranteed purse in the multi-million-dollar range, that check has to clear through site fees, network licensing rights, ticket gates, and pay-per-view buys.

When an elite fighter possesses a purely defensive, safety-first ring style, the math turns hostile very quickly. Traditional promoters like Matchroom, Top Rank, or Queensberry understand what it takes to make an event profitable.

If external backers refuse to absorb those deficits, Stevenson will eventually face two stark paths: either accept realistic purses based on actual revenue generation, or find a wealthy benefactor willing to burn capital regardless of the balance sheet.

The moment Shakur put pen to paper with Zuffa and immediately waved off Jose “Rayo” Valenzuela, the whole premise of the deal fell apart. Dana White’s business model has always run on control, matching his roster internally, and fighters taking the bouts handed to them. Shakur treated the setup like a traditional boxing boutique where he could dictate terms, pick who makes financial sense, and snub the promoter’s own in-house assets.

Cutting bait after just three months was simply accepting the obvious. Shakur’s approach to the sport is completely incompatible with Dana White’s playbook.

“Give it maybe a year or two, we will get to 147 where everybody is pressing me to just be a 147-pounder,” Stevenson said. “I will get there, but on my term and not on nobody else’s.”

Ghana News.content:
…Bank of Ghana, Ministry of Finance, banks, traders and industry examine why cheaper money is reaching some borrowers faster than others

Lower interest rates are reaching borrowers of Ghana’s universal banks faster than customers of community and microfinance banks, according to a survey of banks presented at the third Post-Monetary Policy Committee (Post-MPC) Policy Seminar of Chartered Institute of Bankers, Ghana (CIB Ghana).

The seminar, held at the CIB Ghana Auditorium and streamed on the Institute’s social media platforms, brought together the Bank of Ghana (BoG), the Ministry of Finance, banks, traders and industry. Discussions centered on monetary policy transmission, credit growth and non-performing loans (NPLs).It followed the 132nd meeting of the BoG’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), which voted unanimously on 24 September to keep the policy rate unchanged at 14.0 percent.

Credit growth and credit quality must move together

Opening the seminar, the President of CIB Ghana Governing Council, Dr. Mrs. Ellen Ohene-Afoakwa, FCIB, said monetary policy had implications beyond economists and central bankers, as its effects were transmitted through financial markets, lending conditions, businesses and households. She said that the effectiveness of monetary policy depended not only on changes in the policy rate but also on the extent to which those changes were transmitted to the wider economy.“As an institute, we recognise that credit growth and credit quality must move together,” she said.

She added that Ghana needed a banking sector capable of providing adequate credit to productive sectors while maintaining strong risk management and responsible lending practices. On NPLs, she said greater attention should be placed on preventing bad loans than on recovering them after they had deteriorated.

Central bank perspective

In remarks read on his behalf by the BoG’s Director of Research, Dr. Simon Harvey, the Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr. Johnson P. Asiama, said changes in the policy rate do not pass through to borrowers at once, because banks also weigh funding costs, credit risk, operating costs and expected losses when pricing loans.

“This transmission is neither automatic nor instantaneous,” the Governor said.

He said the aim of monetary policy was not simply to achieve lower interest rates but to maintain anchored inflation expectations, a stable currency and sound financial institutions. He also called for a stronger focus on preventing NPLs. “The objective is not simply to achieve lower interest rates,” he said.

The Governor said the MPC found CIB Ghana’s Pre-MPC survey, which is presented to the Committee ahead of each meeting, insightful, helpful and complementary to its own analytical models.

Industry survey

The Chief Executive Officer of CIB Ghana, Mr. Robert Dzato, FCIB, presented findings from the Institute’s September Pre-MPC sentiment survey, which the CIB Ghana research team conducts among banks ahead of each MPC meeting to gather industry insights to support the work of the MPC. Mr. Dzato said the survey showed strong appetite among banks to lend, although the impact of monetary policy transmission varied across market segments. “We see appetite to lend is quite high,” he said, noting that “the real impact of the transmission of monetary policy varies across the various segments.”

Lending rates differed widely by type of bank. Most universal banks surveyed reported lending at 10 to 15 percent. Among community banks, 46 percent reported lending at 21 to 25 percent, up from 36 percent in the July survey, while microfinance banks reported rates of roughly 31 to 40 percent.

Other findings:

About 65 percent of respondents expressed high confidence in the macroeconomic environment.

About 80 percent consider the current policy stance effective in containing inflation.

86 percent of respondents expected the MPC to hold the policy rate, as it did

70 percent expect inflation to rise over the next three months.

71 percent of the banks are confident of meeting the 10 percent NPL directive by the end of 2026.

Although most banks were confident about the wider economy, a majority expected inflation to rise in the coming months, an upside risk that also featured in the panel’s discussion of the MPC’s decision to hold. On asset quality, he described banks’ confidence in meeting the NPL target of 10 percent by year end, as encouraging but warned that faster credit growth had to be matched by stronger monitoring, recovery and risk mitigation. “We are driving credit growth for obvious reasons,” Mr. Dzato said, adding that loans that were not repaid on time could create another problem for the sector.

Panel discussion

The panel was moderated by Mrs. Ellen Gyamera, ACIB, Head of the Petroleum Fund at the BoG, and comprised Dr. Simon Harvey, Director of Research of Bank of Ghana; Mr Frederick Amissah, a Technical Advisor to the Ministry of Finance; Dr. Charles Atuahene, Executive Member of Finance and Administration Committee of Association of Ghana Industries (AGI); Mr. John Awuah, Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Association of Banks and Mr. Clement Boateng, the President of the Ghana Union of Traders Association (GUTA).

Dr. Harvey set out the basis for the MPC’s decision to hold the policy rate, including upside risks to inflation. Mr. Amissah spoke on coordination between fiscal and monetary authorities, and on the role of fiscal discipline in keeping prices stable and bringing down government borrowing costs. Panellists noted that loan pricing had fallen from its past highs and discussed the scope for further declines over time. Mr. Awuah addressed access to credit, the documentation and record-keeping borrowers need to qualify, and the role of collateral enforcement and the courts in recovering bad loans, drawing comparisons with NPL levels elsewhere in the region.

Mr. Boateng called for repayment terms, including grace periods, that reflect traders’ import cycles and shipping delays. Dr. Atuahene discussed how exchange rate movements affect exporters’ competitiveness, input costs and businesses’ appetite to borrow.

Institute update

Dr. Ohene-Afoakwa highlighted the Institute’s growth in professional education, certification and ethics, including its Non-Interest Banking Certification, Branch CEO Programme, digital and ESG certifications and Ethics 2.0 class. She also noted Ghana’s success in winning the right to host the World Conference of Banking Institutes in 2028. She also appealed for support for the Institute’s planned modern bankers’ house and business complex, describing the project as an investment in the future of the banking profession and in building a stronger, more professional and future-ready financial sector. The seminar forms part of events leading up to the annual Bankers Week.

Ghana News.title: Kofi Adams explores Hyundai partnership to develop school sports
Ghana News.content:
Ghana's Sports and Recreation Minister, Kofi Adams, has held talks with Hyundai Motor Group executives on a proposed partnership to develop school sports, football infrastructure and archery in the country.

The meeting, held at the Ministry on Monday, 19 October 2026, brought together Hyundai Motor Group Executive Vice-President Ilbum Kim, Ghana's Ambassador to South Korea, Kojo Choi, and representatives of Hyundai's operations in Ghana.

The discussions focused on strengthening school and grassroots sports, improving access to equipment and developing facilities to support young athletes.

Mr Adams said the government was prioritising school and grassroots sports as the foundation for sustainable sporting development.

He noted that about 1.3 million students attend senior high and senior high technical schools in Ghana, highlighting the need for better infrastructure, equipment and corporate support to strengthen existing school competitions.

The minister acknowledged that grassroots sports might not generate immediate commercial returns but argued that establishing strong structures and standards could encourage greater private-sector investment.

One of the key proposals discussed was Hyundai's potential support for the development of FIFA Arena mini-football pitches in Ghana, with the possibility of delivering the facilities in early 2027.

Mr Kim reaffirmed the company's belief in sport as a tool for social development and expressed interest in working with FIFA to bring the initiative to Ghana.

He also commended the Ministry's commitment to youth development, noting Ghana's football heritage and potential.

Mr Adams welcomed the proposal but called for a broader partnership that would also provide schools with footballs, boots and other essential training equipment.

He said the proposed facilities should deliver lasting benefits to the communities in which they are established.

The minister also proposed an annual Hyundai National School Sports Championship to strengthen organised school competitions and provide a platform for identifying and developing young talent.

In response, Mr Kim said Hyundai would explore the possibility of reviving its One Million Dream Balls for Africa initiative, which was introduced during the 2010 FIFA World Cup in South Africa.

He said the company intended to engage its affiliated football club, Jeonbuk Hyundai Motors, and former United Nations Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon to explore renewed support for the programme.

The proposed revival could provide an avenue for expanding access to football equipment among young players across the continent.

The discussions identified archery as another potential area of cooperation, drawing on Hyundai's longstanding investment in the sport in South Korea.

Ambassador Kojo Choi said the development of archery in Ghana could attract interest from Hyundai's leadership and create opportunities for equipment support, technical exchanges and youth development.

Both sides also highlighted the longstanding diplomatic relationship between Ghana and South Korea, which will mark its 50th anniversary in 2027.

They noted existing Korean support for taekwondo development in Ghana and expressed optimism about extending cooperation to other sporting disciplines.

The Ministry and Hyundai Motor Group are expected to continue discussions on the proposed initiatives, with the aim of expanding sporting opportunities and creating sustainable development pathways for young people across Ghana.

Ghana News.title: Breathing Poison: Toxic smoke from Agbogbloshie e-waste burning still making workers sick
Ghana News.content:
By Prince Owusu Asiedu

Smoke from burning electronic waste at Agbogbloshie in Accra is filling the air with toxic chemicals, and researchers have long said the harmful effects are already getting into people's bodies — making them sick and, in some cases, killing them.

It has been nearly two decades since clear evidence of direct human exposure to e-waste contaminants was found among workers at Agbogbloshie. In a 2012 study, urine samples from 20 male e-waste workers aged between 15 and 42 found significantly higher levels of iron, the flame-retardant antimony, and lead in the urine of the e-waste workers.

"The findings suggest that the workers were absorbing these metals through their work, potentially by inhaling fumes and coming into contact with burnt metals and ash," said Dr. Kwadwo Ansong, acting director of the Water Research Institute of Ghana’s Council for Scientific and Industrial Research, the national body for applied scientific research, who led the study.

Agbogbloshie e-waste site has been a growing problem for governments and locals for decades.

Ghanaians discard old televisions, refrigerators, computers, mobile phones, air conditioners and other electrical appliances. Some of these items enter the informal recycling system, where scrap dealers dismantle equipment and recover valuable materials such as copper and aluminium.

Ghana has also received large quantities of used electrical and electronic equipment from abroad in return for payment. While some products are still functional and are sold as second-hand goods, others are destined for Ghana’s scrap heaps, making rich countries’ waste Ghanaians’ problem.

The second-hand market provides relatively affordable appliances and creates income for traders, collectors, dismantlers and scrap dealers. But informal recycling involves open burning, which releases airborne contaminants.

The levels of toxins found in urine samples show how bad the impact is. Toxins in bodily fluids show they have spread throughout people’s organs through the bloodstream, typical of prolonged exposure. That can lead to profound health effects and diseases that are among Ghana’s fast-growing burden of hypertension, diabetes, stroke and cancer.

For many workers, the danger to their lives has already become clear. 35-year-old scrap dealer Musah Abdulai said he has worked in the scrap business for about 15 years. In July this year, his blood pressure skyrocketed.

"I have been handling materials at the site and inhaling smoke from burning e-waste every day,” he said in Twi. “I became seriously ill and had to be hospitalised.”

Doctors told him his exposure to toxic smoke at the scrap yard was responsible.

"They asked me whether I smoked cigarettes. I told them I don't. They said the toxic smoke was the cause," he said.

Abdulai spent GH¢3,000 (US$263) he did not have on treatment.

More evidence of the toll from toxic e-waste at the site came from blood and breast milk samples taken from e-waste workers and sellers, including mothers who attended Ridge Hospital and Tema Hospital.

"According to the tests, we found the presence of chemicals Dioxins, Furans, polychlorinated Biphenyls," said Pennante Bruce-Vanderpuije, a researcher at the Water Research Institute of Ghana’s Council, in studies published in 2019 and 2020.

She warned that exposure may extend beyond e-waste workers because contaminated air, water, soil and food could affect people living in surrounding communities. In addition to causing harm to the mothers, she warned about the risk to the developing organs and brains of babies from ingesting the contaminated breast milk.

But she urged mothers not to stop breastfeeding because of the findings. “The benefits of breast milk remain greater than the risks posed by the detected chemicals. We should not discourage breastfeeding.”

Instead, researchers said government must act fast to clean up the site more comprehensively than it has in the past.

Agbogbloshie is one of the worst locations for air pollution in Accra. With one of Africa’s fastest-growing populations, people are driving up air pollution as they demand more transport, consume more transported goods, and burn more household waste.

Public health data has shown a rise in a range of chronic illnesses linked to air pollution. Dr Louisa Ademki Matey, Metropolitan Director of the Ghana Health Service, says respiratory illness was the number one reason for Out-Patient Department attendance from 2022 to 2024.

"We attribute it to pollutants from open burning and dust particles," Dr. Matey said in an interview. "This pollution can lead to conditions such as pneumonia, heart attack, stroke, and worsen people with chronic conditions. Pregnant women can have miscarriages and premature births with babies because it affects the organs very badly.”

Government has been working for the last five years to combat the Agbogbloshie air pollution crisis. In 2021, the government demolished the Agbogbloshie scrapyard as part of a redevelopment exercise. But scrap dealers returned to parts of the area. In 2025, Ibrahim Murtala Mohammed, then Minister for Environment, Science and Technology, warned scrap dealers against burning e-waste.

The current Environmental Protection Authority, working with environment advocates Green Advocacy Ghana and Pure Earth, has tried giving scrap dealers wire-stripping machines to save them from burning the plastic that encases copper in the wires they are scrapping.

"But they felt it was time-consuming, so they went back to burning copper with fire,” said Prof. Michael Ayamga-Adongo, Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the Environmental Protection Authority. “We are also buying copper directly from them and placing e-waste collection containers at malls for people to drop collapsed gadgets.”

Dr. Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, Minister for Environment, Science and Technology, has urged the Authority to prosecute polluters.

"Nobody should be compromised. EPA must collaborate with other stakeholders to improve their operations to reduce pollution in any form in the country," she said in an interview following her appointment as minister.

The Accra Metropolitan Assembly and other assemblies have intensified education on open burning at Agbogbloshie and its environs, with some success.

"We have been engaging drivers, traders and scrap dealers about the dangers to their health,” said Florence Kuukyi, Director of the Metro Health Department. She provided data from air quality monitoring showing that air pollution in Agbogbloshie had reduced between July 2025 and 2025.

But as efforts to clean the site intensify, for many here, the risk to their livelihood is the more immediate danger than their health.

Fuseni Fatawu, a trader who buys condemned phones, laptops and other electronic equipment, said exposure to smoke has become part of his daily working environment.

"I frequently suffer from headaches and coughs,” he said in Twi. He has been diagnosed with high blood pressure and diabetes. He seeks treatment at the hospital regularly, “but I continue working here because this trade is how I feed my family.”

He is one of many who would like government help to move away from here and build a business somewhere safe. Without it, he said, he has no choice but to continue to see his health decline.

This story was a collaboration with New Narratives as part of the Clean Air Ghana Reporting Project. Funding was provided by the Clean Air Fund, which had no say in the story’s content.

Ghana News.title: Hindsight: Sekondi Sports Stadium reopens, but sustainability and functionality issues remain
Ghana News.content:
On October 13, the Sekondi Sports Stadium came back to life.

For the first time in seven years, the stadium hosted a competitive, elite-level football match: an Olympic Qualifier between Ghana's Black Queens and Mauritius.

In the end, the Queens put seven past Mauritius.

A fitting result to mark the reopening of a stadium many had not used in nearly a decade.

Much has changed since it was last used.

The beams, weak compression rings, weak trusses, and corroded roofing sheets have all been replaced.

Now, they spot an unmistakable coating system, ostensibly to prevent deterioration in the manner of the former state.

The old plastic seats, previously covered in dust and whatever else its recent users left on it, have also been replaced by brightly-colored new ones that,

From the West Stand, East through to the North Stand, every single seat has been removed and replaced.

Approximately twenty-five feet from the stands, lies familiar, green-pigmented plants joined together by their stems and held in place by the soil - the playing surface.

Before last week's opening, the last memory fans had of the pitch was an insect-infested, brownish grass. Like crops on farms in the dry seasons, whose owners have relocated to the next village in search of water: nutrient-deficient and neglected.

Now, however, it has a familiar green look to it, even if not entirely Bermuda, Kentucky, or Perennial grass.

The scoreboard has been fixed too.

But that is as far as it goes.

They only fixed the broken parts without addressing the main challenges with the stadium.

Concerns.

The stadium is still is very limited in terms of what it can host.

It can host track and field events, but the results recorded will not be recognized internationally because the stadium does not meet required standards.

The tartan tracks, for example, are not internationally certified. So do not expect Benjamin Azamati or any of Ghana’s elite-level athletes to be running on it.

What it can do is host inter-school events in the Sekondi Takoradi Metropolis like it always has – even then, there is a limit to the disciplines that can be held there.

There is no space for basketball, volleyball, or tennis.

Next year will be the 20th anniversary of the Sekondi Sports Stadium.

For a renovation this close to the anniversary, it would have been prudent to consider fixing these issues once and for all.

Maintenance and sustainability

If anything symbolizes the poor maintenance culture at the stadium, it is the forty rooms that were marked as hotel spaces, but have not been touched since the stadium was opened in 2007.

For nineteen years, the forty rooms have been empty.

The NSA could have rented the rooms out as offices, but chose not to.

The internal bureaucracies of the institution have often been blamed.

But it is hard to take these seriously.

After all, it is not as though the process for its lease was ever set in motion.

Across seven different governments and a million appointees to its head office and the Sports Development Officers (NSA Regional Heads), nobody did anything about the quietly sleeping 40 rooms.

Probably because the empty rooms did not speak loudly enough.

Or if we pretended the media had not made enough noise to draw the NSA's attention.

At the moment, there are no plans to furnish the rooms and use them for the intended purposes.

Ghana News.title: World Cup visa scandal: $26,000 paid to police on behalf of Ampofo Ankrah
Ghana News.content:
A total of $26,000 has reportedly been paid to the police on behalf of suspended National Sports Authority (NSA) Director-General Yaw Ampofo Ankrah, part of the $56,000 he is alleged to have received as commission from proceeds linked to the World Cup visa scandal.

People familiar with the payment told JoySports that the money was paid last week by a friend of Mr Ankrah, with the approval of the suspended NSA boss and his lawyers.

The sources said the individual had undertaken to pay the outstanding balance.

JoySports contacted Mr Ankrah on 15 October to verify the payment, but he did not respond to the request for comment.

The payment comes amid investigations into allegations of visa racketeering involving NSA officials and other individuals in connection with arrangements for the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico.

Mr Ankrah has denied the allegations levelled against him in a petition filed by the NSA's former Chief Operations Officer, Yaw Gyamfi Kusi Awere.

"I challenge any man or woman to come forward and say they have given me even a penny to help them to process visas. I have never and will never do such a thing," he said in a statement last month.

Earlier this month, his lawyer, Jerry Avenorgbor, told Newsfile that the police were investigating the allegations "aggressively" and that Mr Ankrah had made multiple appearances before the Criminal Investigations Department (CID).

Sources familiar with the investigation said Mr Ankrah had told investigators that he and Mr Gyamfi had exchanged money over the course of their relationship, which dates back to 1989.

However, he maintained that he did not know the money in question represented commission from prospective travellers seeking visa assistance.

Mr Gyamfi filed the petition seeking police intervention to recover the $56,000 he alleged Mr Ankrah had received as commission from prospective travellers.

Mr Ankrah maintains that the allegations against him concerning visa-related payments are unfounded.

Sources familiar with this scheme said about 180 prospective travellers had paid between $4,000 and $25,000 for visa assistance in the hope of travelling to the 2026 World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico.

None of the applicants seeking support to travel to Canada received visas, while about 37 out of the 180 applicants obtained visas.

A list of 90 people submitted by Mr Ankrah to the Sports Ministry on 19 May 2026, seeking support for visa applications, did not result in any of the applicants receiving a visa appointment date.

Mr Gyamfi has claimed that the individuals paid money before their names were included on the list submitted for visa support.

The people are demanding a refund.

Mr Ankrah has denied knowledge of wrongdoing and recently told Sporty FM that he was "200 percent sure" he would "be exonerated".

JoySports investigation uncovered the use of an office at the NSA by Tribe Culture Fest to operate the visa-related scheme.

The NSA has, however, said it did not authorise visa facilitation activities at its premises.

On 1 October, President John Dramani Mahama suspended Mr Ankrah as Director-General of the NSA pending investigations into the alleged visa racketeering.

The suspension followed a report submitted to the Presidency by Sports Minister Kofi Adams concerning the allegations.

The police investigation is expected to establish the circumstances surrounding the alleged payments, the roles of the individuals involved and whether any offences were committed.

Meanwhile, President has set up a committee a the Jubilee House Chaired by Professor Francis Dodoo to investigate the scandal.

Ghana News.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Starting the 2027 Strategic Planning Process
Ghana News.content:
Daily Insights

By Ernest De-Graft Egyir

Insight.

Strategic planning for 2027 should begin before the current year closes. CEOs who wait until December risk making important decisions under time pressure, relying on incomplete analysis, or carrying existing priorities into the new year without sufficient review.

Starting early gives the executive team time to examine current performance, understand market developments, reassess strategic assumptions, and determine what the organization must do differently to achieve its next set of objectives.

Key Strategies:

Review current-year financial and operational performance. Assess changes in customer expectations, competition, technology, and the broader business environment. Identify strategic assumptions that need to be reconsidered. Consult executives and relevant stakeholders on emerging priorities. Establish a realistic planning timetable with clear responsibilities and milestones.

CEO Leadership Actions.

✅ Initiate the 2027 strategic planning process with the executive team.

✅ Require evidence-based assessments of current performance and future opportunities.

✅ Identify the major strategic questions that leadership must resolve before approving the 2027 plan.

Actionable Tip.

Ask your executive team: “What have we learned in 2026 that should fundamentally influence our strategy for 2027?”

Why This Matters?

Early planning creates room for better analysis, meaningful discussion, and deliberate resource allocation. It allows the CEO to enter 2027 with a clearer direction rather than spending the first quarter correcting decisions that should have been made earlier.

About the Author.✍🏿

Ernest De-Graft Egyir, CEO advisor, Thought Leader and Founding CEO of Chief Executives Network Ghana, convenes the Ghana CEO Summit and served on Ghana’s Economic Dialogue Planning Committee

Ghana News.title: IEAG demands probe into reported MSC office assault, warns of rising tensions at Tema Port
Ghana News.content:
The Importers and Exporters Association of Ghana (IEAG) has called for an impartial investigation into a reported assault incident at the Mediterranean Shipping Company (MSC) office at the Tema Port, warning that unresolved operational challenges could trigger further confrontations between port users and service providers.

The Association says persistent delays in shipping invoices, payment confirmation and container releases, alongside mounting charges and disruptions to cargo movement, are increasing financial pressure on businesses operating at the port.

In a press statement dated October 19, 2026, IEAG’s Executive Secretary, Samson Asaki Awingobit, condemned violence and unlawful conduct while urging the authorities to investigate the reported incident and address the underlying grievances.

“Any allegation of assault must be investigated impartially by the appropriate authorities, and anyone found culpable must be dealt with in accordance with the law,” the statement said.

The Association cautioned that prolonged delays and uncertainty over essential shipping services could heighten frustration among importers, clearing agents and other port users, potentially leading to further confrontations.

IEAG warned that unresolved tensions could result in serious injuries, property destruction, disruptions to port operations and threats to the safety of workers and the wider port community.

“The authorities must not wait for a preventable confrontation to result in serious injury or loss of life before taking decisive action,” it said.

Beyond the reported MSC office incident, the Association raised concerns about disruptions at the Meridian Port Services (MPS) Terminal 3, where more than 120 trucks reportedly scheduled to transfer containers were delayed by issues attributed to terminal operations.

According to IEAG, such disruptions can prolong truck turnaround times, increase the cost of container movements, affect haulage schedules and create bottlenecks across the wider logistics chain.

The Association said allegations that the delays were contributing to the accumulation of rent, storage and other charges had not been independently established and should be investigated transparently.

It has called on the Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority (GPHA), working with MPS and other relevant stakeholders, to establish the causes of the disruptions, determine responsibility and clarify the basis for any additional charges imposed on affected port users.

IEAG is also urging the Minister for Finance to convene an emergency meeting involving the Ghana Shippers’ Authority, GPHA, shipping lines, terminal operators and other industry stakeholders to address the operational challenges and security concerns.

The Association wants the meeting to secure enforceable service timelines, effective complaints mechanisms, transparent performance monitoring and fair treatment of additional charges where service-provider failures are established.

It also wants applicable Service Level Agreements to be enforced, arguing that shipping lines and terminal operators must be held accountable for their obligations just as shippers are expected to comply with container-return deadlines and other contractual requirements.

“Accountability in the maritime sector must be reciprocal. Shippers must fulfil their obligations, but shipping lines and terminal operators must equally be held accountable for the services they are contracted or required to provide,” the statement said.

IEAG says a coordinated intervention is necessary to restore confidence, improve port efficiency and prevent further escalation of tensions within Ghana’s maritime trade and logistics sector.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Morocco’s not-so-new government faces new challenges
World.content:
The new cabinet has doubled down on continuity at a time of regional turmoil and domestic anxiety.

On October 16, King Mohammed VI of Morocco appointed a new government headed by Prime Minister Fatima Zohra Al Mansouri. This is the first time in Moroccan history that a woman is leading the government – a precedent that was covered widely in international media.

In the Moroccan context, however, what is important is that Al Mansouri hails from the Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM), which won the most seats in parliamentary elections in September. The party was founded by Ali Himma, a close associate and adviser to the king.

PAM, which has formed a coalition with three other parties, dominates the new government. This signals continuity rather than potential for change.

A party aligned with the monarchy

When thinking about what trajectory the new government is likely to take, it is important to consider PAM’s evolution.

The party was established in 2008 with the aim of countering the rise of political Islam in Morocco and in particular, the Justice and Development Party (PJD). The Arab Spring, which saw mass protests across the country, brought changes to the Moroccan political scene, allowing more space for political forces like the PJD and, to an extent, curbing the influence of the establishment, known as the Makhzen.

In 2011, Himma distanced himself from PAM and became an adviser to the king. Yet, the party continued to be perceived by other political groups as tied to the Makhzen.

For years, PAM carried the stigma of its origins, but it persisted in trying to gain acceptance. In the 2016 elections, it challenged the PJD and secured the second-biggest number of votes, thus establishing itself as a legitimate political force. Yet this was still not enough to enable it to lead the government.



The party subsequently reinvented itself by rejuvenating its ranks and gaining experience in public affairs through its participation in the 2021 government as a coalition partner. In the latest elections, PAM finally won.

This election victory, however, needs to be put into perspective: 62 percent of eligible voters stayed away from the polls. On election day, the authorities had to call on people to go out and vote.

Apart from the low turnout, there were suspicions of irregularities, but because in some cases the official election records were not released, observers and political parties were unable to obtain tangible evidence.

There was also the familiar phenomenon of influential figures being brought into political parties at the last minute to boost electoral prospects. For example, just two months before the election, Faouzi Laaqjea, president of the Royal Moroccan Football Federation, whose popularity stems from the achievements of Moroccan football, officially joined PAM.

To secure a majority in parliament, the party has had to form a coalition with forces which had previously questioned its legitimacy. While PAM has gained legitimacy through this alliance, the other parties and their leaders may now lose credibility.

The newly formed government has retained more than half the members of its predecessor, not to mention the so-called sovereign ministries, which fall directly within the king’s reserved powers.
