The directive, contained in a statement signed by Secretary to the State Government, Dr Kingsley Emu, was a mark of respect for Uduaghan, who governed Delta State from 2007 to 2015.

Sheriff Oborevwori, Ede Dafinone Mourn

Oborevwori expressed sadness over Uduaghan’s death, describing him as a detribalised leader, whose contributions to the development of the state would not be forgotten.

In a condolence message by his Chief Press Secretary, Sir Festus Ahon, Oborevwori sympathised with the late governor’s wife, Roli, his children, the entire Uduaghan family, the Itsekiri nation, and Deltans over the painful loss.

The governor recalled Uduaghan’s years in office, stating that he made significant contributions to infrastructure development in the state.

He described the former governor as a leader who looked beyond ethnic differences and worked for the overall development of Delta State.

Oborevwori said Uduaghan’s years in public service had left a good mark on the state, adding that his death was a loss to Delta and the country at large.

He prayed for the peaceful repose of the former governor’s soul and asked God to comfort his wife, children, family members, the Itsekiri nation, and all those grieving his death.

Senator Ede Dafinone, who the senator for Delta Central Senatorial District, described Uduaghan as a distinguished statesman, whose contributions to the development of the state will remain indelible.

Dafinone, in a condolence statement he personally signed, expressed profound sadness over the former governor’s death, describing it as a great loss to Delta State and Nigeria.

He stated that Uduaghan’s years of service as Commissioner for Health, Secretary to the State Government, and two-term governor reflected his commitment to public service and good governance.

According to the senator, the former governor will be remembered for his inclusive leadership, infrastructural development, and efforts to promote unity and peaceful coexistence among the diverse ethnic groups in Delta State.

Orode Uduaghan

Daughter of the deceased former governor of Delta State, Orode Uduaghan, paid an emotional tribute to her father, saying her love for him would endure forever.

Orode, the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Warri North I Constituency, expressed her grief in a brief emotional post on her official Facebook page following the former governor’s death on Monday.

“Thank you for everything. I love you yesterday, today and forever. Sleep well Papa,” she wrote, adding a love emoji.

Delta APC

All Progressives Congress (APC) in Delta State expressed deep sorrow over the passing of Uduaghan.

The party’s State Chairman, Chief Solomon Arenyeka, in a statement by State Publicity Secretary, Valentine Onojeghuo, last night, said the former governor’s years of public service and contributions to Delta State would remain an important part of the state’s political and developmental history.

Arenyeka described Uduaghan as a detribalised leader, accomplished public servant and statesman who promoted unity, mutual respect, and peaceful coexistence among the diverse ethnic groups in the state.

The APC chairman stated, “The passing of Dr. Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan is a painful loss to Delta State and our country. He was a leader who recognised that our diversity is a source of strength and that the progress of Delta State depends on our collective commitment to unity, peace and development.”

Ifeanyi Okowa

Immediate past Governor of Delta State, Senator Ifeanyi Okowa, expressed sadness over the death of his predecessor, Dr. Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan.

Okowa said, in a condolence message, “I received with deep sadness the news of the passing of my predecessor and brother, His Excellency, Dr. Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan.

“As the governor who served Delta State before me, Dr. Uduaghan was an important part of our state’s journey. His years of service and contributions to Delta’s development remain part of our collective history.”

Okowa said the death was a painful loss to them as a family and extended condolences to his wife, Roli, children and the entire Uduaghan family.

David Mark

National Chairman of African Democratic Congress (ADC), Senator David Mark, described Uduaghan’s passing as a painful loss to Delta State, the Niger Delta, and Nigeria.

Mark, in a condolence message, said Uduaghan’s death was particularly saddening, given his contributions to public service and the development of Delta State during his years in leadership.

In a statement by his Special Adviser, Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbndiyan, the ADC chairman stated that Uduaghan’s years in public office placed him at the centre of efforts to advance peace, development, and improved living conditions for the people of Delta State.

According to Mark, the late former governor’s experience in governance and his service to the people would remain an important part of his public legacy.

The statement said, “Dr. Emmanuel Uduaghan’s death is a painful loss to Delta State and our country. He was a public servant who devoted a significant part of his life to the service of his people and the development of his state.

“His passing is a moment of grief for his family, the people of Delta State and all those who had the privilege of working with him or benefiting from his years of service.”

Emomotimi Guwor

Chairman, Conference of Speakers of State Legislatures in Nigeria and Speaker, Delta State House of Assembly, Hon. Emomotimi Guwor, expressed sorrow over the passing of Uduaghan.

Guwor, in a condolence message by his Chief Press Secretary, Mr. Nkem Nwaeke, said Uduaghan’s death was a great and painful loss to Delta State and the nation, particularly at a time when his experience and counsel as an elder statesman remained invaluable.

Guwor described Uduaghan as a passionate leader whose vision, policies, and commitment to public service positively impacted the lives of many Deltans during his eight-year administration.

Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan

Senator Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan described her in-law’s death as a profound loss to his family, the people of Delta State, and Nigerians, who valued his years of public service.

In a condolence message, Akpoti-Uduaghan said the deceased was a revered patriarch whose life reflected family devotion, public service, and contributions to the development of Delta State.

She expressed sympathy with the Uduaghan family, saying his death has created a painful void that would be difficult to fill.

The Kogi Central senator stated, “Words are painfully inadequate to express the depth of my sorrow at the passing of His Excellency, Dr. Chief Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan. His death is a profound loss, and my heart goes out to the entire Uduaghan family at this incredibly difficult moment.”

Christian Association of Nigeria

Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), in a statement by its President, Archbishop Daniel Okoh, extended condolences to Uduaghan’s family, the government, and people of Delta State.

Okoh said Uduaghan played a notable role during a period of heightened political tension in Nigeria and commended his commitment to dialogue and preservation of national unity.

He described the former governor’s passing as a loss to his family and to all who valued his contributions to public service and nation-building, praying God to comfort his family and grant his soul eternal rest.

Jonathan Ukodhiko

The member representing Isoko North and Isoko South Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Jonathan Ukodhiko, described Uduaghn’s passing as a painful loss to the state.

In a condolence message by his Media Team, Ukodhiko commiserated with the late governor’s wife, Deaconess Roli Uduaghan, his children, the Uduaghan family of Abigborodo, the Itsekiri nation, and the entire people of Delta State.

The federal lawmaker, who is Deputy Chairman of House Committee on Science and Technology, acknowledged Uduaghan’s contributions to the development of Delta State, particularly in public administration, human capital development, infrastructure and security.

Ukodhiko said, “This is a painful loss, not only to his immediate family and the Itsekiri nation but also to Delta State, which he served in various capacities, including as governor. I pray that God grants his family the strength to bear this irreparable loss.”

Government Ekpemupolo

High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, expressed sadness over the death of Uduaghan, describing his demise as unexpected and a great loss.

Tompolo, the Ibe-Ebidouwei of the Ijaw Nation and Chairman of Tantita Security Services Nigeria Limited, expressed his condolences in a statement signed by his Media Consultant, Dr Paul Bebenimibo.

In his condolence message, Tompolo recalled Uduaghan’s contributions during the period of the Niger Delta agitations, particularly his support for the Presidential Amnesty Programme and the pipeline surveillance initiative introduced during the administrations of the late President Umaru Musa Yar’Adua and former President Goodluck Jonathan.

He stated that the former governor played an important role during a critical period in the Niger Delta, when efforts were being made to address insecurity, promote peace, and improve stability in the oil-producing region.

Tompolo said Uduaghan’s contributions would not be forgotten, adding that the former governor would be greatly missed.

Ambassador Oma Djebah

Former Nigerian Envoy to Thailand, Ambassador Oma Djebah, expressed shock over the news of Uduaghan’s demise, calling the sad development a huge loss to Delta State, Nigeria, and, indeed, all loved ones across various international jurisdictions.

Djebah added that the late former governor left a legacy of a huge positive impact.

He stated, “I am deeply shocked and saddened over the sad demise of this great leader, a patriot, and a very compassionate administrator who gave his all in his service to Delta State and Nigeria.

“His death has created a void that would be very difficult to fill. I’m still short of words to convey my feelings over this sad loss.”

Djebah, who served as Commissioner for Information under Uduaghan, added, “He was resilient, forthright, educated and visionary. He was a great boss, friend, leader and astute administrator. His politics was highly refined. He led from the front, and with his heart.”

Uduaghan, a medical doctor by profession, governed Delta State from 2007 to 2015, completing two terms in office.

Before becoming governor, he served as the state’s Commissioner for Health between 1999 and 2003 and, subsequently, as Secretary to the State Government from 2003 to 2007.

He succeeded former Governor James Ibori in 2007 and remained active in Delta State and national politics after leaving office in 2015.

Born on October 22, 1954, Uduaghan died three days before his 72nd birthday.

World.title: Gombe Govt Commiserates with Bauchi over Death of Health Agency CEO, Four Children
World.content:
Segun Awofadeji in Gombe

Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya of Gombe State has expressed deep sorrow over the tragic death of the Executive Secretary of the Bauchi State Health Contributory Management Agency (BASHCMA), Alhaji Ibrahim Ladan Duguri and four of his children in a fatal road accident.

Governor Inuwa Yahaya described the incident as heartbreaking, saying the tragic loss of a father and four of his children in such painful circumstances was devastating and a profound loss to the bereaved family and the entire Bauchi State.

This is contained in a press release issued by Ismaila Uba Misilli, Director-General (Press Affairs), Government House, Gombe, and made available to journalists on Monday.

The governor, on behalf of the government and people of Gombe State, extended his heartfelt condolences to his Bauchi State counterpart, Senator Bala Abdulkadir Mohammed, the government and people of Bauchi State, and the immediate and extended family the deceased, the statement said.

Governor Inuwa Yahaya said the people of Gombe State shared in the grief of their Bauchi neighbours at this difficult moment, stressing that the tragedy has touched the hearts of many beyond the borders of Bauchi State.

“Our hearts are with the government and people of Bauchi State, particularly the bereaved family, as they grapple with this painful loss. The people of Gombe State join you in mourning Alhaji Ibrahim Duguri and his beloved children. We pray that Almighty Allah grants the family the strength and fortitude to bear this devastating tragedy,” the governor said.

He beseeched Almighty Allah to forgive the shortcomings of the deceased, grant them Aljannat Firdaus, and comfort the family, friends, colleagues and all those affected by the tragedy.

The governor also prayed for the speedy and complete recovery of Suleiman, the surviving son who sustained critical injuries in the accident.

World.title: 2027: Wike Meets Fubara’s Supporters
World.content:
Olawale Ajimotokan in Abuja

Minister of the FCT, Nyesom Wike, has forged a realignment with the supporters of Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, ahead of the 2027 general election.

The parley, held yesterday in Port Harcourt, brought together Wike, youth leaders and supporters loyal to Fubara, signalled a significant step towards reconciling the rival political camps and building a united front under the Rainbow Coalition.

Wike urged political stakeholders in the state to put past disagreements behind them and mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu’s second-term ambition.

He noted that a strong electoral performance would improve Rivers State’s prospects for federal appointments, infrastructure projects and greater political influence.

“All I want to hear in this state is Tinubu and nothing but Tinubu,” Wike said.

He declared that Rivers must position itself strategically to maximise the benefits of its relationship with the federal government.

He argued that delivering a high number of votes for Tinubu in 2027 would strengthen the state’s bargaining power at the national level and create more opportunities for its people, particularly young people.

According to the FCT minister, the political calculations surrounding the next general election should be driven by the long-term interests of Rivers State rather than lingering personal grievances.

“I am not going to be governor again; this is for your own interest. I want this state to grow. I want this state to play an important role in the politics of Nigeria,” he said.

Wike also pointed to federal appointments and infrastructure projects, including the Bonny road, as evidence of the benefits of maintaining a productive relationship with the Tinubu administration.

He called on grassroots political leaders and youth groups to return to their respective local government areas, reconcile aggrieved members and prepare for the establishment of campaign committees ahead of the elections and the president’s anticipated visit to the state.

Speaking on behalf of Fubara’s supporters, former Port Harcourt Mayor, Ezebunwo Ichemati, declared the group’s willingness to work with Wike and other members of the Rainbow Coalition to deliver Tinubu and the coalition’s candidates in the forthcoming elections.

He described the meeting as a turning point in the state’s political landscape, suggesting that the engagement could mark a shift from the prolonged rivalry between the Wike and Fubara camps towards cooperation ahead of 2027.

He said Fubara was aware of and supported the meeting, presenting the engagement as part of a broader reconciliation process involving the two political camps.

World.title: Mining Licence Dispute: Alake’s Aide Challenges UK Report on Blair’s Nigeria Role
World.content:
Folalumi Alaran in Abuja

Special Adviser to the Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Kehinde Bamigbetan, has challenged a British newspaper report questioning former UK Prime Minister Tony Blair’s role in advising Nigeria, arguing the allegations surrounding a mining licence dispute contradict available regulatory records.

Bamigbetan, in a rejoinder to an article published by The Telegraph on October 18, 2026, disputed claims concerning mining company Jupiter and its partners, Basin Mining Limited and Range Mining Limited, insisting the companies lost their licences for failing to pay statutory annual service fees.

He said Basin Mining Limited owed N1.223 billion in outstanding fees, adding that the Nigerian Mining Cadastre Office had issued several notices before the licences were revoked.

He also said legal proceedings to recover the outstanding amounts were underway.

The presidential aide argued that the dispute should be resolved through the appropriate legal process rather than through international publicity, while questioning the basis of allegations that Nigeria’s engagement with the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change could undermine British national security interests.

According to him, the institute and the federal government had denied the suggestion that it held a contract to advise the Nigerian government.

Bamigbetan traced the dispute to reforms introduced by the Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, following his appointment in August 2023, saying the administration had prioritised compliance with the Nigerian Minerals and Mining Act 2007.

He said the ministry revoked at least 1,663 mining licences in November 2023 over regulatory defaults and subsequently provided a three-month window for affected operators to present complaints and seek redress.

The aide alleged that Steve Davis, whom he identified as Jupiter’s promoter, had mounted an international campaign against the federal government following the revocations.

He maintained the companies concerned should meet their statutory obligations or pursue their grievances through the established legal channels.

World.title: Food Security: 235,567 Farmers Benefit as Kwara Gov Flags-off Distribution of Inputs, Support
World.content:
Hammed Shittu in Ilorin





Governor Alhaji AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq of Kwara State on Monday launched the distribution of additional 49,337 agricultural inputs, productive assets and processing equipment for local farmers and vulnerable households in the state.

The gesture according to the governor would go a long way at boosting food security for the residents of the state.

Implemented under FADAMA CARES 2.0, the programme is powered by the World Bank-supported Nigeria Community Action for Resilience and Economic Stimulus (NG-CARES).

At least 186,230 people had earlier benefitted from the initiative. When added to the newly launched 49,337, that brings the total beneficiaries to

235,567.

The governor who stated this in Ilorin while performing the flag-off said farmers are facing some challenges, thereby needing regular support to lessen their losses and earn more.

His words: “I welcome you to this flag of the Kwara FADAMA programme. Our farmers face costly inputs, unpredictable weather, limited equipment, the difficulties of moving and processing produce. Our duty is to remove these barriers and obstacles so that their labor pays.”

AbdulRazaq stated that, “This programme has reached 186,230 beneficiaries. Of this, 54,332 received inputs and services, and 131,898 received productive and processing assets across 10 value chains.

“These figures represent farmers, processors, and families earning better livelihood.

“The phase of the flag-off today will support 49,337 beneficiaries, including true group assets. It provides rice, maize, soyabeans inputs. It also provides equipment ranging from sprayers, water pumps, and power tillers to rice mills.

“We also have cassava processors, fish smoking plants, and commercial boats. This programme will reach a total of 235,556 beneficiaries.

“Our goal is to help farmers produce more, lose less, process better, reach wider markets, and earn more with opportunities for women and young people.”

He congratulated prospective beneficiaries and enjoined them to see the inputs and assets as investment opportunities and not as handouts.

He also acknowledged the active roles played by different stakeholders to make the programme a huge success.

Commissioner for Livestock who is supervising the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, Hon. Olohuntoyosi Thomas, said the government has deployed 48 tractors and two D&R caterpillar bulldozers to drive farming activities and expand agricultural mechanization across the 16 local governments.

Thomas said at least 2,016 state farmers were provided with 8,064 bags of NPK fertilizer through the Federal Government’s Renewed Hope Farm Input Support Programme.

She appreciated all key stakeholders whose contributions have developed the sector, including development partners, public-private investors, farmers’ associations, and traditional institutions.

Commissioner for Finance and Chairman State NG-CARES Steering Committee, Dr. Hauwa Nuru, said Kwara is one of the leading states in delivery and reimbursement, adding the initiative reflects the commitment of the administration to empowering farmers, improving their livelihoods, ensuring food security, and promoting sustainable economic growth.

State Project Coordinator, FADAMA NG-CARES, Dr Busari Toyin Isiaka, explained that FADAMA CARES 2.0 is the agricultural component of NG-CARES, supported by the World Bank through additional financing, adding that its purpose is to improve agricultural production, reduce losses, enhance food security and strengthen beneficiaries’ incomes.

Busari listed items for distribution as rice, maize and soybean inputs, relevant production inputs rather than seeds alone, productive and processing assets such as knapsack sprayers, water pumps, power tillers, grinding machines, rice mills, cassava processing equipment, fish smoking kilns and commercial boats.

State Chairman for the Federated FADAMA Community Association (FFCA), Alhaji Isiaka Yakub Falala, appreciated Governor AbdulRazaq for the administration’s commitment to turning around the agricultural sector and his various support for farmers in the state.

World.title: NO BAIL | Shadrack Sibiya dealt crushing court blow
World.content:
Former deputy national police commissioner Shadrack Sibiya will remain behind bars after the Randburg Magistrate's Court denied him bail on Tuesday, 20 October. Image: X

Former deputy national police commissioner Shadrack Sibiya will remain behind bars after the Randburg Magistrate’s Court denied his bail application on Tuesday, 20 October.

The 59-year-old faces serious charges, including rape, sexual grooming and human trafficking.

Magistrate Hleziphi Mkhasibe ruled that Sibiya failed to prove exceptional circumstances justifying his release.



COURT DENIES SHADRACK SIBIYA BAIL

Mkhasibe raised concerns about alleged witness intimidation and the destruction of evidence during her ruling.

“The finding of the court is that the applicant failed to show exceptional circumstances that permit the applicant’s release on bail. As a result, bail is refused,” she said.

WATCH | NPA spokesperson Kaizer Kganyago says the outcome of Shadrack Sibiya's bail application is in line with what the prosecution had sought, adding that the State is ready to proceed should there be an appeal or as the matter moves toward trial. pic.twitter.com/oKQgZU7oHZ — SABC News (@SABCNews) October 20, 2026

The magistrate also referred to allegations that Sibiya threatened the family of a 16-year-old girl he is accused of sexually grooming.

The State argued that releasing the former police boss could place witnesses at risk and compromise the investigation.

The court found that Sibiya’s alleged conduct raised concerns about possible interference with evidence.



“There is no bail condition that can be imposed to ensure that he complies,” the court said.

R20 000 BAIL OFFER FAILS

Sibiya’s legal team had proposed bail of R20 000, arguing that strict conditions could address the State’s concerns.

His lawyer, advocate Estelle Kilian SC, also offered to surrender his passport and ensure he had no contact with witnesses.

However, the court rejected the proposal.

The ruling followed three weeks of arguments during which prosecutors presented evidence relating to the alleged offences.

Sibiya is accused of raping an 18-year-old woman at a Sandton hotel and sexually grooming a 16-year-old girl.

He has denied the allegations, maintaining that his sexual encounter with the older complainant was consensual.

The former general also faces a firearm-related charge arising from his arrest.

WHEN WILL SIBIYA RETURN TO COURT?

Sibiya, who was arrested on 21 September, remains detained at the Kgosi Mampuru II Correctional Centre in Pretoria.

He resigned from the South African Police Service on 12 October amid disciplinary proceedings.

His criminal case has been postponed to 24 November 2026 for further investigations.

Sibiya remains presumed innocent until proven guilty.

World.title: Siwelele FC demote Lehlohonolo Seema, release Willem Jackson
World.content:
Siwelele FC have decided to retain the services of coach Lehlohonolo Seema who had been suspended by the management.

Seema was suspended alongside his then assistant Willem Jackson following the team’s 3-1 loss to Kaizer Chiefs on 6 September.

Siwelele then roped in the legendary Godfrey Mosoetsa on interim basis, and he has been in charge since then.



Now, addressing Siwelele fans in Sunday’s general meeting, club boss Calvin Le John, said Seema is still part of the club.

The former Lesotho and Orlando Pirates captain had been with the Siwelele first team since the purchase of the SuperSport United status.

He helped Siwelele avoid relegation last season but the team failed to take off this term but that can be attributed to the number of good players they sold.

SEEMA RETURNS TO SIWELELE AS DDC HEAD COACH

“He’s still part of us. Some people will say we have demoted him. He will be our new coach for the DDC, and he will continue,” said Le John as per FARPost.

WILL SEEMA EVER RETURN TO HIS PREVIOUS ROLE AT THE CLUB?

World.title: Rudi Stevens: The GBV workshop speaker at the centre of an assault video row
World.content:
The DA is standing by its ward 108 candidate, Rudi Stevens, after a video from his past resurfaced. Image: Instagram @foreveryenanewspaper

Rudi Stevens is the Democratic Alliance’s (DA’s) candidate for ward 108 in Cape Town.

But weeks before the local government elections, a video from his past has resurfaced.

It appears to show him assaulting his then wife.

Now, critics are demanding answers, while the DA says it believes in second chances.



The video began circulating on social media ahead of the 4 November local government elections.

The South African has seen the video. It appears to show Stevens assaulting his then wife.

It’s understood the video was recorded about five years ago.



The couple have since divorced, and a case opened against Stevens at the time was later withdrawn.

Ward 108 includes Sunbird Park in Kuils River.

WHO IS RUDI STEVENS?

Stevens describes himself as a community leader and a member of the local Residents and Ratepayers Association.



He also identifies himself as an advocate for families affected by gender-based violence and femicide (GBVF).

WHAT THE DA SAYS

DA Cape Town metro chairperson and City of Cape Town mayoral committee member for safety and security JP Smith has defended Stevens.

“What he did is deplorable, but he has turned his life around and has devoted the last five years to campaigning for women’s rights,” Smith told the Weekend Argus.



“The DA believes in second chances and that people can be redeemed.”

Smith pointed to Stevens’s work over the past five years as an emergency responder, community volunteer, first-aid trainer and anti-GBV campaigner.

WHAT STEVENS SAYS

Stevens hasn’t yet commented publicly.



His spokesperson didn’t respond to the Weekend Argus‘s questions by the time of publication, but said a statement would be issued.

Stevens’s former wife declined to comment.

CRITICS DEMAND ANSWERS

Some community leaders have questioned how the DA vetted Stevens as a candidate.



Wendy Williams, of non-profit organisation Roots Community Outreach, said second chances matter, but aren’t the same as public accountability.

“People can change, and second chances matter. But legal eligibility, rehabilitation and public accountability are not the same thing,” she said.

She called on the DA to explain what due diligence it carried out, and whether it assessed the footage before selecting Stevens.



Former City of Cape Town councillor Grant Pascoe also criticised the party’s response.

“A withdrawn case does not prove that an assault never happened,” Pascoe said.

He called for an independent investigation into why the DA continues to support Stevens’s candidacy.



Posters calling on Smith to respond have also circulated on social media.

A WORKSHOP ON MEN’S UPLIFTMENT

The video surfaced days before Stevens was due to give a keynote address at a men’s upliftment workshop in Sunbird Park on Wednesday, 21 October.

Let us know in the comments below…

World.title: OFFICIAL: Sundowns announce another new signing
World.content:
Mamelodi Sundowns have officially announced the signing of Amajita captain Lazola Maku.

Maku joins the Brazilians on a free transfer as he was not attached to any team following his release from Siwelele FC at the end of last season.

Just last week, reports of Maku heading to Chloorkop made headlines in the media, and they have finally proved to be true.



The 19-year-old utility player had trials in Austria upon his release in an attempt to find a home for the current campaign.

However, he was unsuccessful, but he received a career lifeline when Raymond Mdaka included him in the Amajita squad for the U20 COSAFA tournament which South Africa recently won.

Having impressed during the tournament, the Sundowns scouting department recommended that he gets signed.



And Maku has now officially signed on a dotted line in what is believed to be a long-term contract with the African champions.

SUNDOWNS UNVEIL LAZOLA MAKU IN STYLE

𝐋𝐀𝐙𝐎𝐋𝐀 𝐌𝐀𝐊𝐔 𝐉𝐎𝐈𝐍𝐒 𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐘𝐄𝐋𝐋𝐎𝐖 𝐅𝐀𝐌𝐈𝐋𝐘 💛



New colours, new chapter, same ambition. Welcome to Bafana Ba Style, Lazola! 🔥#Sundowns #WelcomeLazola pic.twitter.com/LuzG9vb6u3 — Mamelodi Sundowns FC (@Masandawana) October 20, 2026

MAKU A LONG-TERM MIDFIELD SOLUTION FOR THE BRAZILIANS

At 19, Maku still has a bright and a promising future ahead of him, and he is seen as a long-term solution for Sundowns in that defensive midfield position.



The likes of Teboho Mokoena and Bathusi Aubaas are ageing, and Sundowns would need younger players to slowly take the baton from them.

As reported by The South African last week, the Tshwane giants are also expected to announce the signing of another midfield anchor Jhegson Mendez in January.

The 29-year-old Ecuador international is far more experienced than Maku but he cannot be a long-term solution for the club.

World.title: Ex-Kaizer Chiefs striker ties the knot with Zimbabwean football executive
World.content:
Former Kaizer Chiefs and SuperSport United striker Kingston Nkhatha has reportedly tied the knot, bringing the Zimbabwean footballer into the spotlight for a milestone away from the football pitch.

Nkhatha, who spent two-and-a-half seasons with the Soweto giants, is best remembered by South African football supporters for his time in the Premier Soccer League (PSL), where he also represented SuperSport United.

The wedding confirmation

Zimbabwean sports broadcaster Yvonne Tendai Mangunda confirmed the wedding in a social media post, revealing that she was among the guests at the ceremony.



“Today I am at Kwekwe United CEO Bridgette Mudhosi and former Zimbabwe, Kaizer Chiefs and Supersport forward Kingston Nkhatha’s wedding. A lovely all black affair,” Mangunda wrote.

She also revealed that she had missed Mudhosi’s bridal shower the previous weekend while visiting Claire, but made sure to attend the wedding.

The Herald also described Kingston Nkhatha and Bridget Mudhosi as a “football couple” in a social media post confirming their marriage.

“Football couple……Former Kaizer Chiefs and Dynamos player Kingston Nkhatha tied the knot with Central Region Soccer League side Kwekwe United president Bridget Mudhosi over the weekend,” the publication posted.

The description reflects the couple’s links to Zimbabwean football, with Nkhatha having played for clubs including Kaizer Chiefs, SperSport United and Dynamos, while Mudhosi serves as president of Kwekwe United.

Nkhatha’s Kaizer Chiefs journey

Nkhatha joined Kaizer Chiefs from Black Leopards in July 2012 after the two clubs reached an agreement over his transfer.



According to an announcement published on the club’s official website, the Zimbabwean forward signed a three-year deal with Amakhosi.

His arrival marked an important step in a career that had seen him play for several clubs in Zimbabwe and South Africa.

Before joining Chiefs, Nkhatha had featured for Free State Stars, Carara Kicks and Black Leopards in South Africa.

The striker made his league debut for Chiefs in August 2012, scoring in a 6-0 victory over AmaZulu, according to his career record.

Why Nkhatha left Amakhosi

In January 2015, Chiefs confirmed that Nkhatha had been released early after agreeing to join SuperSport United.

The club’s football manager, Bobby Motaung, thanked the striker for his contribution and wished him well for the future.

Nkhatha had initially been expected to leave when his contract expired later that year, but an agreement between the two clubs allowed him to make the move during the January transfer window.

His departure ended a spell of approximately two-and-a-half years with the Soweto outfit.

He subsequently continued his career with SuperSport United before returning to Zimbabwean football.

World.title: Beyond SASSA grant: How Stokvels and community HELP
World.content:
Did you know there are a number of community-based schemes to help the elderly besides a SASSA grant? Image: File

For many South African pensioners, their SASSA grant is no longer enough, even when it’s augmented by a personal nest egg. As we know, October 2026 passed without a grant top-up, and yet the cost of living just keeps on rising.

Therefore, the old-age SASSA grant sits at R2 400 a month for 60 to 74s. And R2 420 for 75 and older. And don’t hold your breath for Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana to reveal anything concrete about 2027 increases in this week’s MTBPS either …

SASSA GRANT SHRINKING

Unfortunately, Eskom pushed up prices by 8.76% back in April. And municipal customers got a 9.01% hike in July. Plus, a further 8.83% is approved for April 2027. Fuel is dearer, too, with diesel going from R17 to R33 per litre since the National Treasury’s last Budget Speech. So, if you receive a SASSA grant, how exactly are you expected to make a fixed income stretch?



While difficult, the answer is sitting in plain sight. Stokvels started as a way to support communities that banks overlooked, and many are still run by community elders, generally women. The numbers show their scale: an estimated 800 000 groups exist, with 11.5 million members, saving around R50 billion a year. These are the main types of stokvels:

Burial: Members contribute monthly so that a funeral is covered when it happens.

Members contribute monthly so that a funeral is covered when it happens. Grocery: Members pool money and spend it in bulk at year-end, often at wholesalers that offer discounts.

Members pool money and spend it in bulk at year-end, often at wholesalers that offer discounts. Savings: This is a fixed monthly contribution, paid out in turn or on a set date.

The social side of stokvels matters, too. Members check on each other regularly, and someone will notice if you’re battling.

OTHER SUPPORT SYSTEMS BEYOND A SASSA GRANT

The care and support of community is often just as valuable as money. Image: File

Don’t forget that if you’re on a SASSA grant, you probably also qualify for a municipal rebate. Johannesburg pensioners already receiving rates rebates have are covered till 30 June 2027. Cape Town residents have until 30 November 2026 before their next renewal.



Then there are indigent benefits. All municipalities offer discount electricity, water and refuse collection for households that meet a low-income threshold. Rules and figures differ by province, so, contact your local municipality.

SASSA GRANT: WHO QUALIFIES IN 2026

The South African Social Security Agency means test still decides who gets paid a SASSA grant:

Income: R112 200 a year ( R9 350 a month) if single, R224 400 ( R18 700 a month) if married.

a year ( a month) if single, ( a month) if married. Assets: R1 584 000 if single, R3 168 000 if married.

As ever, when applying for a SASSA grant, be careful that large lump-sum payouts and savings don’t show up in your bank account to be counted against your means test.



Also, do your due diligence before backing a stokvel. Not every single one is safe. We’ve received reports that some burial societies run into liquidity trouble. So, at the very least ask where your group’s money is kept. Also checking whether a group is registered with the National Stokvel Association of South Africa (NASASA) is a sensible start.

But what do you think? Is there enough support for the SASSA grant through community schemes like stokvels? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: Former SAPS general arrested in ammunition scandal
World.content:
A former SAPS general has been arrested after police discovered more than 100 rounds of SAPS-issued ammunition during a raid at his Centurion home. Image: Pexels

A 57-year-old former South African Police Service (SAPS) general has been arrested after investigators discovered more than 100 rounds of police-issued ammunition at his Centurion home.

The arrest follows a raid linked to the murder investigation of former deputy national police commissioner Lieutenant-General Sindile Mfazi.

SAPS confirmed the arrest on Tuesday, 20 October 2026.



FORMER SAPS GENERAL ARRESTED AFTER CENTURION RAID

According to SAPS, members of the National Cold Case Unit searched the former general’s home on 6 July 2026.

Investigators seized more than 100 rounds of SAPS-issued ammunition, including R5 and 9mm rounds.

They also confiscated documents and electronic devices believed to be relevant to Mfazi’s murder investigation.



In a statement, national police spokesperson Brigadier Athlenda Mathe, SAPS said the suspect had left the police service more than 17 years ago.

“The former general left the SAPS in 2009, and there are no valid reasons for his possession of the SAPS-issued ammunition,” police said.

The former general now faces a charge of unlawful possession of ammunition in contravention of the Firearms Control Act 60 of 2000.



Police have withheld his identity ahead of his first court appearance.

MFAZI MURDER INVESTIGATION TAKES NEW TURN

The arrest comes as detectives continue investigating the death of Mfazi, who died in July 2021.

His death was initially attributed to COVID-19 complications before investigators uncovered evidence that prompted a murder investigation.



In July 2026, Mathe confirmed that investigators had changed the nature of the case following further investigations.

“We can confirm the case was changed from being registered as an inquest docket to a murder docket,” Mathe said at the time.

She also revealed that examinations conducted after Mfazi’s body was exhumed had detected a poisonous substance.



“The team had to determine whether it was accidentally ingested or whether there was an intention to kill him. After the gathering of evidence and information, the team is quite confident they are investigating a murder case,” Mathe said.

The National Cold Case Unit has since conducted several operations as part of the investigation.

FORMER TOP COP TO APPEAR IN COURT

The 57-year-old suspect is expected to appear before the Johannesburg Magistrate’s Court on Tuesday.



SAPS has not indicated whether he faces additional charges or whether the ammunition discovery is directly connected to Mfazi’s death.

The former general has not been charged with Mfazi’s murder.

Police have also not disclosed whether further arrests are expected.

World.title: RIP | Laerskool Totius boy, 8, dies in tragic accident
World.content:
Eight-year-old Nero van Niekerk, a Grade 2 learner at Laerskool Totius in Bellville, died following a tragic accident on Friday, 16 October. Image: Facebook/Laerskool Totius

An eight-year-old Grade 2 learner from Laerskool Totius in Bellville, Cape Town, has died following a tragic accident, leaving his school community in mourning.

Nero van Niekerk died on Friday, 16 October, just three months after celebrating his eighth birthday.

The school broke the news on Facebook on Sunday, prompting an outpouring of condolences from teachers, parents and community members.



LAERSKOOL TOTIUS CONFIRMS LEARNER’S DEATH

Laerskool Totius, in Bellville’s Boston suburb, shared a memorial tribute to Nero, who was born on 17 July 2018.

The school expressed its heartbreak and extended condolences to his family, friends and classmates.

It also called on the community to keep Nero’s loved ones in their prayers.

However, the school did not disclose the circumstances surrounding the accident.

TEACHER’S HEARTBREAKING FINAL MESSAGE

Nero’s teacher, Madeleine van Zyl, shared an emotional farewell in the comments.

“Juffrou gaan jou baie mis, jy het diep spore in my hart getrap,” she wrote.



The message translates to: “Teacher will miss you so much. You left deep footprints in my heart.”

Van Zyl also remembered Nero as a mischievous little boy and offered her condolences to his grieving family.

Her message drew attention as parents and community members reacted to the young learner’s sudden death.

‘TOO MANY YOUNG CHILDREN ARE DYING’

The school’s announcement sparked an emotional response on Facebook.

Anzel Strydom expressed her sadness over the death. “My hart kry so seer,” she wrote, meaning: “My heart aches so much.”

Another commenter, Bramie Lubbe, wrote: “Te veel jong kinders sterf.” This translates to: “Too many young children are dying.”

Others sent messages of strength and comfort to Nero’s family and the school.

WHAT CAUSED NERO VAN NIEKERK’S DEATH?

Laerskool Totius has confirmed that Nero died following an accident but has not revealed where it happened or what led to his death.

The school has not released further details about the incident.

The circumstances surrounding the eight-year-old’s death therefore remain unclear.

World.title: LIVESTREAM | AKA and Tibz murder trial continues
World.content:
DURBAN - The murder trial of rapper Kiernan "AKA" Forbes and his friend Tebello "Tibz" Motsoane continues in the Durban High Court.

On Monday, a ballistics expert linked empty bullet casings from two shootings to the same firearm in the AKA and Tibz murder trial.

The expert was testifying at the trial of the seven men accused of murdering the rapper and his friend.

World.title: Shadrack Sibiya denied bail
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Former deputy national police commissioner Shadrack Sibiya has been denied bail.

The 59-year-old former police official appeared in the Randburg Magistrate’s Court on Tuesday, where he faces charges of sexual grooming, human trafficking and the reckless handling of a firearm.

He is accused of raping an 18-year-old woman and sexually grooming a 16-year-old girl.

According to the allegations, Sibiya gave the 18-year-old woman alcohol before she lost consciousness and was raped at a hotel in Sandton.

The State opposed his release on bail, arguing that he could interfere with witnesses or flee the country.

READ | Sibiya rape accuser fears for her safety if he is granted bail

Delivering the bail judgment, Magistrate Hleziphi Mkhasibe agreed with the State that Sibiya posed a threat to witnesses.

“The court has carefully balanced the applicant’s constitutional right, his personal circumstances, the presumption of innocence and the interests of justice. The finding of the court is that the applicant failed to show exceptional circumstances that permit his release on bail,” Mkhasibe said.

She added that there was evidence suggesting Sibiya would go to great lengths to conceal evidence against him, including allegations that he had disposed of cellphone evidence.

“He was aware that his cellular phones were being intercepted. The applicant’s behaviour demonstrates that the accused is likely to tamper with evidence. There is no bail condition that can be imposed to ensure that he complies,” the court said.

World.title: Police assess readiness ahead of local government elections
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Police have begun assessing election readiness in Gauteng as preparations ramp up for the upcoming local government elections.

National Police Commissioner Fannie Masemola says police are confident they can ensure a safe and peaceful election, while urging political parties and campaigners to exercise patience and respect everyone’s democratic right to campaign.

"All other provinces will follow, and we'll be able to measure how ready we are but indeed I know there has been a lot of preparation around this," he said.

"We are and will be in a position to deliver or to make sure that the elections take place in an environment that is conducive to a free and fair election."

World.title: Lula or Bolsonaro's son? Brazil makes a final choice
World.content:
RIO DE JANEIRO - A presidential runoff between Brazil's incumbent leader Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and his right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro will decide the fate of Latin America's largest democracy on Sunday.

Lula, on the cusp of 81 and seeking a fourth non-consecutive term, is facing stiff competition from the 45-year-old senator, who is the son of jailed ex-leader Jair Bolsonaro.

Flavio Bolsonaro defied expectations by nabbing 47 percent of the first-round vote over Lula's 45 percent in early October.

The runoff victor will either preserve the vast country of 214 million people as a left-wing stronghold in Latin America, or usher it into the ranks of right-wing administrations loyal to US President Donald Trump.

Trump has not yet explicitly endorsed Flavio Bolsonaro, but the White House has loomed large over a bitterly divisive election campaign.

Lula's political party has accused US tech giant Meta of election "interference" by allegedly restricting the incumbent's WhatsApp and Instagram content.

The company has denied doing anything to favour either side, but previously said that some of Lula's campaign ads had been mistakenly deactivated due to technical errors not isolated to Brazil.

That controversy is unfolding amid a campaign that has largely played out on social media, a realm typically dominated by the political right.

But Brazilian leftists are upping their game, and Lula has begun appealing to voters via front-facing despite not owning his own cell phone.

- 'The right to dream' -

A recent Datafolha institute poll gave Bolsonaro 51 percent of voting intentions compared with 49 percent for Lula, placing the pair in a technical tie given the margin of error.

Polls had underestimated the scale of support for the right-wing candidate ahead of the first round, however.

"Brazil is going to retire you," Flavio Bolsonaro hurled at his rival during a heated televised debate riddled with low blows on Sunday night.

He pledged to restore "hope and the right to dream" during a rally in the northern Amazonian state of Para on Monday.

The senator has campaigned on promises to improve purchasing power and tackle insecurity -- two huge concerns among Brazil's roughly 160 million registered voters.

"Today, the situation is difficult, with the government raising taxes on those who work to feed the welfare dependency of low-income people," civil servant Geneci Bispo, 58, told AFP at a Sao Paulo rally on Sunday.

Flavio Bolsonaro has also railed against corruption on the campaign trail, honing in on Lula's previous conviction which was later annulled.

The senator himself is under investigation for corruption over the funding of a biopic about his father, partly financed by a banker embroiled in one of the biggest financial scandals in Brazilian history.

- Democracy a 'fragile thing' -

The shock result of the first round appears to have invigorated the left, with Lula's camp staging massive rallies ever since.

"I want to thank the Brazilian people who took to the streets to ensure the continuity of democracy in this country," the president said.

Jair Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year prison sentence under house arrest for attempting a coup following his electoral defeat to Lula in 2022.

Flavio Bolsonaro has sworn to liberate his father if elected.

"Democracy is a very precious and fragile thing," said marketing professional Camila Hassen, 35, at a leftist protest in Rio de Janeiro on Sunday.

Lula has passed a series of social measures at the eleventh hour in a bid to turn things around for his camp.

His administration last month announced an increase to Bolsa Familia, Lula's flagship allowance for poor families, which came into effect this week.

The veteran politician also scored an important win by getting parliamentary approval of a reduction in working hours, an extremely popular measure that even Flavio Bolsonaro supported.

World.title: Japan probe on its way to Mars moon
World.content:
TOKYO - A Japanese spacecraft was on its way to one of Mars's moons on Tuesday on a world-first mission to retrieve samples, potentially helping unlock the origins of the Solar System and life on Earth.

The flagship H3 rocket carrying the unmanned Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) probe blasted off into a pitch-black sky from the Tanegashima Space Center at 4:41 am (1941 GMT Monday), according to a live stream broadcast by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency.

Over an hour later, JAXA announced via the live broadcast that the probe had successfully separated from the H3 and was "beginning its journey toward the Martian system".

"I'd dreamt of this day, so I'm incredibly happy," said JAXA scientist Mari Aida. "Right now I feel really relieved."

Following the separation, JAXA said it received signals from the spacecraft as expected, confirming it was operating normally.

Despite the early hour in Japan, thousands of people tuned into the live stream, posting messages of encouragement.

The spacecraft is due to arrive near Mars around August next year, where it will orbit one of its moons, Phobos.

A French-German rover dubbed IDEFIX -- the French name for the comic hero Asterix's dog -- will be the first vehicle to travel across Phobos, conducting surface observations aimed at ensuring a safe landing.

Once MMX arrives on Phobos, it will collect at least 10 grams (0.35 ounces) of material from the surface during its planned three years in the Red Planet's vicinity.

The mission -- which aims to be the first round trip to the Martian region -- is a collaboration with US and European space agencies, as well as numerous universities and tech companies.

- 'Paradigm-shifting science'-

Scientists hope it will help lay the groundwork for eventual human exploration.

"The samples from MMX will bring forth paradigm-shifting science on the Mars system for generations to come, especially as NASA prepares to send the first humans to Mars," Nicky Fox, administrator of NASA's Science Mission Directorate, said in a message broadcast on the JAXA live stream.

JAXA hopes the mission will reveal how Mars and its two moons formed, a key piece of knowledge in working out how the Solar System was born.

One theory for the origin of the moons -- the "giant impact" hypothesis -- is that they formed after a celestial body collided with Mars.

The "capture" hypothesis, meanwhile, postulates that the moons are asteroids pulled in by Mars's gravity.

Determining which theory is correct will help reveal "how a habitable environment for life might have arisen on the terrestrial planets", JAXA said, referring to the four rocky worlds closest to the Sun -- Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars.

JAXA said the mission will also explore the possibility of using Phobos as a "natural space station" by establishing the requirements for a round trip -- something "essential for crewed Mars exploration".

It will also observe the planet's other moon, Deimos, although it will not land on it.

US and Chinese space agencies have also been vying to be the first to return rock samples from the surface of Mars back to Earth.

NASA's Perseverance rover, which has been roaming across Mars since 2021, has already collected samples.

The return mission, however, was effectively cancelled by the administration of President Donald Trump following a vote by Congress in January.

China's Tianwen-3 spacecraft is scheduled for launch around 2028 and hopes to return Mars samples to Earth as early as 2031 -- potentially before the Japanese mission's return.

World.title: EU unveils strategy to boost Arctic presence
World.content:
BRUSSELS - The EU is to unveil plans to bolster its foothold in the Arctic as it grapples with pressure from Russia and the United States in the key strategic region.

From critical raw materials to icebreakers and undersea cables, the bloc wants to up its presence in the geopolitical battleground, according to a draft of its new "strategy for the Arctic" seen by AFP.

"The new reality in the Arctic requires Europe to be a strong and reliable partner. That is precisely what we aim to achieve with our new strategy," said Jozef Sikela, the EU's head of international partnerships.

"It addresses the region's most pressing challenges, from accelerating climate change to growing security and geopolitical tensions, and sets out how Europe should respond."

Competition is on the rise in the Arctic as global warming causes sea ice to melt. Countries such as Russia, China and the United States have been ramping up activity, racing to claim natural resources and new maritime routes.

With three Arctic nations among its 27 members -- Denmark, Finland and Sweden -- the European Union has skin in the game.

And President Donald Trump's repeated threats to bring Greenland -- a vast, autonomous Danish territory -- under US control have rattled Europe.

Given that what happens in the far north also has repercussions further south, the strategy, which is to be presented by the EU chief Ursula von der Leyen, aims to set out a common EU approach to the region.

The draft seen by AFP stresses the need to cooperation with "like-minded" non-EU nations, such as Canada, Britain and Norway, and envisages a regular summit of "Northern Neighbourhood" partners.

World.title: Ronaldo handed 30-day suspension after walking out on Portugal
World.content:
LISBON - Cristiano Ronaldo has been handed a 30-day suspension for leaving the Portuguese national team camp, the country's football federation (FPF) announced on Monday.

The 41-year-old abruptly left the Portugal camp on September 30 during the UEFA Nations League, before accusing coach Jorge Jesus of breaking his word about giving him game time.

Ronaldo apologised to supporters earlier in October, adding he would accept any punishment that was imposed.

The former Manchester United and Real Madrid star, who will also have to pay a fine of 255 euros ($286), has received the minimum penalty provided for in the federation's regulations, which stipulate suspensions of between one and six months for leaving the national team.

Ronaldo left Portugal's squad after first being made to warm up as a substitute against Norway on September 27 and not being brought on, and then finding out he would not start against Denmark in the match on October 1.

Ronaldo's suspension takes effect from the day of the Denmark match, meaning he has already served 19 days of his ban and will complete it by the end of October.

The FPF disciplinary committee said it took into account "the remorse shown in the statement" issued by Ronaldo on October 6, in which he admitted his mistake and expressed his willingness to accept a punishment.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner is Portugal's all-time top goalscorer and record appearance-maker in men's international football.

But in his absence, Portugal won all four of their Nations League matches and qualified for the quarter-finals with two games to spare.

Portugal host Denmark on November 14 and then travel to face Wales on November 17 in their final two Nations League Group A4 matches -- by which time Ronaldo will have served his suspension.

- 'Putting in the work' -

In a social media post shortly after his walk-out, Ronaldo accused Portugal boss Jesus of breaking his word about giving him game time in Nations League matches but insisted he was not retiring from international duty.

"I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team," Ronaldo posted.

He said Jesus had gone back on his word about bringing him on against Norway, and then in a press conference before the Denmark match had not said a series of points they had agreed upon during a conversation beforehand.

One of Ronaldo's pre-approved talking points was that Jesus had "made a mistake in asking someone of the stature of Pele or Maradona to warm up and then not sending him on in the match".

Jesus, speaking several days later, said he would select Ronaldo for international duty if the forward was playing for his club Al Nassr, and was interested in being called up.

Following the FPF's announcement, Ronaldo did not directly react to the news on Instagram but did post a picture of himself preparing to train with his Saudi club, accompanied with the caption, "Putting in the work".

World.title: Middle East conflict adds pressure ahead of Mini Budget
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana will table the Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement (MTBPS) on Wednesday, setting out the government’s fiscal outlook and spending plans.

Often referred to as the Mini Budget, the statement provides an update on the state of the economy and the government’s finances. Unlike the February national budget, it does not typically include detailed tax and social grant announcements.

However, economists and market commentators will be watching for indications of whether tax increases could return to the agenda in February 2027.

The conflict in the Middle East has added pressure to the economic outlook, with potential implications for fuel prices, inflation and government finances.

Government has spent R17 billion funding fuel levy relief this year, and Godongwana may face renewed calls to review the levies motorists pay.

Debt will also be in focus. In February, government projected that debt would stabilise at about 75% of gross domestic product (GDP) before beginning to decline.

Why does it matter?

The Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement sets the direction for the fiscal framework ahead of the next national budget.

It gives Parliament and the public an update on National Treasury’s assessment of the economy, government revenue, spending pressures and the country’s debt position.

It also provides an opportunity for Parliament and the public to engage with the government’s fiscal plans months before the next national budget is tabled.

When is it tabled?

The MTBPS is generally presented in October, about four months before the national budget in February.

The national budget is usually tabled after the State of the Nation Address (SONA). The MTBPS follows the Budget Review Recommendations Report process and provides an interim update on government’s fiscal plans.

World.title: From broken promises to high cost of living and failed reforms: The making of Ruto's scorecard
World.content:
Lamu County officials, led by Chief Engineer for Roads and Structural Works David Jomeli, inspect an affordable housing project in Lamu County. [Robert Menza, Standard]

A year after President William Ruto pledged to make Kenya food-secure, 2.7 million people face crisis-level hunger, inflation and the cost-of-living measure has climbed to 6.8 per cent, and key flagship promises remain unfulfilled, a Standard review of his then Mashujaa Day speech shows.

In his October 2025 Mashujaa Day address at Ithookwe Stadium in Kitui County, Ruto outlined an ambitious agenda centred on four pillars.

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.
