World.title: Croatia Lagging Further and Further Behind on Innovation Ranking
World.content:
October the 20th, 2026 – Despite being the home of many successful startups, Croatia keeps on lagging further and further behind on the innovation ranking.

Croatia has unfortunately fallen six places on the Global Innovation Index ranking for 2026 and is now in 46th place among 139 countries. Index reports that the Academic Trade Union warns that such a result is a consequence of the Government’s poor economic and innovation policy, and particularly highlights the weak cooperation between universities and the economy. It is calling for the establishment of a special ministry that would deal with higher education, science and innovation.

According to the latest report of the World Intellectual Property Organisation (WIPO), Croatia was in 40th place last year and this year has fallen to 46th. Of the 39 European economies covered by the research it is in 28th place. The Academic Trade Union considers this to be yet another warning that Croatia must change the way it develops the economy, science and higher education.

croatia is getting further behind european innovation leaders

The Global Innovation Index compares economies according to approximately 80 indicators, among which are investments in research and development, education, technology, the business environment and the application of innovations. Switzerland is in a highly impressive first place for the 16th year in a row, followed by Sweden and the United States of America.

In fourth place came South Korea, fifth Singapore, sixth the United Kingdom, seventh the Netherlands, eighth Finland, ninth Denmark, and tenth China. The Academic Trade Union warns that Croatia lags behind European economies in all the main areas assessed by the index.

croatia has nowhere near enough cooperation between universities and industry

According to the trade union, one of Croatia’s greatest weaknesses is the cooperation between universities and industry, for which they point out that Croatia is only in 84th place. Connecting research with production and entrepreneurship should, they believe, be one of the foundations of economic development. The trade union stresses that for years it has been warning the Croatian Government of the need for better linking of the academic community and the economy, but that its proposals are not being implemented. For these exceptionally poor results, they hold the responsible officials accountable, especially the leadership of the Ministry of Science, Education and Youth. They claim that the responsible persons insufficiently follow the results of international research and do not understand the importance of innovations for the development of the economy.

is a new ministry on the horizon?

The Academic Trade Union proposes the establishment of a Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation. The new ministry, according to their proposal, should coordinate the work of the National Innovation Council and encourage cooperation between universities, scientific institutions and companies. The trade union demands that innovation become the third fundamental task of universities, alongside education and scientific work. It also proposes the adoption of a Law on Innovation that would regulate the financing and functioning of the Croatian innovation system.

could croatia’s investment in r&d ever equal 3% of gdp?

Among the trade union’s proposals is an increase in investment in research and development to 3 percent of Croatian GDP. They also demand a doubling of the number of researchers employed in the economy, especially holders of doctorates, so that Croatia can reduce the lag behind the European Union average. The new ministry should also facilitate the coordination of different state institutions when it comes to innovation, the application of new technologies and their transfer from scientific institutions into the economy. The Academic Trade Union considers that such changes would enable stronger development of industry, increase its contribution to the economy and in the long term contribute to the growth of the standard of living. They called on the government to accept their proposals and change the previous policy of developing science, higher education and innovation.

World.title: Why Your Ancestor’s “Austrian” or “Italian” Passport Doesn’t Mean You Aren’t Legally Croatian
World.content:
October the 19th, 2026 – Croatia hasn’t always been the Croatia we know. You may have ancestors that are listed as being Austrian, Italian or Hungarian, but you might still be legally Croatian.

If you’ve curiously started digging into your family’s emigration history, you have likely unearthed a treasure trove of century-old documents: ship passenger manifests, American or Canadian naturalisation petitions, and faded, yellowed draft cards. However, for a massive segment of the Croatian diaspora, specifically those whose families left Europe during the peak migration waves between the late 1800s and the 1920s, these documents often bring a frustrating surprise.

Under the column labelled “Country of Origin” or “Nationality,” your ancestor’s record might not say “Croatia” at all. Instead, it might explicitly state “Austria,” “Hungary,” “Yugoslavia,” or even “Italy”. For many diaspora members, this feels like an immediate dead end. The common assumption by the mere mortal is as follows: If my great-grandfather left Europe as a citizen of the Austro-Hungarian Empire or the Kingdom of Italy, I must not qualify for Croatian citizenship by descent. Despite this being a common assumption, it’s fortunately totally incorrect. In the eyes of modern citizenship law, an imperial passport from 1910 doesn’t erase your legal right to a modern Croatian passport today. However, proving your lineage across a century of shifting borders requires navigating a complex historical and bureaucratic maze.

roots don’t recognise changing borders, but the ministry of the interior does

To understand why your ancestor’s old paperwork says “Austria” or “Italy,” you have to look at the tumultuous geopolitical history of not only Croatia but the wider region. Before the modern Republic of Croatia declared independence on October the 8th, 1991, the territory was repeatedly carved up, absorbed, and governed by various empires and federations, with a lot of bloodshed in between.

First we need to go all the way back to pre-1918 when Croatia was part of the once mighty Austro-Hungarian Empire. Emigrants from Zagreb, Slavonia, Dalmatia and even the furthest-flung islands all travelled on Austrian or Hungarian documentation. Then came the interwar period & WWII. Following the Treaty of Rapallo in 1920, sections of Istria, Rijeka, Zadar, and several Dalmatian islands (including Cres and Lošinj) were annexed by what was then the Kingdom of Italy. People from these regions suddenly became legal Italian citizens, changed their names to Italian variants, and emigrated under the documentation bearing the Italian flag. Then, from 1945 to 1991, Croatia and the countries of the region became part of the various iterations of Yugoslavia.

You can see how Croatian citizenship applications can often become very confusing territory, but the authorities are fully aware of Croatia’s blurry past and as such even blurrier documentation. When the Croatian Ministry of the Interior evaluates an application for citizenship by descent, they don’t care what a clerk at Ellis Island wrote down way back in 1912. They care about geographic reality that corresponds to modern-day Croatia and historical municipal tracking.

Under the current Croatian Citizenship Act, the key question is whether the specific town or village your ancestor emigrated from sits within the modern, legally recognised borders of Croatia as it is today. If your great-grandfather was born somewhere near Split back in 1905, he was technically born under Austro-Hungarian rule, but because Split is indisputably Croatian territory today, the bloodline connection remains legally valid, long after Austria-Hungary’s demise.

here’s where diy croatian citizenship applications often come to grief…

While the law very much allows for these problematic and complex geographical and historical shifts, the burden of proof rests entirely on the applicant. This is where DIY applications frequently fall apart, stall, and end up shoved to gather dust on a shelf somewhere. If you submit an application to a Croatian consulate with an American death certificate stating your grandfather was born in “Austria,” alongside a modern birth record request, the reviewing officers require a meticulous paper trail that bridges the historical gap. You must prove two things simultaneously in such cases.

The first is what’s known as the registry match. Initially, you need to locate the original historical birth or baptismal record in the local municipal registry or church archive within Croatia, confirming they were registered on that specific territory once upon a time. After you’ve cleared that hurdle, you need to deal witu name and identity reconciliation. What this means is that you need to prove that the “Giovanni” or “Giuseppe” listed on an Italian emigration record from Istria is legally the exact same person as the “Ivan” or “Josip” recorded in the local village archives. You can imagine how difficult this is without administrative help.

If your family came from an area like Istria or Zadar that switched between Italian and Slavic administration, records may be split between different archives, written in different languages (Latin, Italian, or old Croatian scripts), or filed under completely altered surnames.

solving the runaway border problem

Navigating various international treaties, century-old municipal border adjustments, and dual-language archives is a daunting task for anyone working from North America, South America, or Australia. It requires a level of historical expertise and local administrative access that standard translation services or internet databases simply cannot provide. This is where the specialised, ground-level infrastructure put in place by services like Croatian By Descent becomes an invaluable asset for the busy American diaspora.

Instead of letting your application get derailed and shoved to the back of a massive pile by a confusing historical paper trail, their team functions as both legal researchers and archival detectives. They know exactly how to trace your mysterious, multi-national ancestors through the shifting territorial registries, cross-referencing old land records and municipal books to establish an airtight geographic proof for the Ministry of the Interior. They dismantle Croatia’s age-old runaway border problem by making sure your ancestral files are organised, properly reconciled, and professionally translated, transforming deeply confusing geopolitical hurdle into a successful, legally sound submission package.

Skip the administrative confusion and verify your historical eligibility with the expert team at Croatian By Descent, who can make sure changing borders and complicated political histories don’t come between you and your EU passport. This service uses knowledgeable lawyer partners who can readily assist clients with obtaining their family’s records from Croatia, as well as dealing with them after the fact throughout the process.

World.title: Croatia Has Been Unable to Connect Istrian Railway for 150 Years
World.content:
October the 19th, 2026 – The Austro-Hungarians constructed the Istrian railway in just 3 years, but Croatia has been totally unable to connect it for 150!

Istria is the only Croatian region from which trains don’t actually run into the rest of Croatia. Although trains have been running across the peninsula for 150 years, a direct connection of the Istrian railways with the Croatian railway system is only now being planned. Dubravko Grakalic reports for Index that the Istrian railways are connected, primarily because of geography, to the neighbouring Slovenian ones – a project from the 19th century and the era of Austro-Hungarian rule. Back in 1867, when the line was opened to traffic, Emperor and King Franz Joseph I arrived in Pula by train via Slovenia. To this day, Istrian railway destinations are still reached in the same way.

From Zagreb to Pula by train, via Ljubljana, one travels only at weekends. The train departs on Friday and after a seven-hour journey arrives at Pula station. From Pula back to Zagreb it returns only on Sunday. Passengers are also offered transport by train to Lupoglav, then by bus to the Rijeka–Zagreb line. The paradox of the Istrian railways, which today mainly serve freight traffic and local travel to Buzet, has an interesting historical and political context.

austria-hungary’s railway construction

“The railway in Istria was built back in 1876, with the line from the direction of Divača in Slovenia to Pula 122 kilometres long and a branch line 21 kilometres long from Kanfanar to Rovinj, which until that time had been the strongest economic centre of Istria. Although the Istrian population had wanted a railway earlier, because of other interests in the centre of the state in Vienna, whose primary goal was the construction of the line to the main maritime port of the monarchy in Trieste, completed in 1857, the construction of the railway in Istria was of secondary importance,” Dr. Sc. Josip Kajinić, curator of the Croatian Railway Museum of HŽ Infrastruktura and one of the authors of the recent exhibition on the railway in Istria, told Index.

“Circumstances changed as a result of foreign-policy circumstances that led to the construction of the monarchy’s main naval base in Pula in 1853, alongside which a shipyard was also launched. In those new circumstances the monarchy needed a safe and good transport link for the delivery of raw materials and military equipment, and given the poor and sparse road network and the danger from the sea for maritime traffic that threatened from the Kingdom of Italy after its unification, the decision was finally taken to build a railway line in Istria.

The line to Pula was built because of the naval base and the shipyard, and its branch to Rovinj for economic reasons. Because of the already mentioned danger that threatened from the sea, the Istrian railway was built through the interior,” Dr. Kajinić notes. The Istrianer Staatsbahn, as the railway through Istria was called in Austria-Hungary, was built at state expense. The law on it was passed on 22 April 1873, while the 122-kilometre line was built in less than three years by the company Frolich from Graz. Work began in Pazin in December 1873, and some twenty thousand workers worked on it. The cost was lower than planned – 12,760,469 florins. The line was solemnly opened in August 1876, and regular traffic started the same year in September.

By way of comparison, HŽ Infrastruktura began in 2025 the reconstruction of fifty kilometres of the line from the state border to Sv. Petar u Šumi. The plan is for the reconstruction to be completed by the end of 2028. Austria-Hungary built thirteen railway stations, five bridges and the Hum tunnel on the Istrian line.

the development of the line

In 1878 a track was built on the Pula waterfront, from the station to the shipyard. A more interesting line was built in 1887, a twenty-kilometre stretch from the Slovenian Hrpelje via Kozina to Trieste, which shortened the journey between Pula and Trieste. It operated until 1959 and is now an arranged cycling route. A similar fate befell the route of the narrow-gauge railway Poreč–Trieste, known as the Parenzana, Porečanka or Istranka.

“The former 123-kilometre-long narrow-gauge Parenzana line connected Trieste and Poreč, and for a length of 78 kilometres it passed through Croatian areas of Istria. It was built in 1902 and was in use until 1935. Its route is very well preserved and is today used for tourist purposes,” Josip Kajinić adds. The cycling and walking path is called the “Path of Health and Friendship” because it connects three countries.

from the former yugoslavia to the modern day

After the collapse of the once mighty Austria-Hungary, the first extension of the Istrian railways was launched by the then Yugoslavia with the construction of the Lupoglav–Štalije line in 1951. With it the railway was brought to the port in Raša Bay. The Kanfanar–Rovinj line was suspended in 1966 because of the developed road traffic.

“Throughout history the railway in Istria was managed by several administrations – from the Austrian, the Italian, briefly the German during the occupation in the Second World War, and after it the Yugoslav Railways, and since 1991 it has been under the management of the Croatian Railways, today HŽ Infrastruktura d.o.o.,” curator Josip Kajinić says and adds: “Today on the railway line between the Croatian-Slovenian border and the terminal station in Pula there are eight stations and 16 stops. This line is special in that it is probably the most authentic on the entire railway network in the territory of Croatia, with the largest number of originally preserved station buildings and other track facilities.”

michael portillo spotlights a vodnjan station

The cult British travel writer Michael Portillo presented in 2025 in the BBC series “Great Continental Railway Journeys” the station in Vodnjan with its old-fashioned technology that is still in use today.

The story of the railways in Istria is also shown by the recent exhibition “Gremo na makinu!” at the Historical and Maritime Museum of Istria in Pula, as well as the steam locomotive of the FS 835 series located next to the station building in Pula, which is a protected cultural asset and part of the holdings of the Croatian Railway Museum. “With the exhibition we wanted to show how important the railway was for the development of Istria, not only in a transport and economic sense, but also in the everyday life of people. We sought, along with a historical overview of the construction and development of the lines, to present objects that tell us about the functioning of the railway and the people who worked on it. It is particularly interesting that part of the exhibited material is available to the public for the first time, and the former lines that, although they no longer exist today, played an important role in connecting Istria are also covered,” they say for Index at the Historical and Maritime Museum of Istria in Pula.

The government and Croatian Railways have also revived the plan to connect with the Istrian lines by a tunnel through Učka. Although the foundation stone for the construction of the tunnel under Ćićarija was laid as early as 1993 by the then Croatian president Dr. Franjo Tuđman, the state company HŽ Infrastruktura only in May 2026 signed a contract for the documentation and conceptual design of that tunnel. The project should be completed in two years and will cost around two million euros. When the Istrian railways will be directly connected with the rest of Croatia is still not remotely known.

World.title: New Interactive Earthquake Map Reveals Where Danger in Croatia is Greatest
World.content:
October the 19th, 2026 – A new interactive earthquake map reveals here the danger in Croatia is the greatest, with southern Croatia in particular in quite the precarious spot.

Croatian scientists have produced a new seismic hazard assessment for Croatia that incorporates the experiences of the Petrinja earthquake and data on the soil beneath our cities. Index/Nenad Jaric Dauenhauer reports that the danger is greatest along the Adriatic coast, especially down south in the wider Dubrovnik area. The results also reveal something a little less obvious: for low and rigid buildings, including family houses, the new assessment along the coast and far inland in the area of Petrinja gives higher seismic loads than those prescribed, while for high buildings, it mostly gives lower ones.

This new map could serve as a scientific basis for a new Croatian national annex to Eurocode 8, the European standard for earthquake-resistant construction. It describes how strongly the ground could shake, with a certain probability, but it does not announce the date of the next earthquake nor does it itself reveal which building will survive.

why does croatia need a new earthquake map?

The Zagreb earthquake of magnitude 5.5 that struck back in March 2020 and the Petrinja earthquake of magnitude 6.2 later that same year in December showed just how devastating the combination of strong shaking and vulnerable buildings can be. Dubrovnik was almost destroyed in 1667 by an earthquake of estimated magnitude around 7, and Zagreb was struck in 1880 by an earthquake of magnitude around 5.9.

“Destructive earthquakes here are not a footnote in history. That is precisely why probabilistic seismic hazard assessment is the right framework for design and spatial planning across Croatia,” explained Professor Snježana Markušić from the Geophysical Department of the Faculty of Science (PMF) in Zagreb, the first author of the paper. The current Croatian seismic hazard map, an integral part of the national annex to Eurocode 8 from back in 2011, is based on earlier research. In the meantime, scientists have collected new earthquake records and data on local soil conditions, and in 2024 the second generation of Eurocode 8 was also published.

The new assessment was prepared by Snježana Markušić, Iva Žilić, Tomislav Fiket and Anja Majurec from the Geophysical Department of PMF in Zagreb, Davor Stanko from the Faculty of Geotechnical Engineering in Varaždin, and Tvrtko Korbar from the Croatian Geological Survey. The paper was published on the 17th of September 2026 in the journal Bulletin of Earthquake Engineering (BEE).

earthquakes don’t care about borders

Seismic hazards in Croatian cities are also influenced by earthquakes outside of Croatia. For Dubrovnik, for example, the seismic areas located on the territories of both Montenegro and Albania are very important. That is why the processed area is considerably wider than Croatia. Foreshocks and aftershocks were removed from the earthquake catalogue, because the model describes the long-term frequency of mainshocks. “90,003 mainshocks remained, only 14.9 percent of all recorded events. Almost three quarters were aftershocks,” says Tomislav Fiket from PMF.

The authors divided the wider area of Croatia and neighbouring countries into 32 zones according to geological structure, seismic activity and faults, and performed the calculations in the open-source program OpenQuake. “Three large tectonic units – the Adriatic Foreland, the Dinarides and the Pannonian Basin – create very different conditions in the Earth’s crust, so faults across the country move in different ways. We incorporated that diversity into the model, for each zone separately,” explains Tvrtko Korbar from the Croatian Geological Survey.

Two similar houses, one on solid rock and the other on thick deposits of softer soil, will not shake equally during the same earthquake, because softer deposits can amplify the shaking. An important novelty of the paper is therefore the inclusion of soil data, instead of calculating only for solid rock. “A model that includes the actual surface of the terrain directly encompasses the amplification of shaking due to local soil, instead of it being subsequently estimated with a simplified factor,” says Davor Stanko from the Faculty of Geotechnical Engineering. How important local differences are is also shown by a study of Zagreb published in 2025, in which Markušić and Stanko participated. It turned out that in the central and south-eastern parts of the city thick, unconsolidated deposits can amplify seismic waves.

dubrovnik and central dalmatia are areas of concern

The overall seismic hazard is by far the greatest along the coastline, especially down in the Dubrovnik-Neretva area and a little further north in central Dalmatia. Scientists express this danger by the maximum ground acceleration during shaking, in units of g. One g is equal to the acceleration of gravity (9.81 m/s²), so a value of 0.40 g means that the maximum horizontal ground acceleration during shaking reaches 40 percent of that amount. The greater the acceleration, the greater the loads buildings are generally exposed to, but their response also depends on the properties of the structure.

With actual soil conditions taken into consideration, the new assessment gives around 0.40 g across Dubrovnik, 0.32 g in Split, 0.27 g in Rijeka, 0.24 g in Zagreb, 0.22 g in Petrinja and 0.08 g in Osijek. This means that in each of those cities there is about a 10 percent probability that the peak ground acceleration in the next 50 years will exceed the stated value. This is not the strongest possible shaking, nor is it the magnitude of the earthquake: magnitude describes the energy released at the earthquake focus, while ground acceleration describes how strongly the ground shakes at a particular place. “The areas of Sisak, Moslavina and Petrinja, despite the strong earthquake sequence of 2020, according to our results belongs to the group of moderate hazard,” says Markušić. Nevertheless, even weaker shaking can cause great damage if buildings are poorly constructed.

earthquakes have no schedule

The information that a certain level of shaking has a return period of 475 years is easily misleading. It does not mean that such shaking comes once every 475 years and that after it follows centuries of calm. It’s a statistical description: the annual probability of exceedance is about 0.2 percent, which over 50 years, the usual lifespan of a building, accumulates to about 10 percent. The model assumes that earthquakes have no “memory”, as with rolling a die: the previous result does not determine the next one. For critical infrastructure a rarer, stronger shaking is also important, with a return period of 2,475 years and about a 2 percent probability of exceedance in 50 years.

what a single house does and what a building does during an earthquake are very different…

Every building has a natural period of oscillation, the time of one full swing, and it amounts to about a tenth of a second per storey: a family house oscillates with a period of about 0.1 to 0.2 seconds, and a building of about ten storeys with a period of about one second. A building sways most strongly when oscillations of a period similar to its own predominate in the ground motion, similar to a swing that we push at the right moment. According to the new assessment, that shaking is strongest in all the observed cities for a period of 0.2 seconds, i.e. precisely for low buildings.

That’s why low and rigid buildings on the coast and in Petrinja could be exposed to higher seismic loads than those provided for by the current design spectrum. For high and flexible buildings, which sway more slowly, the new assessment almost everywhere gives lower loads than those prescribed. The comparison is nevertheless not entirely equal because the current spectrum refers to solid rock, while the new assessment also includes local soil.

“The results indicate that a map prepared for a uniform reference rock, when local soil is taken into account, can in some places underestimate and in others overestimate the hazard. There is no single correction factor applicable throughout the country,” Markušić explains.

“For the faults responsible for the strongest earthquakes in Croatia, such as the Petrinja and Pokupsko faults, there are still not enough complete data for them to be reliably modelled separately. Their inclusion is a priority for the next generation of models,” explained Korbar. “Croatia’s database of strong earthquake records is still relatively small. Its expansion, together with the preparation of a more detailed national soil database, is one of the key next steps,” adds Žilić.

will the new map force construction rule changes?

The new research represents a scientific study of probabilistic seismic hazard assessment, not a national annex to the standard, and does not prescribe legally binding design values. “We offer a scientific basis on which the competent authorities can rely when they start preparing the new annex that Croatia must adopt for the second generation of Eurocode 8,” Markušić emphasises. The new Croatian earthquake danger map will therefore not change the regulations overnight. It gives the competent authorities a new basis for decisions, and citizens a clearer picture of the hazard. The safety of an individual building still needs to be assessed according to its structure, condition and the soil on which it stands. The greatest value of the new map will be that better knowledge about earthquakes is turned into safer construction.

World.title: 40% of Croatian Retirees are in Poverty, Soup Kitchen Use Increases
World.content:
October the 19th, 2026 – An appalling 40% of Croatian retirees are now living in poverty according to the latest data, with soup kitchen use increasing in a country that keeps pushing the inflationary limits.

According to the latest data from the Croatian Bureau of Statistics, almost every fifth citizen of Croatia lives on the absolute brink of poverty. Index reports that for Croatian retirees, the figures are even more disgraceful, as almost 40% of them actually do live in poverty. What a staggering paradox it is when a country so full of highly expensive resorts and throngs of tourists is also dealing with growing queues in front of soup kitchens.

After decades of work, many people still do not have enough to live a dignified life. “In general, I think that the majority of pensioners don’t live with dignity. I consider a dignified life to be when a person who has worked for 40 years can in retirement live normally, afford to go to the theatre or cinema, and afford the majority of ordinary things,” stated Višnja Stanišić, president of the Croatian Pensioners’ Trade Union.

When a large part of the pension goes on utility bills, many have no choice but to seek help. In the soup kitchens they are greeted every day by volunteers. “Some come who don’t even have boxes to pack the food into, they come literally with ordinary plastic bags and pack the food into them. Quite a lot of poor people come,” volunteer Lovro Maričić revealed.

The situation is also worsened by Croatia’s constantly rising prices. Inflation in September amounted to a deeply concerning 4.7%, which is the second consecutive month of growth. The biggest cause is energy prices, which have risen by approximately 20%. Such growth hits those with the lowest incomes the hardest.

“Every single pensioner has their own personal inflation to try to deal with because they spend on five to six products whose prices have risen considerably more than the official rate, for some by as much as 10%,” Stanišić explained.

“We’ve proposed an amendment with which we’ll cover more than 30,000 pensioners living within the City of Zagreb. We intend to raise the threshold for financial assistance from a pension of 350 to 500 euros,” said Matej Mišić, president of the SDP of the City of Zagreb. While politicians announce more measures, in the soup kitchens the situation is getting harder and harder. “It could be said that the number of users is even higher than last year. Today was quite busy and a lot of people came,” volunteer Lovro Maričić concluded.

World.title: Former Mayor Claims Split Has Been “Disgraced” Worldwide
World.content:
October the 19th, 2026 – Former Split mayor Ivica Puljak has claimed that Split has been “disgraced” worldwide after the violent clash between Torcida and Ajax.

Former Split mayor Ivica Puljak commented on Torcida’s procession ahead of the Hajduk–Ajax match, when antisemitic, Nazi and Ustaše slogans were chanted through the city streets. Index reports that he said that the footage has spread around Europe and the world and that Split has been disgraced. “We owe an apology to the Jews and to all decent people because that is not us, that is not our city,” Puljak stated, Dalmacija Danas reports.

Puljak stressed that condemnations of the incident are not enough if one wants to prevent the repetition of such events. He believes it is necessary to speak openly about the causes and sees responsibility in politics and in the authorities’ attitude towards the return of extremist symbols into public space. “This didn’t start last Thursday and it didn’t start on the street. For years, we’ve been watching a politics for which the most important thing is to stay in power and which for that reason has allied itself with anyone, regardless of where they come from. That same politics has for years silently watched as the dark past returns to public space,” Puljak said.

an (expected) swipe at hdz…

He added that tolerating such phenomena can be understood as permission and opened the question of possible deals between members of the ruling party and fan groups. He also expressed suspicion that this is a staging by HDZ.

“Have certain people from the ruling party made a deal with fan groups that they will have their support at elections, and then these will tolerate everything they do? And who knows what else is hidden behind those deals,” Puljak asked. As a second important problem Puljak singled out clientelism and employment in the public sector. According to his estimate, in Croatia there are at least 10,000 managerial jobs that were not created because of the needs of society, but because of HDZ’s needs for employment.

“croatian society needs to be reset”

He called for the abolition of such positions and said that a change of government must not mean the replacement of party cadres. “The rule must be simple and without exception: always and only the best,” he said. Puljak stated that Croatian society needs to be “reset” and placed on the foundations of science, reason and humanism.

“Those who shouted through Split last Thursday were not defending Croatia, nor Christianity, nor humanism, but were disgracing all three,” he declared. He explained that the symbol of his political option is a broom, with which he wants to convey that long-standing problems need to be removed. “We need to sweep away what has been accumulating in the corners for years, and that is clientelism, corruption and tolerance of hatred,” he said. He concluded his message with a call to citizens for joint action. “Croatia deserves it. Split deserves it. Let’s do it together,” he urged.

World.title: 1,200-year-old archaeological site discovered Iraq’s Babil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The central Iraqi province of Babil announced on Sunday that an exciting archaeological site has been discovered.

Located in the al-Qasim district in the southern part of the province, the remains are believed to date back to the Abbasid era, a period of immense cultural, scientific, and architectural prosperity throughout Iraq.

The Governor of Babil, Ali al-Jamali, conducted an official site visit to examine the structural features, evaluate its historical context, and lay out administrative frameworks to safeguard the artifacts under strict national archaeological laws.

Local officials stressed that this discovery goes much beyond the previous statistics. Professional excavations and investigations are likely to provide additional details about ancient life centuries ago.

Officials are investigating legal alternatives for securely developing the area into a significant tourist destination, raising Babil’s global historical prominence.

The recent announcement follows the discovery of a large ancient city in Basra, dating back 1,200 years, as well as the uncovering of hundreds of ancient Islamic and Hellenistic artifacts revealed by rain at the Borsippa site, both occurring in 2025. This adds to a remarkable series of historical discoveries in Iraq.

The newly discovered archaeological site in Babil’s al-Qasim district provides a crucial physical link to the vast networks that powered the Islamic Golden Age. During the Abbasid era, Iraq was the undisputed geopolitical and economic center of the Islamic world.

World.title: Iraq increases oil exports to 3.4 million barrels per day
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Minister of Oil Basim Khudair said on Monday that the export rate during October has risen to 3.4 million barrels per day through three routes, including the Strait of Hormuz.

Iraq’s crude oil export in October surpassed 3.4 million barrels per day through the Strait of Hormuz, the Turkish port of Ceyhan, and the Syrian port of Baniyas, according to Khudair.

Despite the military conflict in the Strait of Hormuz, the Iraqi Ministry of Oil—through the State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO)—has managed to maintain an average export rate of three million barrels per day over the past nine months, according to the oil minister.

However, since the beginning of October, the export rate has risen to over 3.4 million barrels per day, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

The Ministry of Oil is trying to boost export capacity, which will provide financial revenue for the state. Khudair noted that developing export capacity will allow the government to carry out its tasks and secure the required funds for different governmental expenditures.

Khudair noted that crude oil exports are directed to European and Asian markets, as well as the American market.

Eco Iraq revealed on Saturday that oil production during September reached its highest daily average since the beginning of 2026, at 4.39 million barrels per day.

Iraq’s oil output stayed at normal levels in January and February, averaging more than 4.1 million barrels per day, before falling drastically in March as a result of the war in the region.

Iraq’s average daily oil output was 4.09 million barrels in January and 4.14 million barrels in February before falling to 1.9 million barrels in March and 1.63 million in April.

In May, the country’s oil production fell to 1.4 million barrels per day before rising to 1.52 million in June.

The improvement in oil output continued until the third quarter of the year. According to figures from OPEC, average output increased to 2.9 million barrels per day in July, 3.74 million barrels per day in August, and 4.39 million barrels per day in September.

World.title: Iraq, World Bank discuss financing strategic projects
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Finance Minister Faleh Sari and World Bank Group Vice President for the Middle East and North Africa Ousmane Dione discussed on Thursday financing strategic projects and support for economic reforms in Iraq.

The meeting took place on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group, held in Bangkok, Thailand, according to a statement released by the Finance Ministry.

Sari stressed the World Bank’s role in Iraq’s economic and financial transformation. He outlined the country’s desire to use the World Bank’s expertise and financial contributions to carry out significant projects in the energy, education, transportation, and digital transformation sectors.

The step aims to promote sustainable development and improve the efficiency of public services in Iraq, according to Sari.

Dione praised the collaboration with the Iraqi Finance Ministry, indicating that it has efficiently arranged its operational and communication mechanisms with the World Bank.

The World Bank official highlighted that the efforts of the Iraqi government pave the way for additional initiatives to support the country’s economic and financial goals in the upcoming period.

Sari reaffirmed last week Iraq’s commitment to continuing economic and financial reforms, diversifying revenue sources, and strengthening the role of the private sector.

According to Sari, these measures aim to bolster economic stability and enhance the country’s capacity to deal with regional challenges.

Sari noted that the government is addressing the economic consequences of the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz by reprioritizing expenditures, increasing non-oil revenues, and maintaining the state’s essential obligations while pursuing structural reforms.

“Iraq Vision 2050” represents a strategic plan for reducing dependency on oil, broadening production, empowering the private sector, and achieving inclusive and sustainable economic growth, according to Sari.

The minister noted that the reform package includes enhancing public financial management, automating customs and tax operations, boosting the business and investment climate, upgrading the banking sector, and increasing electronic payment systems.

According to Sari, the partnership with the IMF and the World Bank Group supports the economic and financial reform program.

World.title: Chinese oilfield service firm markets Iraq’s oil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – China-based Anton Oilfield Services Group has sold its first Iraqi crude oil shipment as part of a new supply deal with the State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO).

According to Reuters, the unique arrangement with one of a few Chinese independent oil corporations expanding their activities in Iraq enables Baghdad to access cash to pay service suppliers.

Iraq is attempting to bolster oil exports impacted by the military conflict in the Middle East. In the past few months, greater discounts have enticed traders and refiners, leading to a resurgence in its oil shipments.

The Chinese firm said in a statement on Saturday that the agreement intends to improve Basra Oil Company’s (BOC) crude oil sales and cash flow, provide channels for engineering and services, and expedite payment collection for Anton and partners.

An official in the oil sector indicated that Anton struck an agreement with SOMO to market undetermined amounts of Iraqi crude oil, mostly from the Majnoon oilfield managed by BOC.

In late September, Anton marketed one million barrels of Basra Heavy crude to a trading company.

Anton mentioned that the agreement with SOMO allows it to sell oil from the Dhufriya oilfield in eastern Iraq, where it received a license in 2024 to develop the field.

World.title: Iraq inaugurates first satellite ground station
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Minister of Communications Mustafa Sanad inaugurated on Sunday Iraq’s first satellite ground station in Baghdad, a step aiming to bolster digital sovereignty and develop the country’s telecommunications infrastructure.

In a speech he delivered during the inauguration ceremony, Sanad said that Iraq’s acquisition of a satellite would be impossible without a ground station.

The new facility will serve as a cornerstone for the country’s upcoming national space program, with future expansions planned to establish additional ground stations across other Iraqi provinces depending on population density and administrative assessment.

The station also acts as a complete technological hub that includes a satellite communication gateway, a localized data center, and an internet exchange point.

Developed in partnership with the technology group Commercis, the station links incoming satellite communications directly into Iraq’s expanding domestic fiber-optic terrestrial network.

Iraq previously relied on international infrastructure located outside its borders to route satellite traffic. The government is now actively urging ministries, private companies, and security agencies to migrate their traffic to this local gateway to secure sensitive data.

The station is part of a broader economic vision to transform Iraq into a regional data corridor. By leveraging its geographic location, Iraq aims to serve as a high-speed data transit bridge connecting networks across Asia, Africa, and Europe.

The station provides high-speed enterprise internet, secure government communications, live television feeds, and commercial satellite broadcasting.

World.title: Competing narratives emerge over blast at PMF security compound in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Two days after a powerful blast ripped through a Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) security headquarters in eastern Baghdad, an investigative report published by Al Mada newspaper and monithas revealed sharp contradictions surrounding the incident, presenting four competing narratives ranging from a targeted foreign strike to sabotage and munitions mismanagement.

The explosion struck at approximately 6:00 PM on Saturday, October 17, 2026, inside a facility operated by the PMF Security Directorate located along Sadr Al-Qanat near the Saad Al-Watri Hospital.

While the PMF’s official communique attributed the incident to an internal fire that detonated obsolete, deteriorated munitions—resulting in minor injuries to five personnel—field sources cited by Al Mada report over twenty injuries among PMF security personnel and unidentified associates. Strict security cordons accompanied the medical evacuation via PMF ambulances, fueling speculation regarding the potential presence of Iranian technical personnel at the site.

The circumstances have ignited debate over the operational nature of the facility. As an intelligence and security installation, the complex is not designated to warehouse expired ordnance. Security sources cited in the report claimed that newly arrived military consignments from Iran had been transferred into the depot just a week prior to the detonation.

Preliminary forensic findings referenced in the investigation point to the possibility of an incoming projectile initiating the primary blast, though information sharing on the file remains tightly restricted by the PMF Chief of Staff’s office while a specialized investigative committee established by Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi conducts its inquiry.

Four Competing Accounts

World.title: Iraq opens public university admissions for international schools’ graduates
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research announced on Monday, October 19, 2026, that the electronic admissions portal for international school graduates applying to public universities will open within the coming days for the 2026–2027 academic year.

According to a ministerial press release obtained by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), admissions processing will be managed through the centralized digital application platform Qaddim.

Eligible candidates graduating from accredited international curricula within Iraq will access the admissions system using their standardized examination sequence number and confidential verification credentials issued directly by their respective school administrations.

The ministry advised prospective students and guardians to monitor its official web portal and recognized digital channels for forthcoming regulatory guidelines, grade-weighting criteria, and precise application submission schedules.

The upcoming portal launch represents an institutional mechanism to integrate international school diploma holders into national university admissions channels alongside graduates of the standard ministerial secondary baccalaureate examinations.

World.title: US dollar edges up to 169,500 IQD in Baghdad and provincial exchanges
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar edged upward across parallel retail and wholesale counters in Baghdad and major commercial hubs on Monday, October 19, 2026.

The capital recorded an increase of 500 dinars per $100 compared to prior trading sessions, while regional desks in Erbil and Basra registered fractional gains of 50 dinars per $100.

In Baghdad, licensed exchange shops and retail desks posted dollar cash selling quotes at 169,500 dinars per $100 against purchase bids of 168,500 dinars, reflecting persistent upward pressure in parallel liquidity channels.

In Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan Region, counters listed selling rates at 168,550 dinars per $100 with purchase transactions accepted at 168,000 dinars. Across the southern port province of Basra, foreign exchange desks closed the morning session at a selling price of 168,750 dinars per $100 against buying offers of 168,250 dinars.

The current parallel figures sustain a pronounced gap above the official statutory cash rate mandated by the Central Bank of Iraq, which remains benchmarked at 152,000 dinars per $100.

This continuous premium highlights elevated demand for physical banknotes among local commercial importers navigating foreign trade settlements outside the central electronic clearance window.

World.title: ‘Rural safety net under attack’: Jairam Ramesh calls MGNREGA replacement a ‘surgical strike’
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh on Tuesday called the replacement of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) with the VB-G RAM G Act a âsurgical strikeâ on the social safety net protecting rural India, alleging that the move had weakened support for workers facing distress.

In a post on X, Ramesh referred to drought conditions in Beed and other districts of Maharashtra, which he said were facing their worst drought in a decade. He said MGNREGA had provided a guarantee of support to rural workers during such crises, but alleged that its replacement had undermined that protection.

âBeed and other districts in Maharashtra are facing the worst drought in a decade. MGNREGA was the guarantee of support in such times of extreme distress.

But its replacement with VB-G RAM G is nothing less than a surgical strike on the social safety net that protected rural India,â he wrote.

Jairam ramesh alleges wage theft, fake attendance

World.title: 'No double standards on terrorism': Rajnath Singh's stern warning at SCO meet with Pakistan at the table
World.content:
NEW DELHI: With Pakistanâs deputy PM Ishaq Dar in the room, defence minister

on Tuesday delivered a strong message against

at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) meeting in Tajikistan's Dushanbe.

Addressing representatives of SCO member countries, Rajnath said terrorism remained one of the biggest threats to peace and development, warning that its impact extended far beyond the loss of innocent lives.

âTerrorism not only causes the loss of innocent lives but also disrupts investment and commerce. It radicalises society and deprives our youth of the opportunities they deserve,â the defence minister said.

The defence minister stressed that terrorism could not be justified under any circumstances and called for a united approach against those who enable it.

âThere should be no double standards in dealing with terrorism, and no place for those who finance, support or provide safe havens to terrorists. The entire ecosystem of terrorism must be firmly and collectively dismantled,â he said.

Rajnath's remarks come days after he reiterated Indiaâs firm position on crossborder terrorism, warning on October 15 that any further terrorist acts originating from Pakistan would invite an even stronger response.





Speaking at the Times Network Defence Conclave in New Delhi, he said Indiaâs commitment to dialogue, coexistence and peaceful dispute resolution should not be mistaken for weakness.

âOperation Sindoor, Balakot Airstrikes and Surgical Strikes werenât just military operations; they symbolised a decisive shift in the nationâs approach, moving from diplomatic condemnation to proactive action aimed at rooting out terrorism by reaching its very source,â Rajnath said.

He also said that since 2014, the âshelf lifeâ of most terrorists had fallen to less than a year, with security forces neutralising them within a year of their taking up arms against India.

Emphasising the link between strength and peace, Rajnath said India remained committed to peaceful coexistence while staying prepared to deal with threats to its security.

âOur commitment to peace remains steadfast, yet we are fully prepared to confront any challenge.

Our goal is to build an India that, while advocating for peace, remains vigilant when it comes to security and is fully capable of safeguarding its sovereignty, integrity, and national interests,â he said.

Rajnath meets Tajik, Iranian leaders on SCO sidelines

On the sidelines of the SCO meeting, Singh held separate meetings with Tajikistan Prime Minister Qohir Rosulzoda and Iran's First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref.

During his meeting with Rosulzoda, Singh highlighted the longstanding civilisational ties and close people-to-people connections between India and Tajikistan.

In a post on X, the defence minister said, "Delighted to meet H.E. Mr Qohir Rosulzoda, Prime Minister of Tajikistan at the commencement of SCO Heads of Government meeting in Dushanbe. Underlined the longstanding civilisational ties and deep people to people links between India and Tajikistan."

Rajnath also met Aref and shared details of the interaction on X. "Pleasure to meet H.E. Mr Mohammad Reza Aref, First Vice President of Iran on the sidelines of the SCO Heads of Government meeting in Dushanbe," he wrote.

What is on the SCO agenda?

Rajnath is representing India at the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting in the Tajik capital, where leaders and representatives of member countries have gathered to discuss regional cooperation.

World.title: 'Vote Chori Ki Raasleela’: Youth Congress burns Ravan effigy with Gyanesh's face - watch
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Indian Youth Congress (IYC) on Monday burned an effigy of Ravan bearing the face of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi, demanding his resignation over alleged irregularities in the Election Commissionâs functioning and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

The protest was held at the IYC headquarters on Raisina Road and featured a street performance titled Vote Chori Ki Raasleela, aimed at highlighting allegations of electoral manipulation and questioning the transparency and impartiality of the poll panel, according to a statement issued by the organisation.

Addressing the gathering, IYC national president Uday Bhanu Chib said the protests would continue until Kumar resigned or was jailed.

âGyanesh Kumar, who is finishing off the democracy and Constitution of the country, cannot save himself. We will continue to protest in different forms. This will continue until he goes behind bars or resigns. He has indulged in âvote choriâ. Until he is jailed, people of the country will continue to protest,â Chib told news agency ANI.

Chib said the Election Commission must be accountable to the public and that the CEC should take moral responsibility for concerns raised over electoral transparency.





âDemocracy is not merely about holding elections; it is about ensuring that every vote is respected and every citizen's mandate is protected.

âWhen serious questions are raised about electoral transparency, the responsibility of the Election Commission is to provide clear answers and uphold the highest standards of impartiality,â he said.

In its statement, the IYC said the effigy-burning was intended to convey its opposition to alleged electoral irregularities and demand accountability from the poll panel.

âThrough our 'Vote Chori Ki Raasleela' protest, the Indian Youth Congress is sending a clear message that the youth of this country will not allow the sanctity of democracy to be compromised. The burning of the effigy of CEC Gyanesh Kumar represents our anger and our demand for accountability,â Chib said.

World.title: Rubio India visit: Bilateral with Jaishankar, Jamnagar refinery tour & trade deal - whats on agenda
World.content:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will begin a three-day visit to India on Tuesday, with talks on a proposed bilateral trade deal, energy security and strategic cooperation expected to feature prominently during his meetings with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar and other engagements in Mumbai and Gujaratâs Jamnagar.

Rubio is scheduled to arrive at Mumbaiâs Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport at 2.15 pm on Tuesday, according to the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA). He will lay a wreath at the Taj memorial to honour the victims of the 26/11 terror attacks before holding bilateral talks with Jaishankar at the Taj Mahal Palace hotel.

The two leaders are expected to discuss the India-US Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership, including energy, trade and investment, defence, critical and emerging technologies, and the situation in West Asia.

Rubio will later attend the âFreedom 250 Receptionâ at the Jio World Convention Centre to mark the 250th anniversary of US independence. Jaishankar will be the guest of honour.

Trade deal and energy security in focus

The visit comes as both countries seek to advance negotiations on a proposed trade agreement amid friction over tariffs, energy imports and immigration policies.

Speaking in Uzbekistan ahead of his India visit, Rubio said the two sides were close to finalising the agreement.





"We're trying to finalise a trade deal with India right now. We're very close to doing that."

Rubio also linked the negotiations to Washingtonâs decision to grant a temporary waiver on certain sanctions related to Russian energy purchases. He said Indiaâs energy requirements and its importance as a US partner were among the factors being considered.

"These sanctions were not just sanctions on Russia. They include tariffs on a number of countriesâIndia, for example, and others.

And so I think the president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyse what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy and even to the U.S. economy," Rubio said.

He added that India had diversified its energy sources but continued to rely on Russian supplies because shifting to alternatives could not happen overnight.

"You've got countries like India, for example, that have voluntarily diversified their energy portfolio, but are still getting a substantial amount of energy from Russia because it's hard to pivot from one day to the next.

But they're also an important ally and partner of the United States. So we need that period of time to sort of study all this and figure out what the right combination is," he added.

India and the US have been negotiating the proposed trade pact since early 2025, seeking to address tariff disputes, reduce non-tariff barriers and improve market access. Jaishankar recently said the negotiations were nearing a "landing point".

Jamnagar visit and meeting with Ambani

Rubio will travel to Jamnagar in Gujarat on Wednesday, where he is expected to visit Reliance Industriesâ oil refining complex and meet chairman Mukesh Ambani before returning to Mumbai. The Jamnagar leg of the visit is expected to last around nine hours.

The visit comes as Reliance Industries prepares for a planned investment in a Texas oil refinery, bringing energy cooperation and private-sector investment into focus.

Officials have not confirmed reports that Rubio may also visit the Vantara animal rehabilitation centre in Jamnagar.

Rubio is also expected to engage with Indian business leaders during his visit, although meetings with industrialists Gautam Adani and Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran have not been officially confirmed.

Visit comes amid strains in bilateral ties

Rubioâs trip is his second visit to India this year, following his May visit, when he met Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Jaishankar and attended a Quad foreign ministersâ meeting.

Bilateral relations have faced strains following US tariffs on Indian goods, disagreements over Washingtonâs claims about its role in de-escalating the India-Pakistan military conflict in May 2025, and changes to US immigration policies, including higher H-1B visa fees.

The two sides are also expected to exchange views on the West Asia crisis and regional stability. Rubioâs visit follows his meetings with Central Asian foreign ministers in Uzbekistan, where he promoted US trade, security and investment ties with the region.

World.title: SC judges jokingly threaten to sit on dharna for foot overbridge and pedestrian path
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In the season of dharnas and protests in Delhi, a

bench led by Justice J B Pardiwala last week threatened in a lighter vein to sit on dharna at the Delhi HC main gate if by Nov 25 the govt failed to construct a foot overbridge and pedestrian paths to facilitate safe road crossing for lawyers, litigants and public.

Justices Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan told additional solicitor general Vikramjit Banerjee - âIf you don't do it before the next date, both of us will be at the main gate of the HC, and we will not go home until you complete the work. That's for sure. Baith jaayenge wahan dharna karne ke liye.â

The case related to the stretch of Mathura Road near the HC and Zoological Park, where absence of a foot overbridge and pedestrian safe crossings had been flagged months ago by the SC.

Amicus curiae Gaurav Agrawal informed the court on Friday that a traffic signal has been installed. But that did not satisfy the court which threatened sit-in dharna by the judges.

If to get a work done for benefit of public, the SC judges, even in lighter vein, feel that dharna is a better option than issuing a mandamus to the govt, then it could have serious implications given the stark contrast between right to expeditious justice and the pendency of more than 95,000 cases in the SC.





This is the view expressed by a cross-section of lawyers in lighter vein when TOI sought their responses to Justice Pardiwala's banter.

Even if one can tell litigants that they must not complain about the 36,000 cases which are pending 'only' for five years in the apex court which has time and again ruled that right to speedy justice is part of right to life, what would the SC tell the litigants who are waiting patiently for the balance of nearly 60,000 cases?

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

If they decide to enforce their right to speedy justice through dharna at the SC, it would create a law and order situation, which an already stretched Delhi police will find it difficult to handle, the lawyers feared.

What about those litigants in the HCs who have been awaiting a hearing in their cases for years together, without expecting a decision? They have been routinely told by the SC to await their chance in the HC and declined then out of turn hearing. maximum such application for a direction for early hearing pertain to the Allahabad HC, where over 12 lakh cases are pending, many for decades. If lakhs of litigants decide to hold dharnas at the HC and its bench at Lucknow, would the police be able to handle the surge of protesters?

In the trial courts, the pendency is more than 5.1 crore cases, of which 47 lakh are more than 10 years old and 81 lakh are between 5-10 years-old. What if these litigants, who while awaiting justice have been drained of their finances, are physically exhausted by repeated adjournments and mentally disturbed by the pendency, decide to hold sit-in dharnas at the trial courts?

World.title: Young innovators impress juries with ideas to solve real-world challenges
World.content:
Jury members evaluate entries for TOIâs Ideas for India contest in Delhi

-

Ideas For India

NEW DELHI: Three separate juries evaluated entries in the three categories for the award and the panel members acknowledged at the end of the day that the quality of applicants was excellent. In each of the categories, bulk of those shortlisted for evaluation by the jury were very young, either still in college or just out of it, though there were some older innovators too.Over 14,000 applications were received, which were filtered down by Techgig to 1,000 and Grant Thornton shortlisted it to 35 finalists that were split between three juries. While first was on sovereign technology for India handled 14 entries, second on Inclusive Innovation for Bharat met a dozen applications and third on Sustainable & Resilient India dealt with nine entries.The juries followed a pattern of a short presentation by the applicants, followed by questions from jury members and then a brief discussion between the members before scoring the applicant. Several jury members admitted that they were pleasantly surprised by how well thought through the presentations were, especially given the age of most applicants.Even where some aspect of the road to implementation may have not occurred to the applicants â say, a compliance issue or consent to be obtained â it was striking how eager the innovators were to learn from the experience of those who had worked in the real world for decades and knew what it takes to translate brilliant ideas into real solutions.The maturity to take hard questions as essential inputs rather than as harsh criticism was quite remarkable.The diversity of the presentations was also a striking aspect. In the technology sovereignty category, for instance, the ideas ranged from closing a felt gap in middle sized drones to faster and more efficient identification and countering of cyberattacks to dealing with ships that go âdarkâ, which may not always be for innocent reasons.But these were not just ideas. The drone entry had already done some testing in the field with army units, the dark ships idea had been explored with a port and so on.Such was the overall quality of the applicants that at least in two categories some of the jury members voiced the opinion that perhaps the awards need not be restricted to two in each category. There was, after all, no compulsion to stick to a bell curve, they pointed out. Most left the venue feeling satisfied that they had done their bit to encourage a cohort whose innovative mindset was matched by its enthusiasm to do good for society and for India.

World.title: Alberta voters reject separation from Canada in referendum
World.content:
Voters in Canada's oil-rich province of Alberta have rejected a proposal to begin a process toward independence, results showed early Tuesday (October 20, 2026), delivering a victory for Prime Minister Mark Carney and supporters of Canadian unity amid U.S. President Donald Trump's trade war and annexation threats.

The vote was not a direct referendum on independence but would have set oil-rich Alberta on a path toward a future vote on separation from Canada.

With more than 1 million votes counted, about 76% supported remaining in Canada, compared with 23% who backed beginning a process that could lead to separation.

“We are a solid country that's united from coast to coast to coast,” Thomas Lukaszuk, a former Alberta deputy premier who led the Forever Canadian campaign against separation, told supporters.

Results were delayed after late openings forced more than 100 polling stations to extend voting hours on Monday (October 19, 2026). More than 1.35 million Albertans, or 43% of eligible voters, cast advance or special ballots. Albertans were deciding whether to remain in Canada or begin a legal process that could have lead to a second vote on separation.

Alberta, home to the world's fourth-largest proven oil reserves, is cowboy country and a conservative stronghold whose political culture has long had more in common with the American West than much of Canada. Resentment toward Ottawa runs deep, but has not traditionally translated into widespread support for independence.

Dustin Degenhardt, a Wainwright voter, said Albertans have long been mistreated by Ottawa. “Alberta has essentially been treated as, you know, a colony,” he said after voting. “They want to take and take and take from us and not return anything.”

Taylor MacIsaac, another Wainwright voter, backed separation. “I think it'll be good for Alberta to separate personally, as a very conservative individual that grew up in rural Alberta,” she said.

Dave Malka, 59, of Edmonton, criticized spending money on a “referendum on a referendum” rather than health care.

With Mr. Trump threatening Canada, Mr. Malka said, “It seems to be happening at the absolute worst time when we should be united; instead we're fighting among ourselves.”

Jake Graham, 35, of Calgary, attended a Carney rally wearing maple leaf pants and a Canada hockey jacket. He hopes the vote ends the debate. “I hope this squashes this for a long time to come and that it's clear and decisive, that these grumblings disappear for a while and we can be a united Canada,” he said.

Despite the proposal's apparent failure, separatist leaders have said they turned a fringe cause into a movement that will not disappear.

Mr. Carney earlier urged Albertans to deliver a decisive vote for unity. “Vote like Canada's future depends on it because it does,” he told a rally in Edmonton, where he grew up.

Alberta Premier Danielle Smith called the referendum amid pressure from separatists within her governing United Conservative Party, even though she opposes independence. She cited a poll showing just 22% support for separation, a figure she said was still too high.

Separatist parties traditionally attracted only 1% or 2% of the vote, former Premier Jason Kenney said. Anger over COVID-19 restrictions helped mobilize activists who later embraced the separatist movement, he said.

Mr. Trump's trade war and threats to make Canada the 51st U.S. State have helped Carney rally support in Alberta, where Liberal prime ministers have historically been unpopular.

Separatist advocate Jeff Rath said he would be thrilled if 30% of Albertans voted to begin the separation process. He wants Smith ousted as leader of her governing United Conservative Party and said the party could splinter, potentially creating a new pro-independence party.

World.title: U.P. Panchayat poll: Is BJP looking to bypass the semi final?
World.content:
“Before May, we could get work of ₹5 lakh done at the Gram Sabha level. Now, for even ₹10 lakh worth of work, we need approval from the district administration,” says a village Pradhan from Kasganj district in Uttar Pradesh, citing the delay in local body elections in the State.

The Allahabad High Court’s directive to the Uttar Pradesh government and the State Election Commission (SEC) to complete the three-tier panchayat elections within three months has sparked conversations in village chaupals.

The State government had deferred the elections, due after the previous term expired in May 2026, to await a report from the Dedicated Backward Classes Commission on OBC reservations. The government put an interim arrangement in place where the outgoing Gram Pradhans are temporarily functioning as administrators until the new elected bodies take charge.

However, the High Court ruled that the polls cannot be delayed past constitutional limits and must proceed under the existing 27% OBC reservation framework. The figure comes from the previous exercise before the 2021 polls, when, instead of a triple-test survey that investigates political backwardness, the State conducted a rapid survey to estimate the OBC population for reservation purposes.

Political observers and opposition leaders argued that the State government knew the May 2026 expiration date and could have set up the commission months, or even a year, in advance to prevent a governance vacuum. They reminded the court that the Supreme Court-mandated “triple test” formula for providing Other Backward Classes (OBC) reservations in local body elections has been in place since 2010 and was made mandatory by the Supreme Court in 2021.

Welcoming the High Court order, Panchayati Raj Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar said the State is ready to hold the polls. “The High Court has issued its order; the Backward Classes Commission should take care of the matter. What do we have to do? We are ready to comply with the order. Once the Commission’s report is submitted, why would there be any need to approach the Supreme Court?,” he said in a media conference.

However, Rashtriya Panchayatiraj Gram Pradhan Sangathan (RPGPS), an organisation that advocates for the rights of village heads and Panchayati Raj institutions, said it would challenge the order in the Supreme Court because the court requires reservation for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) against its triple test formula, which says if the Triple Test requirements (including forming a dedicated commission) are not met, the seats reserved for OBCs must be treated as unreserved/open category seats.

It further claimed a significant discrepancy between voter lists prepared for panchayat elections and those for assembly polls. “Abhi Gaon ki satta Gaon ke haath main hai (At present the power of the village is in the hands of villagers), said Akhilesh Singh, national president of RPGPS. He pointed out that this was the first time gram pradhans have been made administrators after their tenures expired to manage routine affairs. “Hence, we should not rush into the election process that harms rural governance by trying to bypass incomplete voter rolls and ongoing OBC triple test surveys,” he said.

Samajwadi Party President Akhilesh Yadav, Congress MP Tanuj Punia, and AAP leader Sanjay Singh have also flagged discrepancies in voter lists. While several Indian states borrow, sync, or adopt the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) master voter list for local elections, U.P. is one of the few exceptions, strictly maintaining its own independent electoral rolls for local body polls.

A leader of the Primary School Teachers’ union, associated with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), said that when SIR was presented as a panacea for all ills, it would have been better to work on a common voter list. “At present, there are separate BLOs for the two rolls. It means more work for teachers in the Census year, and politically it creates an impression that there is something wrong with the enumeration process when everyone knows that the two lists cannot be completely aligned.”

Sources in the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and its ally Rashtriya Lok Dal (RDL) say the Panchayat elections were put on the back burner because the ruling dispensation didn’t want to create “bad blood amidst its rural cadre in the election year.”

While U.P. panchayat elections are fought without official party symbols, they heavily influence grassroots politics. When a political party backs a specific candidate, parties feel the rejected contender and his supporters may turn against it in subsequent assembly elections. “It is a well-recognised dynamic in rural politics, but you have to live with it, and the panchayat poll is considered a kind of semi-final,” said a hopeful with BJP links. “It seems the party wants to go straight into the final,” he remarked.

An RLD insider said there is meaningful silence on the ground because people know the government is not in a mood to conduct Panchayat polls before the Assembly elections. “Had it been conducted in May, we were ready, but now with little gap between the two polls it is neither practically nor politically viable,” he said.

Alleging that the State government deliberately delayed the process because it doesn’t want to face the anger of its core support base, Samajwadi Party’s national spokesperson Abdul Hafiz Gandhi said that “UGC guidelines, theft in donations to Ram Temple and paper leaks created an impression against the BJP, threatening its upper-caste vote.”

Further, citing newspaper reports from the 2021 elections, Mr. Gandhi said SP-supported candidates outperformed BJP-supported ones in Zila Panchayat polls. “I assume it is this fear that has caused the delay, but still I urge the BJP-led government to clarify the reasons and ensure that the entire electoral process, including reservation, is completed within the court-mandated period.”

Meanwhile, at a meeting in Ghaziabad, CM Yogi Adityanath projected the upcoming MLC election for teacher and graduate constituencies as the semi-final.

World.title: PSG-Barcelona match in Champions League to go ahead amid shock over France’s violent unrest
World.content:
The showpiece Champions League match between Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona will go ahead as planned on Tuesday in the French capital city, the French Interior minister confirmed, despite a weekend of protests marred by violence and looting across the country.

Also read | France protest: Prime Minister calls for localised curfews in cities to curb rioting, looting

Many French citizens have been left shocked by the images of violence that have drawn worldwide attention and highlighted the country's tense social climate. On Monday, French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said he has instructed prefects to impose “very limited” and “localized” curfews in cities to prevent more rioting and looting.

The violence targeted city halls, other public buildings and hundreds of businesses across the country, leading to more than 2,000 arrests.

Tuesday's (October 20, 2026) match between PSG and Barcelona at the Parc des Princes will require a robust security deployment, with police forces already strained following weeks of student protests. In May, Paris police detained dozens of people after violence disrupted celebrations of PSG's second Champions League title win and a group tried to storm a police station in the French capital.

Speaking after an emergency meeting with top government officials, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said the possibility of calling off planned events was discussed, including football matches.

“But this does not apply to tomorrow's match between PSG and FC Barcelona,” he said, adding that other matches planned in European competitions this week would not be affected. Nuñez mentioned the match between Lille and Galatasaray scheduled Wednesday in the northern city, where looters also vandalized shops over the weekend.

Nuñez offered his resignation on Sunday (October 18), but French President Emmanuel Macron asked him to stay to respond to police needs in an emergency situation. Macron instructed Nuñez “to take all necessary steps to ensure full transparency about the failures in planning and intelligence-gathering that led to the violence.”

Lecornu said details of the areas to be placed under curfew will be provided later.

Nuñez acknowledged that authorities had “lost control” in some major cities on Saturday (October 17), with hundreds of businesses looted.

World.title: France to impose new curfews where necessary: PM Sebastien Lecornu
World.content:
France will impose new curfews in areas where needed on Tuesday (October 20, 2026), Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said, adding that the measures introduced in several cities the previous day had “helped keep the night calm”.

France was rocked on Saturday (October 17, 2026) by some of its worst rioting in recent years, just six months before the country elects a successor to President Emmanuel Macron.

Accused of failing to anticipate and contain the street violence, the government has pledged to restore order, and had announced partial curfews in Paris and some other cities on Monday (October 19, 2026).

“Targeted curfews have contributed to calm overnight,” Mr. Lecornu wrote on X.

“Tonight new curfews will be decided where the situation requires it. These decisions will be made on the ground, by the prefects, in coordination with the mayors,” he said.

Police confirmed the night had passed without major incidents across France.
