These cases require an isolated facility where staff can properly clean and disinfect surfaces,” Chkhikvishvili said.

She added that Tbilisi had faced a similar crisis in the past, with cases in which serious diseases spread from a shelter in the capital.

A bad reputation

The footage has reignited debate in Georgian society about stray animals and how people treat them. But before examining this long-standing problem, which Georgia has struggled to resolve for decades, it is worth explaining why the images from Gori caused such an uproar.

At first glance, the public reaction might seem to stem from surprise, as though people had assumed the shelter met all the required standards, only to discover that it did not. In reality, the opposite is true: the Gori shelter had long been dogged by grim rumours, and the videos appeared to confirm them.

Activists have been raising concerns about poor living conditions and staff cruelty for years. This spring, the shelter even faced accusations of killing dogs on a large scale.

In April, footage spread across social media showing smoke rising from the Gori shelter’s crematorium at night. The person who filmed it claimed the crematorium had operated throughout the night and that a strong smell of burning hung over the site.

Animal rights activists suspected that staff were killing dogs in large numbers, including live animals. However, no convincing evidence emerged that anyone had burned animals alive, and the authorities never officially confirmed the allegations.

JAMnews covered the case in detail in an in-depth report on the mass capture of stray dogs and growing distrust of the state agencies responsible for their fate.

The October scandal was therefore far from the first time the Gori shelter had come under scrutiny. More than that, the events in Gori formed part of a much broader conflict between the state and animal rights activists, which has continued in Georgia throughout much of 2026.

Where do stray dogs disappear to?

In spring 2026, protests against the mass capture of stray dogs broke out in several Georgian cities. The demonstrations followed numerous reports of missing animals, including dogs that had been sterilised, vaccinated and cared for by so-called community carers — people who regularly feed, treat and look after strays without taking them into their homes.

A JAMnews report published on 23 May featured accounts from residents of different Georgian cities who were trying to find out what had happened to the dogs in their care and secure their return. In interviews with the publication, activists voiced fears that authorities were taking animals away from familiar surroundings and relocating them to places where they could not find food or water, effectively condemning them to die.

The authorities categorically deny allegations of mass killings. According to the official account, staff capture dogs as part of a state population management programme that includes veterinary examinations, sterilisation, vaccination and the subsequent return of animals to their habitat. Activists, however, say the programme captures all dogs, including those that underwent sterilisation long ago.

This raises one of the main contradictions. Under the programme’s rules, authorities cannot return animals to every location. Restrictions apply in areas near schools, kindergartens, medical facilities, markets and food outlets.

Yet stray dogs tend to live precisely around shops, markets and cafés. In cities such as Tbilisi, it would be difficult to find a street without a school, clinic or shop nearby. This raises an obvious question: where do the authorities take dogs that they cannot release at the places where they captured them? And who monitors what happens to the animals after they leave the shelter?

Animal rights activists who spoke to JAMnews say they have yet to secure a transparent, accessible system for tracking the fate of every captured animal.

Countless strays

Nobody knows exactly how many stray dogs live in Georgia. Despite the problem having persisted for decades, the country still lacks reliable nationwide statistics.

Relatively reliable figures exist only for Tbilisi, where the municipal Animal Monitoring Agency tracks the stray animal population. According to figures from the agency cited by JAMnews, the Georgian capital had around 29,676 stray dogs in 2025.

Animal rights activists estimate that Georgia could have hundreds of thousands of stray animals, but independent nationwide counts have yet to verify that figure.

The scale of the problem is also reflected in public attitudes. According to a CRRC Georgia poll for the National Democratic Institute (NDI), conducted in October 2023, 22% of respondents considered stray animals one of the country’s main social problems.

This comes as little surprise. Stray dogs are a familiar sight on Georgia’s streets. People encounter them near shops, markets, bus stops, residential courtyards and tourist areas. Many dogs wear special tags on their ears, indicating that they have undergone registration and veterinary procedures. Local residents and tourists often feed them.

However, peaceful coexistence between people and animals does not always work. Reports of dog attacks on people regularly emerge in Georgia, while the risk of rabies remains a public health concern. Calls to control the stray dog population and protect public safety therefore have a real basis.

Simply removing dogs from the streets, however, does not stop the population from growing. As long as pet dogs continue to breed without control and people abandon unwanted puppies, new animals will take the place of those authorities capture.

New laws, old problems

In 2025, Georgia’s parliament passed a law on pets intended to establish a unified legal framework for their care, registration and breeding control. In February 2026, the government approved a dedicated programme to manage the overpopulation of dogs.

The programme centres on an approach known as CNVR: capture, neuter, vaccinate and return. The World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) also describes this approach in its guidelines. When properly implemented, it can gradually reduce animal populations without resorting to mass culling.

However, the way authorities carry out each stage is crucial. Sterilisation must cover a substantial proportion of the population, vaccination must prevent the spread of disease, and the relocation and release of animals must take their welfare and public safety into account.

Georgian animal rights activists have raised numerous concerns about how the authorities implement these measures. They accuse state agencies of lacking transparency, mistreating animals, violating shelter standards and failing to monitor what happens to animals after their capture.

The overall effectiveness of government policy has also come under scrutiny. The authorities have tried to tackle the problem before, regularly announcing tenders over the years for sterilisation campaigns targeting stray animals in the regions. Yet the scale of the problem suggests that these programmes have failed to deliver significant results.

According to animal rights activists, private individuals still carry out much of the sterilisation work in practice. Animal carers and volunteers pay for operations, specialist non-governmental organisations take part, and volunteers from European countries travel to Georgia to help run sterilisation campaigns. Activists say state programmes reach far fewer animals than necessary, and they also question the quality of the work.

“Let the dog go”: where stray animals come from

Another serious problem is irresponsible ownership. In Georgia, people even use the common expression “let the dog go” to describe a practice in which owners take unwanted animals far from home and abandon them in a forest or by the roadside.

In rural areas, owners may abandon a dog because it hunts domestic poultry or otherwise “misbehaves”.

Energetic breeds that need plenty of attention and exercise are particularly vulnerable, as are hunting dogs that fail to meet their owners’ expectations. Meanwhile, effective controls on animal breeding remain largely absent.

The legal framework to tackle such practices already exists. Georgia’s 2025 Law on Pets explicitly prohibits owners from abandoning their animals and requires them to register their pets, partly to prevent such cases.

The law also introduces restrictions on dog breeding. Since July 2026, a three-year moratorium on breeding certain breeds has been in force.

The footage from the Gori shelter offers a glimpse of how effectively these rules work in practice. If the authorities properly enforced the law, many of the puppies found there — along with the hundreds of other emaciated and abandoned animals that people encounter along Georgian roads — might never have ended up on the streets.

Diana Petriashvili, Mediaset

Gori shelter

World.title: “No to torture!” Saturday march in Tbilisi. “Protests in Georgia” video podcast
World.content:
The “Saturday marches” are part of an ongoing protest movement that has continued in Georgia for 689 days.

Protesters are demanding that Georgia return to the path of European integration and that all political prisoners be released. They are also calling for the repeal of all anti-democratic laws passed by the ruling Georgian Dream party over the past two years.

Protesters and opposition parties point out that part of Georgian society still does not recognise the results of the parliamentary election held in autumn 2024. They are calling for early parliamentary elections.

Over the course of nearly two years of protests, dozens of people have been arrested. Many have been charged with criminal offences and sentenced to prison.

For the first time in independent Georgia’s history, the country has around 150 prisoners of conscience, including women. Among them is Mzia Amaglobeli, founder of the independent media outlets Batumelebi and Netgazeti. She was sentenced to two years in prison for slapping a police officer.

The protests continue despite an intensifying crackdown on civil society and the media.

World.title: Georgia: Billionaire Ivanishvili meets ruling party leaders – what is known about their talks after silent video release
World.content:
Ivanishvili Georgian Dream meeting

On 17 October, a rare political event took place in Georgia.

Bidzina Ivanishvili, founder and honorary chairman of the ruling Georgian Dream party, chaired a meeting of the party’s political council, followed by a meeting of the parliamentary majority, at the party’s central office.

This was the first public appearance in several months by Ivanishvili, whom many consider Georgia’s “shadow” ruler.

Yet it could hardly be called an “appearance”. Ivanishvili himself said nothing to journalists. The party’s press office released only silent footage of the meetings.

What was discussed behind closed doors became known through three sources: Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze’s briefing, the party’s written statement, and a brief comment by parliamentary majority leader Irakli Kirtskhalia.

Kobakhidze emphasised that Ivanishvili had expressed “pain” over his former team-mates who are in prison. This likely refers primarily to former Prime Minister Irakli Gharibashvili, who for many years was considered Bidzina Ivanishvili’s closest and most loyal ally but has now been convicted of large-scale corruption.

However, in the party’s statement, this issue is presented in a different tone.

It is stated that corruption problems within the team have been “fully and effectively” overcome.

While the meetings were underway, citizens protested outside the building under the slogan “Georgia against Ivanishvili”. One of the banners read, “Supporting Georgian Dream = betraying the country”, while another said, “14 bloody years”, referring to the years Georgian Dream has been in power.

Who joined the political council

The only publicly announced decision from the meetings was to expand the political council. Parliamentary majority leader Irakli Kirtskhalia and Zurab Pataradze, head of the government of the Autonomous Republic of Ajara, joined the body.

Footage released by the press office shows Ivanishvili entering the meeting, shaking hands with MPs and taking his seat. Irakli Kobakhidze, parliamentary speaker Shalva Papuashvili, Tbilisi Mayor Kakha Kaladze and Irakli Kirtskhalia sat beside him at the head table. Ministers were also present.

According to Kobakhidze, both meetings addressed current domestic and foreign policy issues. The party statement referred to “political and economic processes” in the country. It also said time was devoted to initiatives and reforms recently announced by the government.

The context behind Ivanishvili’s meetings with ruling party leaders

Bidzina Ivanishvili rarely appears in public. He has been under US sanctions since 2024.

His participation in party meetings on 17 October came amid an apparent crisis within the government.

Former senior Georgian Dream officials have been arrested one after another on corruption charges.

The most high-profile case involves former Prime Minister Irakli Gharibashvili.

In January 2026, he was sentenced to five years in prison under a plea agreement. In August, prosecutors brought a new bribery charge against him.

Gharibashvili has been publishing letters from prison in which he accuses Irakli Kobakhidze and former Deputy Prime Minister Mamuka Mdinaradze. On August 27, Mamuka Mdinaradze resigned from his post and announced his departure from politics. He denied any connection to the letters.

Another important factor in the context of Ivanishvili’s meeting with ruling party leaders is that the Constitutional Court is due to hear the authorities’ case seeking to ban opposition parties in just a few days.

According to opposition representatives, hearings were scheduled for October 21, 22 and 23. In response, an alliance of nine opposition parties announced a rally in Tbilisi on 25 October under the slogan “Georgia without Ivanishvili. Georgia deserves better.”

Gharibashvili is Ivanishvili’s “heartache” – and the statement about “overcoming difficulties”

After the meetings at the ruling party’s office, journalists asked Irakli Kobakhidze whether the possibility of releasing former Prime Minister Irakli Gharibashvili from prison had been discussed.

Kobakhidze replied that there had not. According to him, Ivanishvili gave a general assessment of “the developments”.

“For all of us, including, of course, first and foremost, Bidzina Ivanishvili, what happened is painful, when events unfold this way and former members of the team are serving sentences for specific crimes (…)”, Kobakhidze said.

He added: “What happened is regrettable. It was, of course, something of a blow to the team.”

Gharibashvili was sentenced to five years in prison in January 2026 following a plea agreement. In August, prosecutors brought a new charge against him. According to the prosecution, the former prime minister accepted 750,000 lari (about $290,000) in bribes.

Gharibashvili’s lawyers say he denies the new charge.

There is no mention of “heartache” in the party statement’s account of the same subject. According to the statement, Ivanishvili reviewed the corruption challenges the team had faced in the past and said that “as a result of the effective work of the prime minister, the government team and the security apparatus, these challenges have been fully and effectively overcome”.

Kobakhidze: “Friendship is none of your business“

Kobakhidze said the team had also discussed Mamuka Mdinaradze, a former deputy prime minister who previously served as head of the State Security Service.

Mdinaradze resigned from his post on August 27 and announced his departure from politics. At the time, he denied that his resignation was connected to Garibashvili’s letters published from prison.

Kobakhidze declined to elaborate publicly. “Mamuka Mdinaradze has left politics”, he said, adding that he did not consider it appropriate to bring the issue to the fore in these circumstances. He said he remained in occasional contact with Mdinaradze. He did not give a direct answer when asked whether they were still friends.

“Why are you asking about friendship? Friendship is none of your business”, he told journalists.

Journalists also raised the issue of a controversial social media post by Georgian Dream party member Dito Samkharadze, who wrote that “rats” [informers] had been identified within the ruling party.”

Kobakhidze was asked whether Samkharadze also meant Mdinaradze and whether legal proceedings against him were expected.

“I don’t know what you’re referring to,” the prime minister replied. He said there was “no basis whatsoever” for such speculation.

Parliamentary majority leader Kirtskhalia: “Ivanishvili spoke mostly about Kobakhidze“

Journalists asked Irakli Kirtskhalia to comment on growing public speculation that Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze could soon resign.

According to him, Ivanishvili devoted more time to Kobakhidze than to anyone else, “expressing support and praise, which the entire team, of course, shares”.

“Ivanishvili said that the government is performing very well under Kobakhidze’s leadership, and that not only is there no reason for his resignation, but every day confirms that he is the best prime minister,” Kirtskhalia said.

He described the resignation rumours as gossip spread by the opposition.

Scandal over possible corruption in spending on the Patriarch’s funeral

At a press briefing, Irakli Kobakhidze addressed the main political issue: allegations of possible corruption in spending on the Patriarch’s funeral.

He said preliminary information from the Government Administration showed “no indication of any improper expenditure”. He also said a large portion of the allocated funds had been returned.

In September, speaking on Rustavi 2, Kobakhidze provided specific figures: according to preliminary data, 722,000 lari (about $275,000) of the 3 million lari (about $1,100,000) allocated had been spent. The questions he answered concerned former Culture Minister Tika Rukhadze’s possible involvement in the alleged embezzlement.

Kobakhidze said detailed information would be presented to the public in the near future. Asked whether investigative agencies should look into the matter, he replied:

“First, we will present detailed information to you, and if any questions remain on this issue, let us discuss them together.”

“Whatever they call us, we keep winning” – Kobakhidze on media restrictions

Irakli Kobakhidze also commented on restrictions on the use of various words and expressions in the media adopted by the Communications Commission.

On 9 October, Transparency International – Georgia reported that the Communications Commission had objected to expressions used by independent TV channels Formula and Pirveli. The commission compiled a list of 93 words and phrases that it banned from use, including “regime”, “oligarch” and “prime minister appointed by Ivanishvili”, according to TI. Fines for using words on the list were increased to 10,000 lari (nearly $4,000).

Kobakhidze explained the decision as necessary to uphold the principle of objectivity.

He said these rules had existed in legislation for years, but an enforcement mechanism had not previously been in place. News programmes are now required to maintain neutrality.

That requirement does not apply to programmes expressing their hosts’ own views, Prime Minister said.

“Nothing bothers us. We win elections and emerge victorious from every political confrontation. Whether they call us a regime or a dictatorship, we win either way”, Kobakhidze said.

News in Georgia

World.title: Uzbekistan, US-based Nasdaq review stock exchange upgrade plans
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 20. Uzbekistan’s National Agency for Perspective Projects (NAPP) and the Tashkent Republican Stock Exchange discussed modernizing the country’s stock market infrastructure with Nasdaq during a meeting in Samarkand on October 19.

This was reflected in the statement by the Republican Stock Exchange Tashkent, following a meeting on the sidelines of the U.S.-Uzbekistan Business and Investment Council sessions held within the C5+1 framework, which brings together the United States and five Central Asian countries.

The discussions focused on plans to upgrade the Tashkent Stock Exchange’s trading, clearing, brokerage and market surveillance systems. The parties reviewed progress on the exchange’s request-for-proposals (RFP) process and explored available technological solutions.

Nasdaq proposed arranging an on-site visit to study the operations of the Stockholm Stock Exchange, including its trading, clearing, brokerage, depository and market surveillance systems, as well as the technologies used to integrate these functions.

The proposed visit would allow Uzbek representatives to examine the practical application of modern stock market infrastructure and assess potential solutions for the exchange’s modernization project.

The meeting is expected to inform the ongoing selection of technology providers under the RFP process.

Nasdaq is a U.S.-based financial technology company that operates stock exchanges and provides trading technology, market surveillance, clearing-related solutions and other services to financial market operators worldwide. Its technology is used by exchanges and financial institutions in multiple countries.

World.title: Kazakhstan, Belarus to pilot electronic road transport permits in 2027
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 20. Kazakhstan and Belarus have agreed to establish a joint working group on electronic permits for international road transport by the end of 2026 and conduct a pilot project in 2027, according to the Ministry of Transport of Kazakhstan.

The agreements were reached at a meeting of the Kazakhstan-Belarus Joint Commission on International Road Transport in Astana. The parties discussed bilateral and transit freight transportation, as well as further steps to digitize the permit system.

The pilot project will focus on the use of electronic permits for international road transport. The transition to an electronic format is expected to reduce administrative procedures, improve transparency in transportation and speed up document processing.

The parties also discussed prospects for introducing an unlimited quota for international road transport permits.

To meet carriers’ needs, Kazakhstan and Belarus agreed to exchange an additional 5,000 permits for international road transport in 2026. A preliminary quota of 50,000 permits was agreed for 2027.

The decisions are intended to create additional opportunities for international freight transportation and support trade and economic ties between the two countries.

The meeting also highlighted sustained growth in freight transportation between Kazakhstan and Belarus and the importance of both countries in developing international transport corridors.

Following the meeting, the parties reaffirmed their interest in strengthening cooperation in road transport, improving conditions for international transportation and further developing bilateral transport links.

World.title: Uzbekistan’s TMK proposes metal recovery project with U.S. firm
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 20. Uzbekistan Technological Metals Complex (TMK) has proposed a joint project with U.S. company Metallica Commodities to recover valuable minerals and metals from industrial waste during a meeting on October 19 in Samarkand.

This was reflected in the statement by the TMK, following a meeting between TMK representatives and Adrian Bazilio, Metallica Commodities’ managing director for trade and operations in Africa.

The talks focused on the potential use of the U.S. company’s industrial waste processing technology to recover valuable materials from TMK’s production waste.

TMK proposed implementing joint projects based on the technology at its Kelajak Metallari technology park. The initiative also prompted discussions on assessing opportunities to process industrial waste across Uzbekistan and other Central Asian countries.

The sides expressed interest in further examining the project’s technological and practical feasibility and agreed to work together on evaluating its implementation.

The discussions remain at the assessment stage, with further technical evaluation expected to determine the project's feasibility.

Metallica Commodities Corp. is a U.S.-based metals and minerals trading company specializing in ferrous and nonferrous metals, mineral resources and industrial byproducts. Its activities also include mineral asset development and metal recovery from secondary materials, including electronic waste. The company’s experience in metals trading and recycling is relevant to the proposed project with TMK to assess the recovery of valuable materials from industrial waste.

World.title: Azerbaijan warns of lack of control over data uploaded to AI tools
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 20. Employees in government institutions use artificial intelligence (AI) tools; however, there is no mechanism in place to monitor the data that these employees input into these AI tools, Head of Department at the State Service for Special Communication and Information Security of Azerbaijan, Lieutenant General Nadir Novruzov, said at the 8th Summit of Heads of Information Security for State Institutions in Baku on Tuesday, Trend’s correspondent reports from the event.

Novruzov pointed out that even instances such as the leakage of voice data to external AI solutions are often overlooked.

"Even if we implement controls over certain AI tools, for example, by setting up proxies, employees may find that a specific task is blocked by these proxies. In such cases, they will simply turn to other AI tools. These tools, which operate outside our oversight, are referred to as 'shadow AI'," he explained.

The primary objective of the summit is to foster the exchange of experience among the heads of information security within state institutions, strengthen cooperation in the fields of information security and cybersecurity, and discuss pressing issues related to modern technological challenges and the application of artificial intelligence.

The summit will cover topics such as the integration of artificial intelligence into public administration and digital infrastructure, the opportunities it presents, emerging cyber threats, the implementation of principles for a reliable and secure digital state, data management, as well as the identification, assessment, and management of information security and cybersecurity risks.

World.title: KAZ Minerals, China's NFC explore joint mineral surveys in Kazakhstan
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 20. KAZ Minerals and China Nonferrous Metal Industry's Foreign Engineering and Construction Co., Ltd. (NFC), a subsidiary of China Nonferrous Metal Mining Group (CNMC), have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on cooperation in geological exploration, according to KAZ Minerals.

"The Memorandum provides for exploring opportunities to apply advanced technologies to the exploration and evaluation of Kazakhstan’s mineral resources," the company said.

The memorandum expands the scope of cooperation between the companies and reflects KAZ Minerals’ efforts to advance mineral exploration in Kazakhstan. The parties plan to establish a joint working group to coordinate further activities and develop a roadmap for cooperation.

KAZ Minerals is a copper-focused mining company operating large-scale, low-cost open-pit and underground mines in Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan.

Its key assets include the Aktogay copper mine in Kazakhstan’s Abay region, which has sulfide processing plants producing copper concentrate and an oxide plant producing cathode copper; the Bozshakol open-pit copper mine in Pavlodar region; the Bozymchak copper-gold mine in Kyrgyzstan, which transitioned to underground mining in 2024; and the East Region operations in Kazakhstan, comprising three underground mines and two processing plants producing copper, zinc, silver and gold.

World.title: Uzbekistan's My Freighter secures UK approval for cargo flights
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 20. Uzbekistan-based cargo airline My Freighter has received approval to operate cargo flights to the United Kingdom after being designated an ACC3 carrier by the UK Department for Transport, the company said on October 14.

This was reflected in the statement by My Freighter.

The designation confirms that the airline’s cargo security procedures meet UK aviation security requirements for transporting freight from airports outside the country.

ACC3 status is mandatory for airlines carrying cargo and mail into the United Kingdom from third-country airports. It requires carriers to ensure that shipments undergo security screening in accordance with UK standards before departure.

The approval will allow My Freighter to offer cargo transportation services between Tashkent and the UK, providing shippers and freight forwarders in Uzbekistan and the wider region with another route to the British market.

The company, part of Centrum Holding, said flights to the United Kingdom would begin soon, with the schedule to be announced separately.

My Freighter specializes in air cargo transportation and operates from Uzbekistan as part of Centrum Holding’s logistics and aviation business. The company has been developing its international route network to connect markets in Asia and Europe.

The ACC3 designation marks a regulatory step toward expanding the airline’s operations in the UK market. The company has not yet announced the launch date, flight frequency or destinations in the United Kingdom.

World.title: Azerbaijan's green energy to boost Caspian-Europe ties – South Korean envoy
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 20. The development of renewable energy in Azerbaijan and the strengthening of energy connectivity between the Caspian region and Europe could open up new opportunities for regional cooperation and sustainable development, Ambassador of South Korea to Azerbaijan, Kang Kymgu, said at the conference "Middle Corridor and prospects of Eurasian transport connectivity: Azerbaijan and Korea" in Baku on Tuesday, Trend’s correspondent reports from the event.

According to Kymgu, Korea follows developments in the South Caucasus with particular interest, as Korea and Azerbaijan share similarities in their geopolitical positioning, and both nations face challenges stemming from complex regional dynamics.

Noting that Azerbaijan and Armenia initialed a peace agreement in August 2025, the ambassador described this as a significant step toward ensuring long-term peace and stability in the region.

"Since then, positive changes have emerged, and efforts to consolidate peace and foster regional cooperation have continued. These developments could create new opportunities for regional connectivity and draw greater attention to the Middle Corridor," he said.

The diplomat emphasized that the Middle Corridor is evolving into an extensive connectivity network, encompassing not only trade and logistics but also energy and digital infrastructure.

"In this context, Azerbaijan’s growing focus on renewable energy deserves special attention. Building upon its experience in the traditional energy sector, Azerbaijan is implementing new initiatives to develop renewable energy sources and strengthen energy connectivity between the Caspian region and Europe," the ambassador noted.

Kymgu referred to a World Bank report published in September 2026, according to which strategic investments in the Middle Corridor could more than triple trade volumes and halve transit times by 2040. According to him, the report also highlights the corridor's potential for driving economic growth and regional integration.

"As global supply chains shift under the influence of geopolitical uncertainty, the importance of reliable and diversified transport links continues to grow. The Middle Corridor opens up new opportunities for cooperation among countries in the South Caucasus, Central Asia, and Northeast Asia, including Korea.

For Korea, whose economic development is closely tied to international trade and global connectivity, these opportunities are of particular significance," he explained.

In conclusion, the ambassador expressed his confidence that the conference would serve as another meaningful step in the development of academic exchange between Korea and Azerbaijan, and would contribute to strengthening the ties between the two nations.

The Middle Corridor is a multimodal trade and transport route connecting Asia and Europe through Central Asia, the Caspian Sea, Azerbaijan, Georgia and Türkiye. The route begins in China and runs through Central Asia before crossing the Caspian Sea and continuing through Azerbaijan, Georgia and Türkiye to European markets.

The Middle Corridor is being developed as an alternative to traditional northern and southern transport routes, providing connectivity between Asian markets, including China, and Europe.

World.title: Eni launches start-up activities at Egypt's Meleiha Phase 2 gas project
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 20. Italian energy company Eni has launched start-up activities at the Meleiha Phase 2 (MP2) project in Egypt’s Western Desert, marking a milestone in the development of a new gas hub within the Merged Meleiha concession, the company said on October 20.

The project will increase gas processing capacity in the area and support the growth of domestic natural gas production. The new facility is designed to process up to 100 million standard cubic feet of gas per day.

“Meleiha Phase 2” includes an integrated infrastructure system comprising development wells, gathering systems, trunklines and a dedicated gas export pipeline. The facilities will connect new production to Egypt’s existing gas infrastructure, enabling the “rapid monetization of resources and enhanced operational efficiency,” according to Eni.

The company said the project confirms its role as “a strategic partner of Egypt” and reaffirms its long-standing commitment to contributing to the country’s energy security through the development of the Western Desert’s resources.

The project is also expected to increase natural gas availability on the domestic market. Eni said it had been developed in accordance with the “highest standards of operational excellence, safety and environmental sustainability.”

Eni has been present in Egypt since 1954 and is currently the country’s leading energy producer. Its equity hydrocarbon production in Egypt averaged approximately 242,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day in 2025.

Through its subsidiaries and joint ventures, Eni operates across the energy value chain, with exploration, development and production activities in the Western Desert, the Gulf of Suez, the Nile Delta and the Eastern Mediterranean.

World.title: Landholders and politicians push for tougher laws on renewable energy developments
World.content:
A coalition of rural community groups is demanding tougher laws governing renewable energy developments, including mandatory turbine setbacks, stricter decommissioning rules and stronger protections for neighbouring landholders.

Regional Voices Queensland (RVQ), a loose alliance of about 12 community action groups representing communities affected by renewable energy projects across the state, brought landholders, farming industry representatives and politicians together for its first major meeting today at the Franz family farm beside the Wambo Wind Farm at Diamondy, 280 kilometres north-west of Brisbane.

The meeting, co-organised by Member for Maranoa David Littleproud, focused on reforms to planning laws, with more than 70 participants travelling from communities including the Southern Downs and other parts of regional Queensland.

Regional Voices Queensland members are demanding tougher laws governing renewable energy developments. (ABC Southern Qld: Brandon Long)

RVQ chair and Property Rights Australia board member, Jim Willmott, described the alliance as a "supergroup" formed after community organisations dealing with individual projects identified common concerns.

"What we found is a lot of community groups were dealing with individual projects themselves, but they all had the same common issues," Mr Willmott said.

The group is calling for a minimum 3-kilometre setback from residences and up-front decommissioning bonds.

Queensland's wind farm code has not allowed developers to comply simply by meeting a specified separation distance since 2024.

Projects must meet all of the code's performance outcomes, including noise criteria at neighbouring dwellings.

David Littleproud says affected landholders wanted clarity around the issue. (ABC Southern Qld: Brandon Long)

Mr Littleproud said affected landholders were seeking practical safeguards rather than opposing renewable energy outright.

"They're not asking for anything irrational," he said.

"They're actually being quite considered and it's coming from a lived experience."

Farm co-owner Glenn Franz, who does not host the turbines, said the experience of living beside the wind farm had highlighted gaps in existing protections, particularly around visual amenity and the financial risks associated with dismantling turbines at the end of their operational lives.

"We've got 13 wind turbines surrounding us within a 3km zone," Mr Franz said.

"There's got to be safeguards for the future.

"It'd be nice to have the security up front, not as a pay-as-you-go-down-the-track sort of scheme."

Karl Stefanovic interviewed landholders at the meeting. (ABC Southern Qld: Brandon Long)

The Wambo Wind Farm, a joint venture between state-owned Stanwell and energy infrastructure group Cubico, received planning approval in 2020.

Mr Franz said while the project was well advanced, other communities were at the start of the process and could learn from the Diamondy community's experience.

Anna Lethbridge and Brendan Taylor from AgForce attended the meeting. (ABC Southern Qld: Brandon Long)

AgForce policy adviser Anna Lethbridge said safeguards needed to extend beyond project hosts to neighbouring producers, including protections against contamination and impacts on agricultural accreditation.

"From an AgForce perspective, we're not opposed to renewables," Ms Lethbridge said.

" If you are going to host a project, you need to be fully informed of all the risks so you can make an informed decision. "

Queensland regulates wind farm developments through its planning and environmental assessment framework, including State Code 23 and applicable approval conditions.

Since 2025, new wind farm applications must undergo impact assessment and provide financial security for decommissioning.

However, RVQ is concerned the wording is vague and could still leave landholders or taxpayers liable.

Developers must now also negotiate a community benefit agreement with the relevant council before lodging an application.

World.title: Police believe underworld gang gave gun to 13yo charged over drive-by shooting
World.content:
WA police are investigating whether a 13-year-old Victorian boy allegedly involved in a drive-by shooting in suburban Perth on the weekend was recruited by an underworld organisation which gave him a self-loading firearm.

The boy allegedly used a semi-automatic rifle to fire more than 20 shots into a Gosnells house, hitting a bedroom window and wall, around 12:40am on Saturday.

Seven people were inside the home at the time, including children. One man received minor injuries from shattered glass, but no one was seriously hurt.

However, they are not thought to be the intended targets.

Loading...

Detectives believe the boy was recruited by an underworld organisation and given a pick-up and drop off location for the gun, the ABC understands.

The instructions are understood to have been delivered electronically.

The semi-automatic firearm involved in the incident has not been found.

The ABC understands his family had only moved him to WA weeks ago.

Rare weapon

Two semi-automatic rifles were used in the devastating Port Arthur massacre in 1996 in which 35 people were killed.

The Category D weapons have been outlawed in Western Australia ever since, captured as part of the sweeping reforms following the mass shooting.

The shooting left multiple bullet holes in the Gosnells home. (ABC News)

Only police, the military and certain government agencies are legally able to use the long-arm weapons.

WA Firearm Traders Association president Bevan Steele said the weapon allegedly used by the 13-year-old boy was "a highly illicit firearm" that could only have been smuggled into the country illegally.

"We haven't seen these firearms in WA, in the legal environment, since 1996 … if you had one of these on your dealer's license, it is gone, well and truly," Mr Steele said.

The upper floor of the Gosnells home was riddled with bullets. (ABC News)

In other states, Category D weapons are restricted to professional hunters, many of whom shoot out of aircraft.

Exactly how the lethal self-loading weapon allegedly got into the hands of a 13-year-old is not known.

"A 13-year-old boy having access to a weapon like that and carrying out that act, allegedly, is extremely concerning," said Police Minister Reece Whitby.

Police arrested the teenager on Monday and charged him with eight offences including unlawful use of a firearm, endangering life, possession of stolen property and no authority to drive.

He will reappear in Perth Children's Court next week.

World.title: Cumulative impacts of data centre gas plants overlooked, court hears
World.content:
A court has heard the "cumulative impacts" of a series of gas plants proposed to run data centres in the Southern Highlands are being ignored as a result of fragmented planning decisions.

Seven community members gave evidence at the site of the development in Moss Vale on Tuesday morning, kicking off a three-day hearing in the Land and Environment Court.

The court is considering developer Nakar Property's appeal of a refusal by Wingecarribee Shire Council for one of its projects on the site.

The application was for a 16-megawatt gas-fired power plant and battery storage system to power data centres.

Separately, the developer has secured approval for another gas-fired plant on the site, a 14MW facility, and is seeking state government approval for a third, 673MW plant.

More than 100 community members gathered on the site ahead of the Land and Environment Court hearing. (ABC Illawarra: Penny Burfitt)

A crowd of more than 100 community members, Land and Environment Court Commissioner Nicola Targett, and representatives for the council and the applicant gathered in an open field in Moss Vale for the first day of the hearing.

The first community member to address the court was Dane Shanahan, who introduced himself by his Gundungurra name, Mullyang.

The emerging knowledge-holder for the region's traditional landowners told the court his name meant "eagle" and, as he outlined his community's concerns about the project, two wedge-tailed eagles appeared in the sky above the open-air court.

After the proceedings, Mr Shanahan described the appearance of the birds as an "ancestral presence".

He was one of several speakers to urge the commissioner to consider the application for the 16MW facility in the broader context of the development.

"Each piece is being presented as small — each piece is being assessed on its own and no-one is looking at the whole," Mr Shanahan told the court.

The court is only assessing the appeal lodged by Nakar Property for the 16MW facility and battery, but Gabby Kent, who lives 1 kilometre from the proposed site, agreed with Mr Shanahan's argument.

"The planning processes may be separate, but the cumulative impacts to my family … and my community are not," she said.

Will McCarthy says the project needs to be looked at as a whole. (ABC Illawarra: Penny Burfitt)

Will McCarthy, whose home overlooks the development, echoed those sentiments.

"At some point the planning system needs to stand back at look at the development as a whole," he told the commissioner.

The court heard the applicant had submitted an amended plan for the development to speakers and parties ahead of the hearing.

That submission included changes such as painting exhaust stacks green to address visual amenity, and adding some onsite solar power generation.

Consultation challenged

Mr Shanahan told the court no Gundungurra people had been consulted as part of the development application's Aboriginal Heritage Assessment, despite the cultural significance of a waterway that would be cut off by the project.

"It is as significant to the Gundungurra as Genesis is to Christians," he said.

"The applicant has proposed to reshape an ancestral waterway without asking the people [whether] it will scar."

The power plant and battery would provide power to data centres on Cloud Carrier's Moss Vale site. (Supplied: Cloud Carrier)

Jacqueline Duc raised concerns about the health impacts of pollutants, telling the court carcinogens from gas power-plants had been linked to lung and childhood cancers.

She also raised concerns about the project being located within the Sydney water catchment, saying its tributaries eventually flowed into Warragamba Dam, which supplied 80 per cent of the city's drinking water.

The applicant's lawyer, James Smith, did not question any of the community speakers.

The court will hear from the applicant's attorney and the council's representative, Michael Staunton, in coming days.

World.title: New laws to prevent WA schools discriminating against LGBTQIA+ staff, students
World.content:
Religious schools will no longer be allowed to sack teachers or expel students due to their sexuality, or to reject students due to a disability, under new laws proposed by the Western Australian government.

Religious institutions, including schools, will still be allowed to discriminate based on religion, but not other grounds under a rewrite of the state's Equal Opportunity Act.

Attorney General Tony Buti said that would stop institutions discriminating against people in the LGBTQIA+ community.

"The exemption is purely on religion, not on sexual orientation," he said.

Tony Buti says religious schools will still be able to choose not to hire people based on their religion. (ABC News: Keane Bourke)

The proposed laws will also include broader protections against discriminating against a person's disabilities in all circumstances, including schools.

Felicity Creagh is a mother of two autistic children and said she was "relieved and encouraged" to see the government's proposed laws.

"For families like mine, this is about more than legislation. It means we have a greater chance of being heard, believed, and taken seriously," she said alongside Dr Buti at a press conference.

Felicity Creagh says the proposed laws will give her family the chance to be seen and heard. (ABC News: Keane Bourke)

"It means stronger protections when we ask for reasonable adjustments and accommodations for our children."

'Hate is not ok'

Dr Buti said the bill was the biggest overhaul of the state's anti-discrimination laws in more than 40 years, and would widen the scope of who was protected.

It will seek to outlaw discrimination against people who are homeless, exposed to domestic violence, who are pregnant or breastfeeding, or involved in union activity.

The proposed laws come after an initial tranche of laws in 2024 which the WA government implemented aimed at improving the lives of people in the LGBTQIA+ community.

Those laws removed the need to undergo medical or surgical reassignment to change a person's sex or gender, and abolished the state's Gender Reassignment Board which managed applications for gender changes.

The WA government's latest proposed overhaul follows Independent MP Allegra Spender's calls to reform federal laws which exempt religious institutions from the Sex Discrimination Act.

Roger Cook says nobody should face discrimination. (ABC News: Keane Bourke)

WA Premier Roger Cook said his message was clear: "Hate is not OK in WA."

"Anti-Semitism, Islamaphobia, discrimination, acts of violence or intimidation, have taken hold in Australia and in WA in recent times," he said.

"Nobody should face discrimination or abuse based on their race, religion, sexuality or disability."

Shadow Attorney General Nick Goiran said the opposition would carefully scrutinise the bill once it was introduced in parliament on Wednesday.

"The current Equal Opportunity Act is more than 200 pages, so it is reasonable to expect the government's proposed rewrite is at least as long," he said.

"In that context, the Opposition will carefully scrutinise the bill once it is introduced, consult with those impacted, and test the premier's assertion that these changes will bring Western Australia into line with other states."

World.title: Police probe WA woman's sudden death after random breath test
World.content:
Police are investigating a woman's sudden death after a roadside breath test in Western Australia's Midwest.

Geraldton Police were conducting random breath testing on Brand Highway in Mount Tarcoola, about 400 kilometres north of Perth, when the woman, aged in her 50s, was stopped just before 7pm on Monday.

A WA Police spokesperson said the woman was issued a driving prohibition notice and released from custody.

"Shortly afterwards, the woman began experiencing a medical issue," the spokesperson said.

"Police offered assistance; however, the offer was declined. As a precaution, officers contacted St John WA.

"A short time later, the woman became unresponsive."

Geraldton police were conducting random breath testing on Brand Highway. (ABC News: Sissy Reyes)

The spokesperson said officers at the gave the woman first aid until paramedics arrived about 10 minutes after the initial call from police.

A St John Ambulance spokesperson said the woman was taken to Geraldton Regional Hospital under priority one conditions, arriving just after 8.20pm, but was later declared dead.

Police said the incident was being treated as a death in police presence, with the Internal Affairs Unit overseeing the probe.

A report will be prepared for the coroner.

World.title: WA woman's 'harrowing' ordeal stranded in Bali hospital after fall
World.content:
A West Australian grandmother is facing a potential bill of $100,000 to return home to Australia after falling down stairs at a Bali restaurant.

Estelle Ravenscroft, 79, and her husband Keith remain in Bali, where Ms Ravenscroft is in the intensive care unit at a local hospital.

Ms Ravenscroft broke both her legs in the fall.

The harrowing ordeal has been exacerbated by mounting medical expenses as Ms Ravenscroft is not covered by insurance.

Mr Ravenscroft said it was difficult to obtain travel insurance, because of their age.

Indonesia is not among the 11 countries with which Australia has a reciprocal arrangement for publicly-funded emergency care.

Fight for life

Ms Ravenscroft's family said the 79-year-old had gone for lunch at a restaurant and fallen down the stairs, which had no rails.

Speaking this morning, Mr Ravenscroft said his wife had pulled through after a nine-hour operation at a local hospital.

"It's been stressful and harrowing," he said.

"She's sitting up now, but there are some difficulties breathing, and issues with transfusions, but she's pulled through the operation OK, which is really fantastic."

Estelle Ravenscroft broke multiple bones when she fell at a restaurant. (Supplied: Leonie Walsh)

The couple's family has appealed to the community for help with expenses through an online fundraising website.

"It's way, way, way beyond what we could have imagined," Mr Ravenscroft said.

Travel insurance costs soar

Mr Ravenscroft said travel insurance was increasingly difficult to obtain as people aged.

"When you get a certain age, you'll find having the insurances that you think you can have, are not available," he said.

"I'd prefer not to go into that, because I'm here at the moment to make sure that my wife is OK. I want to get her home. The family wants to get her home."

Ms Ravenscroft's sister Marilyn Jones said the family was grateful for the support offered by the WA community.

Estelle Ravenscroft was on holiday with her husband in Bali when she fell at a restaurant. (Supplied: Marilyn Jones)

"The amount daily is climbing," she said.

Ms Jones said she was aware of commentary around the couple's lack of adequate travel insurance.

"It's pulled us down terribly," she said.

"There are some not very nice people out there, but there are also some wonderful people out there.

" So we're just hoping that people can feel her pain. "

Shop around for insurance

National Seniors Australia chief executive Chris Grice urged older Australians to investigate all options for travel insurance before travelling overseas.

"It's hard enough for folk to navigate the health system in Australia," he said.

''So I just feel so badly for someone who is caught in a foreign land, who perhaps can't get home because of the costs involved."

He said he was aware of seniors who struggled to get travel insurance as they aged, but urged people to persist.

"It depends on age and existing conditions," he said.

"It doesn't mean they can't get cover. It all depends on how they are being treated."

He said people needed to try and speak directly to an insurer, rather than apply online, if they had concerns.

An Insurance Council of Australia spokesperson said its thoughts were with the Ravenscrofts and acknowledged the strain many households were under.

"While cost of living is putting pressure on household budgets, a single overseas medical emergency, evacuation, or trip cancellation can cost far more than the premium of even a comprehensive policy," she said.

World.title: Batchelor homeless shelter concerned it has 'lost contact' with residents
World.content:
Mission Australia says it may have "lost contact" with some residents moved to a new homeless shelter in Batchelor after the closure of a 400-bed facility in Darwin, while a domestic violence service is reporting "increased presentations".

The last of those living at the YiSSA short-stay facility were bussed to the town of about 500 people 100 kilometres south of the Northern Territory capital last week after the NT government rejected a Commonwealth offer to help buy the site.

Mission Australia says a long-term solution beyond the Batchelor site's 19-month lease is needed. (ABC News: Tilda Colling)

Speaking to the media today, NT Children and Families Minister Robyn Cahill said just 23 people had taken up the offer to relocate to the Batchelor Transitional Facility (BTF).

Mission Australia runs the BTF and NT director Paul Royce said the organisation had helped with the transition to the new 90-bed facility in the outback town.

"A number of people we know have moved in with family, a number of people have returned to country, but we do worry we've lost contact with some people," he said.

Paul Royce says one man considered going to jail rather than having to leave Darwin. (ABC News: Pete Garnish)

"We were speaking with a gentleman at YiSSA who was contemplating holding up a bottle shop so he could get accommodation in jail for another six months, he saw that as a viable alternative to going to Batchelor," he said.

"We always spoke about the long-term solution for homelessness, we know this is not the solution in Batchelor, it's a much smaller facility."

Mission Australia currently has four staff working alongside the Department of Children and Families in the Batchelor facility, trying to transition people out of homelessness.

But Dr Royce emphasised the need for longer-term solutions past the end of the 19-month lease for the Batchelor site.

It follows the introduction of the NT government's new public housing policy this week, allowing tenants to be evicted after a single "significant" breach.

Lia Finocchiaro says the Batchelor residents will "get a beautiful double bed and a TV". (ABC News: Pete Garnish)

Speaking on Mix 104.9 yesterday, Chief Minister Lia Finocchiaro said she was not concerned that the policy could see more vulnerable people on the streets.

"Because we have a lovely new facility out at Batchelor where homeless people can go and you'll get a beautiful double bed and a TV and an ensuite, it'll be great," she said.

"We will be dealing with those people as we do and homeless people will be given the opportunity at Batchelor."

'Antithesis' of reducing crime

Top End Women's Legal Service chief executive Caitlin Weatherby-Fell said it was "outrageous" that the BTF was expected to alleviate homelessness.

"We've had increased presentations from women seeking emergency and crisis accommodation, presenting with increased risk and needing safety planning to ensure they and their children are safe from violence," she said.

Caitlin Wetherby-Fell says the government does not appear to understand the impact of homelessness. (ABC RN: Kristina Kukolja)

"When women and children are exited into homelessness, it makes them far more vulnerable to family and domestic violence.

"It's compounding the problem we are already seeing in the territory, where we continue to see the highest rates of violence in the country.

"This appears to be a government that doesn't understand the impact of homelessness on the community at large.

" For a government who are set upon a reducing crime strategy, this is certainly the antithesis to meeting that goal. "

Domestic Violence Prevention Minister Robyn Cahill was contacted for comment but did not respond by deadline.

Local Labor member for Batchelor Dheran Young said the town's residents also held concerns about access to services for BTF residents, particularly domestic and family violence programs.

Dheran Young says the decision to move residents to Batchelor was "completely inappropriate". (ABC News: Pete Garnish)

"Obviously there can be clear links between homelessness and crime but that is out of people being put in very vulnerable situations and not having a home for themselves," he said.

"The future of the facility of YiSSA needs to be back in Darwin, the services are in Darwin.

"It is completely inappropriate to send people down to Batchelor."

World.title: November 1 is looming. But Sam Walker is keeping contract talks on hold
World.content:
SportNRLRugby League World Cup November 1 is looming. But Sam Walker is keeping contract talks on hold Nick Wright October 20, 2026 — 7:09pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Kangaroos debutant Sam Walker says he has put all thoughts of his club future on hold until after he makes his Test debut for Australia. The premiership-winning Roosters halfback is set to line up in the green and gold for the first time on Sunday as part of a new-look halves pairing with Tom Dearden, with Cameron Munster named on the bench and Mitchell Moses’ World Cup campaign over due to a leg injury. Sam Walker in Brisbane at Kangaroos training on Tuesday. Getty Images Walker will become one of the hottest properties on the open market if he hasn’t inked an extension with the Tricolours come the November 1 free agency deadline. The 24-year-old has said he hopes to sign a new Roosters deal before then, with his camp reportedly seeking close to $1.7 million a season over four years from 2028. The Roosters are reportedly prepared to offer Walker around $1.5 million a season.



Now with an NRL premiership and three Maroons caps on his resume, Walker is poised to become one of the highest-paid players in the game. But he’s determined not to let his contract situation distract him from his looming Kangaroos debut. “There’s no looking at that at the moment,” walker said on Tuesday. “My goal is completely on Sunday, and once that all happens I’ll be able to sit down and have a good look about it. Sam Walker celebrates with Roosters fans after winning the grand final. Getty Images “But at the moment, my goal is to represent Australia and get that jersey done first.” Walker and Dearden came up through the Broncos’ academy together, but have not played alongside each other at the scrum base. Walker replaced an injured Dearden (syndesmosis) for this year’s State of Origin series, in which he starred in game one and claimed man of the match honours in game two.



Munster is expected to come straight back into the No.6 jumper after being given a rest against Fiji at Suncorp Stadium on Sunday, but Walker was not viewing the battle in Brisbane as a shootout between him and Dearden for the right to join the Melbourne Storm champion in the halves. “We’ve almost grown up with each other, our families have known each other for a very long time, and Tommy and I have been mates for a long time,” Walker said. Loading “There’s no talk about that [a shootout]. Whatever is best for the Australian side – we’re really clear on that. Our focus at the moment is Sunday, and putting our best foot forward for our country.” In another world, Walker could have been wearing England colours at the World Cup, having been born in Leeds, but he joked that his family “would’ve killed me if I represented anyone other than Australia”.



Related Article Rugby League World Cup Is the Kangaroos battle with Walsh heating up? Not in Tedesco’s eyes Walker has had to overcome plenty of obstacles to don the green and gold, most recently a syndesmosis injury suffered in round 26 that could easily have ended his season. Incredibly, he was cleared to return for the Roosters’ preliminary final against the Dolphins barely a month later, putting himself firmly in the frame to succeed the injured Nathan Cleary and Moses. “I had to work really hard there for about a month and sacrificed a lot. I had to work really hard at my rehab and make sure I could put myself back in the best position for the Roosters,” Walker said. “I’m really proud of the team at the Roosters for getting into a position where I could allow myself to come back because we had a coupe of weeks there where it was knockout footy.



“I was really confident [I would come back], once they gave me the timeline of when I could possibly get back on the field I had a really clear goal and set my targets on that.” Walker will feature in a new-look spine against Fiji, with he and Dearden joined by fullback James Tedesco (replacing Reece Walsh) and hooker Blayke Brailey, who makes his own Test debut with Harry Grant rested. Blayke Brailey will make his debut for Australia on Sunday, having toured in last year’s Ashes but not played. Getty Images Brailey established himself as one of the more creative dummy-halves in the NRL this season, earning his maiden NSW call-up in the process and managing 15 try assists and 14 linebreak assists in Cronulla’s run to the semi-finals. The 28-year-old was adamant that his style would not clash with Walker’s, with both players eager to attack when they sensed an opportunity.



Related Article NRL 2026 62 tries in 53 games: The attacking phenom leading World Cup’s NRL hopefuls “I know he plays ad-lib, he likes to be off the cuff, he likes to be all-out attack – so hopefully that complements my game well,” Brailey said. “I think the way he moves and the way he plays [suits me]. I was a half myself, and I kind of know where he’s going to be and how he’s going to play, so hopefully we do link up and really connect. “In this team, what you see you back yourself. I know Kevvie will give us full rein where whatever you see, you take … it’s a luxury we have in our team where we have so much strike.”

The NSW Liberal MP whose 690-word speech sparked the corruption watchdog’s investigation into his own party says he would pay the price of whistleblowing again as he announced he will exit politics at the 2027 election. In announcing his resignation, Ray Williams acknowledged the personal toll of exposing allegations of impropriety within his own party. His sole motivation in making the “unpleasant decision” was to ensure the Liberal Party upheld the “highest standards possible”. Liberal backbencher Ray Williams announced he will exit politics at the next election. Wolter Peeters “I want to make it clear that at no time have my actions been motivated by any malice or personal agenda. In fact, I knew that I would be shunned as most whistleblowers are, right or wrong. I happened to be right and more so than I initially understood,” the Kellyville MP wrote. “There is no place for corruption in any organisation including my own. However, the sad reality is that in Australia, as a whistleblower, career opportunities quickly disappear and people choose not to associate themselves with you.”



Related Article Operation Rosny The late-night speech that blew apart the NSW Liberals The veteran MP wrote that regardless of that, he would “do it all again if ever I was faced with the choice of doing the right thing on behalf of my party and my community”. The statement, which circulated among Liberal MPs on Tuesday afternoon and obtained by the Herald, is expected to be formally released on Wednesday morning. In a parliamentary speech in 2022, Williams detailed his concerns about “undemocratic political processes” within the Liberal Party, questioning how popularly elected mayor Michelle Byrne and six sitting Liberal councillors were replaced by the Liberals’ state executive “without the usual preselection processes normally afforded to such positions”. The backbencher alleged Christian Ellis and other senior members of the party “were paid significant funds” to install new councillors on The Hills Shire Council who would support property developer Jean Nassif future development applications.



Then-Liberal premier Dominic Perrottet referred Williams’ claims to the Independent Commission Against Corruption the next morning. The allegations sparked the corruption watchdog’s high-profile Operation Rosny probe which finished public hearings in late September. Presiding commissioner Fabian Gleeson, SC, has 180 days after final submissions to hand down his findings from the blockbuster corruption inquiry. William’s exit leaves Byrne as the early frontrunner to succeed him in his northwestern Sydney electorate, said a Liberal source on the condition of anonymity so they could speak freely. With Australia’s migration settings facing severe political pressure, the former state multiculturalism minister said he dedicated himself to “ensuring everyone who called NSW home and did the right thing, was treated equally and respectfully”.



“Sydney can be proud that we have integrated more people from cultural backgrounds more successfully than any other city in Australia,” he wrote. Williams joins Liberal James Griffin, Alister Henskens and Mark Taylor as the party MPs who will exit politics in March next year. World.title: The new tech shopping for you while you sleep
World.content:
LifestyleFashionMelbourne Fashion Week The new tech shopping for you while you sleep Courtney Thompson October 20, 2026 — 7:00pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

One of the most memorable scenes from the 1995 cult classic film Clueless (a movie full of memorable scenes) occurs early on, inside Cher Horowitz’s bedroom. After waking up, Horowitz, played by Alicia Silverstone, walks over to her closet and consults a computer for what she should wear to school that day. The computer shows her different combinations of her clothes, and informs her when something clashes via an aggressive “MISS-MATCH” warning. When she finds an outfit she wants to wear, it gives her an image of what it would look like on her. In 1995, the scene felt like a far-flung possibility. In 2026, it’s not that far off how AI is shaping the way we interact with fashion and shopping today. Models wearing local designers Perple (left) and Gotham (right), who “reject AI perfectionism”. Justin McManus Like all industries, AI is disrupting fashion. In 2023, Oroton was one of the first local labels to experiment with augmented reality (AR) similar to Cher’s computer in Clueless, unveiling AR windows at the Queen Victoria Building in Sydney and Queen Street Mall in Brisbane where customers could virtually try on their bags in the windows.



Since then, AI has become deeply embedded in every stage of how people shop online, improving fit recommendations, virtual try-on, trend forecasting and stock management. Related Article Fashion Week The style lesson to borrow from Nicole Kidman’s Paris Fashion Week look According to a new report by Stripe and Thoughtworks, 81 per cent of shoppers in Australia and New Zealand have already used AI to help them shop online. “Most use it for advice rather than buying and the businesses we talk to are asking, not whether this is coming, but how quickly they need to build the trust, capability and infrastructure to keep up,” says Kathryn Heffernan, Thoughtworks managing director for retail and travel, APAC. One of the most recent developments has been agentic commerce, with spending on the technology projected to grow from $5 billion to $47 billion by 2030.



Traditionally, when you shop online you do all the work: search, scroll, filter, compare and then buy. Agentic commerce outsources the bulk of that labour to an AI assistant. You tell the assistant what you’re looking for – “a cotton midi dress for a summer wedding that is under $300 and will arrive by the end of the week” – then it goes out, finds sites with options in your size, and compares them for you. If you allow it, the assistant can also make the purchase. In 1995, Cher Horowitz used a computer program to help pick out fashionable outfits. Today, 81 per cent of shoppers do too. CBS via Getty Images Heffernan says it’s a welcome advancement for time-poor people who want to cut back on the admin of online shopping.



“Comparing options is tedious: opening tabs, checking fabrics, decoding size charts. An AI assistant can read product descriptions, reviews and size guides in seconds and pull them into one side-by-side summary,” she explains. “Done well, it can also help people buy less but better. When it’s easy to compare fabrics, care instructions and reviews, you can make a more considered choice rather than an impulse one. That depends on the tool being built to serve the shopper rather than to push more sales, which is why trust matters so much.” In this process, however, the joy of discovery is lost. Ask any fashion editor, and they’ll tell you about the meditative state they enter when they start trawling online websites for the specific cut of black pants they’ve spent months searching for. Likewise, designers are still figuring out how they can meaningfully integrate AI into their business without affecting their creative output.



Editor's pick Trends Is it a belt? Is it a corset? No, it’s a cummerbund “AI has helped me code my website and add plugins that track sales and improve the site layout,” says Gautam Kapoor, founder and designer of Melbourne-based label Gotham. While the technology is helpful, Kapoor isn’t worried about it impeding their creativity. “AI usually creates from what has already come before. Designing involves going back and forth with an idea many times, and that push and pull is what creates something original and unique,” Kapoor says. “In fashion, this happens in the toiling process, when prototyping a garment, and I don’t believe AI could replicate that.” On Wednesday evening, Gotham will be one of nine designers showing designs as part of the Cult Status runway at Melbourne Fashion Week.



Chris Ran Lin, Club Venus, Hunter Gatherer x BSL, Liandra, Perple, R.Sport, Toilè Studios, Wah-Wah Australia and Wilson Jedd Adams are all inspired by subcultures that sprout from the underground, their work challenging the hyper-perfection of AI in favour of experimentation and individuality. “AI has made me value the importance of the creative journey at a deeper level and appreciate the unique perspective designers across all mediums bring to their art form,” says Huiliana Chandra-Curry, designer of slow fashion label, Perple. “Without a doubt, the importance of well-made, intentional garments will continue to command respect and attention. In an era where AI models will homogenise aesthetics, there is an opportunity for originators to find their people.” See more from Melbourne Fashion Week: A look from sustainable fashion brand Amy Cottrell on the runway at Melbourne Fashion Week 2026. World.content:
NationalWACourts What tobacco crime kings pay enforcers to blow up rival Perth stores Rebecca Peppiatt October 20, 2026 — 6:58pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. The paltry amount crime bosses will pay someone to do their dirty work has been revealed in court as a man who helped ram raid and set fire to a Midland tobacco shop was sentenced. Darryl John Campton, 23, was a drug addict and a career criminal somehow recruited by an organised crime gang in November 2025 to target a store that refused to sell their illegal vapes and smokes. Loading Now he’s heading to jail for his involvement and he didn’t even get paid. Campton was sentenced on Tuesday in the Perth District Court to 4½ years over a spate of offending in September and November 2025, that included the raid on the Great Eastern Highway shop that caused almost $20,000 worth of damage.



The incident was caught on CCTV with Campton seen in the footage with two other men using a stolen car and a street sign to “battery ram” the metal shutters on the front of the shop. They’re later seen peeling apart the metal so they can get inside, pour some fuel from a jerry can and set the shop on fire before fleeing the scene. Campton was paid $5,000 for being the getaway driver. One of his co-offenders carried out the task in return for having his drug debt wiped. Judge Belinda Lonsdale said Campton was “susceptible to pressure from peers” as a result of “a dysfunctional childhood” that included abuse, leading to drug use and anti-social behaviour.



During the hearing, the 23-year-old was also sentenced over a terrifying nighttime burglary in which he woke the occupant of an Iluka property by standing in his bedroom doorway with a hatchet in his hand and a bandana covering his face. He told him to be quiet before stealing keys to a BMW which he later dumped in nearby bushland. He was arrested and confessed to the crime, but two months later was at it again, this time breaking into the home of a Craigie acquaintance. It was his car that was used an hour or so later in the Midland ram raid. The court was told Campton’s history of offending and drug use stretched back into his childhood, including a suggestion he was suffering from fetal alcohol spectrum disorder. “The impetus for this offending is to feed his long-standing and insatiable drug habit,” the court was told. Judge Lonsdale sentenced him to a total of 4½ years in prison – two years for his involvement in the attack on the Midland store which is the same sentence as one of his co-offenders.

World.title: Security briefing for anxious MPs as Helen Haines loses leg, remains in critical condition
World.content:
PoliticsFederalHaines attack Security briefing for anxious MPs as Helen Haines loses leg, remains in critical condition Natassia Chrysanthos Updated October 20, 2026 — 6:50pm ,first published 12:07pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.
